# Behaviors tested by Ariakit and Headless UI

Mined from both repositories' test suites for a headless UI conformance suite. Every bullet is one asserted behavior with the file and test name it came from.

## Sources

### ariakit/ariakit

- Repo: https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit
- Commit: `61bf980998ee83c067b5172cbe0c1891680bd95e`
- Commit date: 2026-09-13
- Shallow clone (`--depth 1`), so only the tip revision was available.
- Layout note: at this revision the example tests no longer live under `examples/**/test.ts`. `examples/` holds source only. The tests moved to `app/src/sandbox/<name>/test*.ts` (474 files) and `app/src/examples/<name>/test*.ts` (4 files). The old `packages/ariakit-core` and `packages/ariakit-react` unit tests are now `packages/ariakit-components/src/<component>/<component>-store.test.ts` (the framework-agnostic store layer), `packages/ariakit-utils/src/*.test.ts`, `packages/ariakit-react-components/src/**/*.test.ts`, and `packages/ariakit-store/src/test.ts`.
- Test-file naming encodes the environment, and the suffix is load-bearing for every bullet below:
  - `test.ts` runs in Vitest against happy-dom, once per framework project (`react` and `solid`), using `@ariakit/test`.
  - `test-browser.ts` runs in Playwright against all three engines (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit).
  - `test-chrome.ts`, `test-safari.ts`, `test-chrome-firefox.ts`, `test-chrome-safari.ts` restrict the Playwright run to those engines, which is itself the record of a browser-specific behavior or a browser-specific bug.
  - `test-mobile.ts` and `test-ios.ts` run at a mobile viewport / on iOS Safari.
  - `test-chrome-js-disabled.ts` runs with JavaScript disabled, pinning progressive-enhancement behavior.
  - `test-public-browser.ts` runs against the deployed public site.
- Files read: `packages/ariakit-test/src/**` (implementation and all 19 test files), `packages/ariakit-components/src/*/[a-z]*-store.test.ts` (10 files), `packages/ariakit-utils/src/*.test.ts`, `packages/ariakit-store/src/test.ts`, `packages/ariakit-react-components/src/**/*.test.ts`, and every `app/src/sandbox/**` / `app/src/examples/**` test file. The complete list is under Files read below.

### tailwindlabs/headlessui

- Repo: https://github.com/tailwindlabs/headlessui
- Commit: `eea57cf46fd6767ed1059012f7073b88eb159fba`
- Commit date: 2026-04-13
- Shallow clone (`--depth 1`).
- Files read: every `packages/@headlessui-react/src/**/*.test.tsx?` and `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/**/*.test.ts?` (55 files, ~59.5k lines), plus both `src/test-utils/` directories and `packages/@headlessui-tailwindcss/src/index.test.ts`.
- React and Vue suites are near-mirrors. Where both assert the same behavior the bullet carries both paths. Where only one does, the bullet is tagged `[react only]` or `[vue only]`.

### Files not read, and why

- `app/src/tests/previews-browser.ts`, `app/src/tests/samples-browser.ts`, `app/src/tests/reference-partials-browser.ts`: site-wide visual sweeps that iterate every preview URL and take screenshots. They assert no component behavior and are gated behind `VISUAL_TEST`.
- `packages/ariakit-scripts/src/*.test.ts` (build, ci, ci-visual, dev, docs, legacy-clean, perf, perf-compare, react18, utils): build-tooling tests for the repo's own CLI, not component behavior.
- `website/build-pages/*.test.ts`, `app/src/lib/*.test.ts`, `.changeset/get-changelog-entry.test.ts`: documentation-site and repo-tooling tests (markdown parsing, routing, OG images, pricing keys, changelog formatting).
- `packages/ariakit-test/src/__use-all-events.test.helper.ts`: a helper imported by other test files rather than a suite of its own; its behavior is covered through the files that import it.
- Ariakit's Solid-specific component sources were not read. The sandbox `test.ts` files are shared between the React and Solid projects, so every bullet tagged to a sandbox `test.ts` covers both frameworks, but Solid-only differences in the implementations are outside what the tests expose.

### Slug notes

- Slugs added beyond the requested list, because nothing in it fit: `accessibility-assertions` (already requested), `controlled-state` (already requested, used here for both the store primitive and the component stores), `utils` (Ariakit's `@ariakit/utils`, `@ariakit/react-utils` and component-level utility tests), `render-props` (Headless UI's shared `render` utility, its public export surface and its Tailwind plugin), `role` (Ariakit's `Role` component and its prop-merging behavior), `collection` (Ariakit's collection store and virtualized renderer), `tag` (Ariakit's tag-input component), `list`, `nav`, `progress`, `table` and `styling` (all from the `@ariakit/ui` styled kit and the `@ariakit/tailwind` plugin).
- Requested slugs with no section, because neither library has such a component at these revisions: `toast`, `accordion`, `collapsible`. Ariakit's closest equivalents are covered under `disclosure` (`DisclosureContent` with its `animated` timeouts, which is what a collapsible would use) and under `dialog` (the notifications sandbox, which is the closest thing to a toast region). `context-menu` and `menubar` exist as their own sections; `hover-card` covers Ariakit's `Hovercard`.
- Where a slug holds bullets from both libraries (`dialog`, `menu`, `popover`, `tooltip`, `combobox`, `listbox`, `select`, `tabs`, `disclosure`, `portal`, `focus-trap`, `checkbox`, `radio-group`, `switch`, `button`, `form`, `composite`, `testing-utilities`), the source tag on each bullet is the only thing that says which library it came from.

## testing-utilities

Ariakit's `@ariakit/test` package. Exported from `packages/ariakit-test/src/index.ts`, which also imports `./shims.ts` for its side effects, so importing the package installs the browser shims. Three entry points: `.` (DOM simulation), `./react` (adds `render`), `./playwright` (role queries over a Playwright `Page`).

### Roles and attributes

- `query` (aliased `q`) builds one query method per ARIA role from a hardcoded list of 82 roles: alert, alertdialog, application, article, banner, blockquote, button, caption, cell, checkbox, code, columnheader, combobox, complementary, contentinfo, definition, deletion, dialog, directory, document, emphasis, feed, figure, form, generic, grid, gridcell, group, heading, img, insertion, link, list, listbox, listitem, log, main, marquee, math, menu, menubar, menuitem, menuitemcheckbox, menuitemradio, meter, navigation, none, note, option, paragraph, presentation, progressbar, radio, radiogroup, region, row, rowgroup, rowheader, scrollbar, search, searchbox, separator, slider, spinbutton, status, strong, subscript, superscript, switch, tab, table, tablist, tabpanel, term, textbox, time, timer, toolbar, tooltip, tree, treegrid, treeitem. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/__aria-role.ts`)
- Each role query accepts an accessible name as a string (matched exactly) or a `RegExp`, and every query exposes `.lazy` (returns a thunk that reruns the query), `.all` (array, possibly empty), `.wait` (findBy, resolves when the element appears), `.maybe` (queryBy, returns `null`), and `.hidden` (include elements excluded by accessibility). `.all.wait`, `.wait.all`, `.wait.hidden`, `.all.hidden` and `.maybe.hidden` compose. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/query.ts`)
- Name matching falls back when Testing Library's computed accessible name does not match: an element with `aria-label` is rejected outright, an element with `aria-labelledby` is matched against the referenced element's `textContent`, and everything else is matched against its `placeholder` if it has one, otherwise its `textContent`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/query.ts`)
- Unless `hidden: true` is passed, any element inside an `[inert]` ancestor is filtered out of role queries. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/query.ts`)
- `query.text` / `q.text` and `query.labeled` / `q.labeled` wrap getByText and getByLabelText with the same `.all` / `.wait` / `.maybe` / `.lazy` variants, and `query.within(element)` rescopes the whole query object to a subtree. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/query.ts`)
- The Playwright entry point exports `query(pageOrLocatorOrFrameLocator)` returning the same role names plus `text`, each delegating to `getByRole` / `getByText` with `exact: true` by default, and re-exports all of `@playwright/test`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/playwright.ts`)
- Given `q.<role>.lazy(name)`, when the returned thunk is called, then the query runs at call time rather than at creation time, and the same holds for each `.all` / `.wait` / `.maybe` variant and for `q.within(el)`-scoped queries. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/query.test.ts`: "lazy role queries run when called", "lazy role query variants run the matching variant", "lazy role queries can be scoped with within")
- Given `q.text.lazy(...)` and `q.labeled.lazy(...)`, when the thunk is called, then the text or label query runs then, and each variant runs its matching Testing Library query. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/query.test.ts`: "lazy text and label queries run when called", "lazy text and label query variants run the matching variant")
- Given no matching element, when a non-`.maybe` query runs, then it throws rather than returning null. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/query.test.ts`: "queries ensure matches by default")

- `commonRenderingScenarios(Control, { getElement })` generates a `describe('Rendering')` block with exactly three tests: "should render a control", "should have an `id` attached", "should be possible to override the `id`". [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/scenarios.tsx)
- `commonControlScenarios(Control)` generates the describe chain "Rendering composition" > "Inside `Field`" with six tests: "should mark the control as disabled, if the `Field` is disabled", "should link a control and a `Label` when inside a `Field`", "should link a control and multiple `Label` components when inside a `Field`", "should link a control and a `Description` when inside a `Field`", "should link a control and multiple `Description` components when inside a `Field`", "should link a control with a `Label` and a `Description` when inside a `Field`". [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/scenarios.tsx)
- Given a control inside a disabled `Field`, when nothing else happens, then the control is disabledish, meaning either `disabled` or `aria-disabled` is set. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/scenarios.tsx: "should mark the control as disabled, if the `Field` is disabled")
- Given a control and one or more `Label` components inside a `Field`, when rendered, then the control's `aria-labelledby` id set contains every label's id. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/scenarios.tsx: "should link a control and a `Label` when inside a `Field`", "should link a control and multiple `Label` components when inside a `Field`")
- Given a control and one, three, or a mix of `Description` components inside a `Field`, when rendered, then the control's `aria-describedby` id set contains every description's id. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/scenarios.tsx: "should link a control and a `Description` when inside a `Field`", "should link a control and multiple `Description` components when inside a `Field`", "should link a control with a `Label` and a `Description` when inside a `Field`")

### Keyboard

- `press(key, element?, options?)` fires `keydown`, applies the key's default action, settles, retargets to the new `activeElement` if the keydown moved focus, then fires `keyup` and applies its default action. It focuses the target first (blurring to the body when the target is `<body>`), and returns without doing anything when the target is neither focusable nor the body. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.ts`)
- `press` routes text-editing keys on a text field through `type()` instead: a single-character key types that character, `Delete` types `"\x7f"`, `Backspace` types `"\b"`, and `Enter` on a `<textarea>` types `"\n"`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.ts`)
- Named shortcuts on `press`: `Escape`, `Backspace`, `Delete`, `Tab`, `ShiftTab` (Tab with `shiftKey: true`), `Enter`, `Space` (key `" "`), `ArrowUp`, `ArrowRight`, `ArrowDown`, `ArrowLeft`, `End`, `Home`, `PageUp`, `PageDown`. Each takes `(element?, options?)`. The same 15 shortcuts exist on `press.down` and `press.up`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.ts`)
- Keydown default actions: `Tab` moves focus to `getNextTabbable()` or, with `shiftKey`, `getPreviousTabbable()`. `Enter` clicks a `<button>` or an input of type button/color/file/image/reset/submit, and otherwise attempts implicit form submission for any other input type except hidden. `Home`/`End` move or extend the caret in a text field. `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` move or extend the caret by one character, collapsing an existing selection when Shift is not held. `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` jump the caret to the start/end of a text field, or increment/decrement a number input by 1 while respecting `min` and `max` and firing `input` then `change`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.ts`)
- Keyup default action: `Space` clicks a `<button>` or an input of type button/color/file/image/reset/submit/checkbox/radio. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.ts`)
- Every default action is skipped when the keydown (or keyup) event's default was prevented, and also skipped whenever `metaKey` is held. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.ts`)
- The synthetic Enter/Space activation click reports an unset pointer (`pointerId: -1`, `pointerType: ""`), which is what Chromium, Firefox and WebKit all report for a keyboard-caused click. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.ts`)
- Enter and Space never activate a disabled control, where "disabled" means the `disabled` IDL attribute, matching `:disabled`, or being inside a disabled `<fieldset>` outside its first `<legend>`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.ts`)
- Implicit submission via Enter in a text input finds the form's first submit-capable `button`/`input` searched from the form's root node and filtered by `element.form === form`, clicks it, and bails out if it is disabled. With no submit button, it dispatches `submit` on the form only when the form has exactly one text input. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.ts`)
- The submission click is built and dispatched synchronously (not through `dispatch.click`) so it lands before `requestSubmit`, and a capture-phase `invalid` listener aborts the submission when native validation fails. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.ts`)
- `press.down(key, element?, options?)` fires only `keydown` plus its default action, focusing the element first. Unlike the combined `press`, it does not type printable characters into text fields. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.ts`)
- `press.up(key, element?, options?)` fires only `keyup` plus its default action on the passed element or the current `activeElement`, and deliberately has no focusability guard so a keyup can land on an element that disabled itself during the matching keydown but is still `document.activeElement`. Because it runs independently it cannot suppress its default based on the earlier keydown having been prevented. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.ts`)
- `type(text, element?, options?)` focuses the element, then per character fires `keydown`, re-reads `activeElement` in case the keydown moved focus, and for a text field computes the next value and caret position, fires `keypress` (with a `charCode`, 13 for `"\n"`) for a plain insertion or `compositionupdate` when `isComposing` is set, then fires `input` with the new value, `selectionStart`/`selectionEnd`, and an `inputType` of `insertText`, `insertCompositionText`, `deleteContentForward` (Delete) or `deleteContentBackward` (Backspace). Then it settles and fires `keyup`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/type.ts`)
- `type` maps `"\b"` to Backspace, `"\x7f"` to Delete, `"\n"` to Enter and `"\t"` to Tab. Backspace with a collapsed caret removes the preceding character; with a selection it removes the selection. Delete with a collapsed caret removes the following character. A composing insertion replaces the previous composition character. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/type.ts`)
- `type` skips the value change and the `input` event entirely when the element is `readOnly` or when `keydown`'s default was prevented, and marks the element `dirty` only when the value actually changed. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/type.ts`)
- `type` temporarily switches an `input[type=email]` to `type=text` for the duration of the call, because email inputs are not text fields and do not accept the synthesized input events, and restores the type afterwards. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/type.ts`)
- Given a control that is disabled by the time the key is released, when `press.up.Space()` runs, then no activation click fires. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.test.ts`: "press.up does not activate a disabled control on Space release")
- Given a control that disables itself in its own keydown handler, when `press.down.Enter()` runs, then no activation click fires. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.test.ts`: "press.down does not activate a control that disables itself on Enter")
- Given a form whose default submit button is disabled, disabled by an ancestor `fieldset`, or is a disabled `input[type=image]`, when Enter is pressed in a text input, then the form is not submitted. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.test.ts`: "press.Enter does not submit a form with a disabled default button", "press.Enter does not submit a form with a fieldset-disabled default button", "press.Enter does not submit a form with a disabled image submitter")
- Given a form with a submit button, when Enter is pressed in a text input, then the default button is clicked to perform implicit submission, and this works even when the button has `pointer-events: none`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.test.ts`: "press.Enter activates the default button for implicit submission", "press.Enter activates a default button with pointer-events none")
- Given a listener that prevents the default button's (or image submitter's) click, when Enter triggers implicit submission, then the form is not submitted. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.test.ts`: "press.Enter respects default button click preventDefault", "press.Enter respects image submitter click preventDefault")
- Given implicit submission, when the default button's click is dispatched, then the event is `composed: true`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.test.ts`: "press.Enter dispatches a composed default button click")
- Given a form with an `input[type=image]` submitter, when Enter is pressed, then the submitter is activated once and not resubmitted after validation runs. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.test.ts`: "press.Enter activates an image submitter for implicit submission", "press.Enter does not resubmit an image submitter after validation")
- Given an image submitter, when Enter triggers submission, then the submit happens before microtasks queued from the click run. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.test.ts`: "press.Enter submits an image submitter before queued click microtasks")
- Given a form with exactly one text input and no submit button, when Enter is pressed, then `submit` is dispatched on the form directly. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.test.ts`: "press.Enter submits a single-input form without a submit button")
- Given a forward text selection, when Shift+Home is pressed, then the selection anchor is kept and the selection extends backwards to offset 0; the mirror holds for Shift+End on a backward selection. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.test.ts`: "press.Home with shiftKey keeps the anchor of a forward selection", "press.End with shiftKey keeps the anchor of a backward selection")
- Given a `<textarea>`, when Enter is pressed, then the `keypress` reports `charCode` 13. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.test.ts`: "press.Enter on a textarea emits an Enter keypress charCode")
- Given a keyboard activation, when the synthetic click fires, then it reports no pointer behind it (`pointerId: -1`, `pointerType: ""`), both for a plain button activation and for an implicit-submission default-button click. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.test.ts`: "press activates a button with no pointer behind the click", "press.Enter submits with no pointer behind the default button click")
- Given modifier keys held during Enter, when the default button's click fires, then it reports the same modifier state. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.test.ts`: "press.Enter keeps modifier state on the default button click")
- Given jsdom rather than happy-dom, when Enter triggers implicit submission, then the default button is still activated and the click reports the same pointer members every other click reports. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.jsdom.test.ts`: "press.Enter activates a default button in jsdom", "press.Enter submits with the same pointer members every click reports")
- Given an image submitter whose validation is handled or stopped by an external listener, when Enter is pressed in jsdom, then the form is not resubmitted. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.jsdom.test.ts`: "press.Enter does not resubmit an image submitter after external validation", "press.Enter does not resubmit an image submitter after stopped validation")
- Given a `readOnly` text field, a prevented `keydown`, or a non-text field, when `type` runs, then no `change` event is dispatched on blur. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/type.test.ts`: "type does not dispatch change after typing into a readonly field", "type does not dispatch change after a prevented keydown", "type does not dispatch change after typing on a non-text field")
- Given an empty text field, when Backspace or Delete is pressed so the value does not change, then no `change` event is dispatched on blur. - `Keys` is a record of partial keyboard event inits: `Space` is `{ key: ' ', keyCode: 32, charCode: 32 }`, `Enter` is `{ key: 'Enter', keyCode: 13, charCode: 13 }`, `Escape` is `{ key: 'Escape', keyCode: 27, charCode: 27 }`, `Tab` is `{ key: 'Tab', keyCode: 9, charCode: 9 }`. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `Keys` defines `Backspace` as `{ key: 'Backspace', keyCode: 8 }` with no `charCode`. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `Keys` defines the arrows with `keyCode` only and no `charCode`: `ArrowLeft` 37, `ArrowUp` 38, `ArrowRight` 39, `ArrowDown` 40. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `Keys` defines `Home` as keyCode 36, `End` as 35, `PageUp` as 33 and `PageDown` as 34, all without `charCode`. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `Keys` carries no modifier flags of its own; `shift(event)` returns a copy of the event init with `shiftKey: true`, and there is no ctrl, meta or alt helper, so those modifiers have to be spread in by hand. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `word(input)` maps each character of the string to a `{ key }` event init and, before returning, fires a single `change` event on the currently focused element with the whole string as the target value, so a typed word arrives as one value change plus per-character key events. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `word` fires that `change` for a focused `input` or `textarea` in React but only for a focused `input` in Vue. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `type(events, element = document.activeElement)` switches to fake timers, replays every event init against the element, then runs all pending timers and waits a frame, and always restores real timers in a finally block. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `type` adds a `charCode` equal to the single character's code point for any key whose `key` string is one character long, unless the event init already supplies `charCode`, and also passes a `type` field naming the current step. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `type` for any key with no special entry fires, in order, `keydown`, `keypress`, `input`, `keyup`; the `input` event is fired unconditionally rather than only when the value changes, which the source flags as a known shortcut. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `type` for `Enter` fires `keydown`, `keypress`, `click`, `keyup`, and the `click` is skipped entirely unless the target is an `HTMLButtonElement`. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `type` for `Space` fires `keydown`, `keypress`, `keyup`, then `click` last, again only on an `HTMLButtonElement`, which is the real browser ordering difference from Enter. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `type` for `Escape` fires `keydown`, `keypress`, `keyup` and no `input`. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `type` for `Backspace` on an `HTMLInputElement` fires `keydown` then `input`, both with a target value equal to the current value minus its last character; on anything else it fires only `keydown`, and either way it then fires `keyup`. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `type` for `Tab` fires `keydown`, then moves focus, then fires `keyup` on the newly focused element, because the focus step returns the new element and `type` rebinds its target to it. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `type` honours `preventDefault` through a per-key cancellation table: by default a cancelled `keydown` suppresses the following `keypress`, and a cancelled `keypress` or `keyup` suppresses nothing. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `type` for `Enter` suppresses both `keypress` and `click` when `keydown` is cancelled, and suppresses `click` when `keypress` is cancelled. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `type` for `Space` suppresses `keypress` and `click` when `keydown` is cancelled, suppresses nothing when `keypress` is cancelled, and suppresses `click` when `keyup` is cancelled. ### Pointer

- `click(element, options?, tap = false)` simulates a full primary-button click as this ordered sequence: `hover(element)` with `button: 0, buttons: 0`, then `mouseDown` (pointerdown, mousedown, focus), then a re-check that the element is still visible (walking up to the first visible ancestor if the hover or press hid it), then `contextmenu` if `button === 2`, then a settle, then `mouseUp` (pointerup, mouseup), then the terminal activation event. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/click.ts`)
- On a non-primary button `click` fires `auxclick` instead of `click`, runs no activation behavior, and therefore never forwards to a label's control or an `option`; the comment records that Chromium and WebKit still fire `auxclick` on disabled controls while Firefox does not, so it is not suppressed. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/click.ts`)
- On a disabled element `click` fires hover, pointerdown, pointerup (but not mousedown/mouseup) and then returns without the terminal `click`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/click.ts`, `packages/ariakit-test/src/mouse-down.ts`, `packages/ariakit-test/src/mouse-up.ts`)
- `click` on a non-focusable element inside a `<label>` dispatches `click` on the label, temporarily disables the label's control so the environment does not auto-click it, then focuses the control and dispatches exactly one `click` on it. Only `click` is forwarded, no mousedown/mouseup, matching how browsers run label activation. If the label's `click` default was prevented, or the control is not focusable, nothing is forwarded. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/click.ts`)
- `click` on an `<option>` inside a `<select>` sets IDL selectedness (not the attribute), then fires `input`, `change`, and `click` on the select. For a `multiple` select, Shift extends the range from the last non-shift-selected option, Ctrl toggles one option, and an unmodified click replaces the selection. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/click.ts`)
- `tap(element, options?)` is `click` without the settle between press and release, reproducing a fast tap. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/tap.ts`)
- `rightClick(element, options?)` is `click` with `button: 2`: hover, pointerdown, mousedown, focus, `contextmenu` while the button is still held, pointerup, mouseup, `auxclick`. No `click` event is fired. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/right-click.ts`)
- `mouseDown(element, options?)` fires `pointerdown` then `mousedown` (with `detail: 1`), then moves focus: it focuses the element when it is focusable and its computed `pointer-events` is not `none`, otherwise the closest focusable ancestor, otherwise blurs the active element. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/mouse-down.ts`)
- `mouseDown` clears a non-collapsed document selection before focusing, unless the press lands on a control that preserves selection: a `button`, a `select`, an `a[href]`, or an `input` whose type is not one of date, datetime-local, email, month, number, password, search, tel, text, time, url, week. A textbox always clears. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/mouse-down.ts`)
- If `pointerdown`'s default is prevented, `mouseDown` suppresses the compatibility `mousedown`, and the suppression is recorded per-document so the matching `mouseUp` also suppresses `mouseup`. Suppression is cleared on the release that ends the gesture. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/mouse-down.ts`, `packages/ariakit-test/src/mouse-up.ts`)
- If `mousedown`'s default is prevented, `mouseDown` skips both the selection clearing and the focus move. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/mouse-down.ts`)
- `mouseUp(element, options?)` fires `pointerup` then `mouseup` with `detail: 1` and `buttons: 0`. A disabled element gets the pointer event but not `mouseup`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/mouse-up.ts`)
- Chorded button gestures follow Pointer Events: when the caller passes a `buttons` mask showing another button already held, `mouseDown` fires `pointermove` instead of `pointerdown` and `mouseUp` fires `pointermove` instead of `pointerup`, while the compatibility `mousedown`/`mouseup` still fire for each button. `isChordedPress` masks out the pressed button's own bit before testing; `isChordedRelease` tests the remaining mask directly. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/__mouse.ts`, `packages/ariakit-test/src/mouse-down.ts`, `packages/ariakit-test/src/mouse-up.ts`)
- The `buttons` bitmask is built from a table that is deliberately not the same ordering as `button`: primary 0 maps to 1, auxiliary 1 maps to 4, secondary 2 maps to 2, 3 maps to 8, 4 maps to 16, 5 maps to 32. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/__mouse.ts`)
- Pointer events report `pressure: 0.5` while a button is held and `0` otherwise, the values Pointer Events defines for a device with no pressure sensor, and `isPrimary: true`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/__mouse.ts`)
- Multi-step helpers (`click`, `select`) strip a caller-supplied `buttons` with `omitButtons` so each phase derives its own mask; `mouseDown` and `mouseUp` run a single phase, so an explicit `buttons` there wins and describes a chord. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/__mouse.ts`)
- `click`, `auxclick` and `contextmenu` reset every pointer-specific member except `pointerId` and `pointerType`: isPrimary, width, height, pressure, tangentialPressure, tiltX, tiltY, twist, altitudeAngle, azimuthAngle, persistentDeviceId, coalescedEvents, predictedEvents. The reset list is a keyed record so TypeScript rejects a table missing a member. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/__mouse.ts`)
- `hover(element, options?)` fires, on the previously hovered element (tracked as `document.lastHovered`): `pointermove`, `mousemove`, then `pointerout`, `pointerleave` (only when the new element is not a descendant), `mouseout`, `mouseleave` (same condition), each with `relatedTarget` set to the new element or `null` when the new element has `pointer-events: none`. Then it settles, then on the new element fires `pointerover`, `pointerenter`, `mouseover`, `mouseenter` (with `relatedTarget` set to the old element), then `pointermove` and `mousemove`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/hover.ts`)
- `hover` skips every mouse-family event on a disabled element while still firing the pointer-family ones, skips the whole enter sequence when the target has `pointer-events: none`, skips the leave sequence when the previous element has `pointer-events: none`, and returns immediately when the target is not visible. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/hover.ts`)
- `select(text, element = document.body, options?)` hovers, presses, dispatches a cancelable non-composed `selectstart`, walks descendant text nodes to build a `Range` covering the first occurrence of `text`, installs it as the document selection, settles, releases, and dispatches `click`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/select.ts`)
- `dispatch(element, event)` re-dispatches any pointer- or mouse-family event on the nearest ancestor whose computed `pointer-events` is not `none`, recursively, matching how browsers route those events. The gated list is mousemove, mouseover, mouseenter, mouseout, mouseleave, auxclick, contextmenu, mousedown, mouseup, pointermove, pointerover, pointerenter, pointerout, pointerleave, pointerdown, pointerup, click. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.ts`)
- Given a button, when `click(button)` runs with the primary button, then exactly this sequence fires with `button buttons detail` values: `pointerdown 0 1 0`, `mousedown 0 1 1`, `focus`, `pointerup 0 0 0`, `mouseup 0 0 1`, `click 0 0 1`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/click.test.ts`: "click with the primary button keeps dispatching click")
- Given a button, when `click(button, { button: 2 })` runs, then the sequence is `pointerdown 2 2 0`, `mousedown 2 2 1`, `focus`, `contextmenu 2 2 0`, `pointerup 2 0 0`, `mouseup 2 0 1`, `auxclick 2 0 1`, identical to `rightClick`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/click.test.ts`: "click with the secondary button matches rightClick")
- Given a button, when `rightClick(button, { shiftKey: true })` runs, then the events are pointerdown, mousedown, focus, contextmenu, pointerup, mouseup, auxclick in that order, no `click` fires, `shiftKey` is true on all of them, and `buttons` is 2 through contextmenu then 0 from pointerup on. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/right-click.test.ts`: "rightClick dispatches a secondary click sequence")
- Given a caller-supplied `buttons` mask, when `click(el, { button: 1, buttons: 1 })` or `rightClick(el, { buttons: 1 })` runs, then the mask is ignored and each phase derives its own: auxiliary gives `pointerdown 1 4`, secondary gives `pointerdown 2 2`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/click.test.ts`: "click and rightClick derive buttons from the button they press")
- Given any `click`, when the pointer first moves onto the element, then pointerover, pointerenter, mouseover, mouseenter, pointermove and mousemove all report `button 0` and `buttons 0` regardless of which button the click will press. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/click.test.ts`: "click moves the pointer onto the element with no button held")
- Given a non-primary button, when `click` runs, then `auxclick` fires instead of `click`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/click.test.ts`: "click with the auxiliary button dispatches auxclick instead of click")
- Given a disabled control, when `click` runs with the auxiliary button, then `auxclick` still fires, matching Chromium and WebKit but not Firefox. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/click.test.ts`: "click with the auxiliary button dispatches auxclick on disabled controls")
- Given a label or an `option`, when `click` runs with the auxiliary button, then no activation behavior runs and nothing is forwarded to the label's control or the select. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/click.test.ts`: "click with the auxiliary button doesn't run activation behavior")
- Given a click gesture with pointer members set, when the terminal `click` fires, then only `pointerId` and `pointerType` carry over and every other pointer member is reset. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/click.test.ts`: "click carries only the pointer identity to the click event")
- Given an auxiliary-button gesture, when `auxclick` fires, then it carries the same pointer identity. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/click.test.ts`: "click with the auxiliary button carries the pointer identity to auxclick")
- Given a click on a label, when the click is forwarded to the label's control, then the forwarded event carries the gesture's pointer identity and the terminal event init from the gesture that activated the label. - Given a multi-select, when an option is shift-clicked, then the `change` listener already sees the updated `selectedOptions`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/click.test.ts`: "shift-click exposes updated selectedOptions on change")
