- `click(element, button = MouseButton.Left)` in React is a thin wrapper that runs `rawClick` inside `act`, so React state updates flush before the assertion; Vue has no `rawClick` and `click` is the implementation itself. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- A left click fires, in order, `pointerdown`, `mousedown`, a focus attempt, `pointerup`, `mouseup`, `click`, each with `{ button: 0 }` as the event init. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- A left click on which `pointerdown` was cancelled skips `mousedown`, the focus attempt and `mouseup`, but still fires `pointerup` and `click`. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- A left click on which `mousedown` was cancelled skips the focus attempt and `mouseup`, but still fires `pointerup` and `click`, mirroring the browser rule that preventing mousedown prevents focus. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- The focus attempt in a left click walks up from the clicked element through its ancestors and calls `focus()` on the first one matching the tabbable selector, which reproduces the browser behaviour of focusing the nearest focusable ancestor rather than the exact target. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- A click on a disabled `HTMLButtonElement` fires nothing at all and returns immediately, so a disabled button never sees pointer, mouse or click events. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- A right click (`MouseButton.Right`) fires `pointerdown`, `mousedown`, `pointerup`, `mouseup` with `{ button: 2 }` and deliberately fires no `click` and no `contextmenu`; the `pointerup`/`mouseup` pair is marked as Firefox-only behaviour. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- A right click on which `pointerdown` was cancelled skips `mousedown` and `mouseup` but still fires `pointerup`. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- There is no exported `contextMenu`, `mouseDown`, `mouseUp`, `mouseOver` or `mouseOut` helper in either framework; `contextmenu` and `dblclick` are never synthesised, and individual down/up events have to be fired through the testing-library `fireEvent` directly. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `mouseEnter(element)` fires `pointerover`, `pointerenter`, `mouseover` in that order and no `mousemove`. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `mouseEnter` in Vue first randomises the fake pointer position and attaches the pointer's `screenX`/`screenY` to all three events; React fires them with no coordinates at all, so React cannot distinguish a real hover from a synthetic one by position. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `mouseMove(element)` advances the fake pointer by one pixel, fires `pointermove` inside the tracking-bypass window, then fires `mousemove` with the pointer's `screenX`/`screenY`, so consecutive moves always report a changed position. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `mouseLeave(element)` advances the fake pointer, fires `pointerout` and `pointerleave` inside the tracking-bypass window, then fires `mouseout` and `mouseleave` with the pointer coordinates. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `mouseDrag(start, end)` fires the full sequence `pointerdown`, `mousedown`, focus attempt, `pointermove`, `mousemove`, `pointerout`, `mouseout` on the starting element, then `pointerover`, `mouseover`, `pointermove`, `mousemove`, `pointerup`, `mouseup`, `click` on the ending element, all with `{ button: 0 }`. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `mouseDrag` skips every `mouse*` event but keeps every `pointer*` event and the final `click` when `pointerdown` or `mousedown` was cancelled, and returns immediately when the starting element is a disabled button. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- Every pointer and keyboard helper ends by awaiting a nested `setImmediate` chain, three deep in React and two deep in Vue, which is how the suites wait for the library's `requestAnimationFrame`-based work without real timers. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- React drives its events through `fireEvent` from `@testing-library/react` while Vue uses `fireEvent` from `@testing-library/dom`, so React events go through the React event system and Vue events are plain DOM dispatches. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `FakePointer` is a 1920x1080 virtual cursor whose `options` getter returns `{ screenX, screenY }` for spreading into an event init. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/fake-pointer.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/fake-pointer.ts)
- `FakePointer.randomize()` jumps to a random integer position inside the 1920x1080 box, and `advance(amount = 1)` moves right by that many pixels, wrapping to the next row at the right edge and back to the top at the bottom edge. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/fake-pointer.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/fake-pointer.ts)
- `FakePointer.bypassingTrackingChecks(cb)` sets the `TEST_BYPASS_TRACKED_POINTER` environment variable to `1` for the duration of the callback and restores the previous value afterwards, because jsdom does not implement pointer positions and the library's pointer tracking would otherwise reject the synthetic events. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/fake-pointer.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/fake-pointer.ts)
- A single module-level `pointer` instance is shared by every test in a file, so pointer position carries across interactions within a file. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/fake-pointer.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/fake-pointer.ts)
- `commonControlScenarios(Control)` also generates the describe chain "Mouse interactions" > "Inside `Field`" with four tests: "should be possible to click a `Label`, and focus the control when in a `Field`", "should not be possible to click a `Label`, if the `Label` has the `passive` prop", "should not be possible to click a `Label` and focus the control, if the control is disabled", "should not be possible to click a `Label` and focus the control, if the `Field` is disabled". [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/scenarios.tsx)
- `commonControlScenarios(Control)` also generates the describe chain "Mouse interactions" > "Inside `Fieldset`" with one test: "should not be possible to click a `Label` and focus the control, if the `Fieldset` is disabled". [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/scenarios.tsx)
- Given a control and a `Label` inside a `Field` with focus on the body, when the label is clicked, then the control becomes the active element. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/scenarios.tsx: "should be possible to click a `Label`, and focus the control when in a `Field`")
- Given a `Label` with the `passive` prop, when the label is clicked, then focus stays on the body. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/scenarios.tsx: "should not be possible to click a `Label`, if the `Label` has the `passive` prop")
- Given a disabled control, a disabled `Field`, or a disabled `Fieldset` wrapping the field, when the label is clicked, then focus stays on the body. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/scenarios.tsx: "should not be possible to click a `Label` and focus the control, if the control is disabled", "should not be possible to click a `Label` and focus the control, if the `Field` is disabled", "should not be possible to click a `Label` and focus the control, if the `Fieldset` is disabled")

### Focus management

- `focus(element)` is a no-op when the element is already focused or is not focusable; otherwise it flushes a pending `change` on the outgoing element (see the dirty-tracking bullet), calls `element.focus()`, and flushes microtasks. It throws on `null`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/focus.ts`)
- `blur(element?)` defaults to `document.activeElement`, returns early for `<body>` or for an element that is not actually focused, flushes a pending `change`, then calls `element.blur()`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/blur.ts`)
- Change-event fidelity: `type` sets a `dirty` flag on an element whose value it changed, and `focus` and `blur` dispatch the deferred `change` event before focus leaves, which is how browsers sequence `change` for text inputs. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/type.ts`, `packages/ariakit-test/src/focus.ts`, `packages/ariakit-test/src/blur.ts`)
- The `focus` shim makes `HTMLElement.prototype.focus` a no-op on a non-focusable element, which jsdom and happy-dom otherwise allow. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/shims.ts`)
- Given a focused element in a React tree, when `blur()` runs, then React's `onBlur` fires and the pending `change` is delivered first. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/blur.react.test.tsx`: "blur")
- Given a React-rendered text container, when `select(text)` runs, then the document selection covers exactly that text. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/select.react.test.tsx`: "select")

- Tab focus is not delegated to the browser or to a real tab order: the helper builds its own tabbable list by querying `document.body` with a selector list of `[contentEditable=true]`, `[tabindex]`, `a[href]`, `area[href]`, `button:not([disabled])`, `iframe`, `input:not([disabled])`, `select:not([disabled])`, `details>summary`, `textarea:not([disabled])`, then focuses the next entry. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- Every selector in that list is suffixed with `:not([tabindex='-1'])`, and in the test environment additionally with `:not([style*='display: none'])`, to work around jsdom letting a hidden element become `document.activeElement`, which real browsers do not allow. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- Tab movement takes the index of the current active element in that list and moves by +1, or by -1 when `shiftKey` is set, wrapping modulo the list length, then calls `focus({ preventScroll: true })` on the result. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- If the focus call does not actually land on the chosen element, the helper recurses with the offset shifted one more step in the same direction, so unfocusable candidates are skipped rather than silently swallowing the Tab. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `focus(element)` calls the native `focus()` on an `HTMLElement` and falls back to firing a synthetic `focus` event for anything else (document, window, non-element node), then waits a frame. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- `blur(element)` calls the native `blur()` on an `HTMLElement` and otherwise fires a synthetic `blur` event, then waits a frame. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- React wraps `focus` and `blur` in `act`, Vue does not, which is the only behavioural difference between the two implementations of those two helpers. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a controlled React input, when `type` runs, then `onChange` fires once per character, in order. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/react.test.tsx`: "type fires a controlled onChange once per character, in order")
- Given a controlled filter input, when typing mid-sequence, then each intermediate render sees the full query typed so far. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/react.test.tsx`: "type reflects the full query in a controlled filter mid-typing")
- Given a React component holding controlled state, when `click` runs, then the state toggles and the DOM reflects it before the helper resolves. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/react.test.tsx`: "click toggles controlled state")

### Forms

- `commonFormScenarios(Control, { performUserInteraction })` generates a `describe('Form compatibility')` block with four tests: "should render native (hidden) form elements for the control", "should submit the form with all the data", "should not submit the data if the control is disabled", "should reset the control when the form is reset" (the last one wrapped in `suppressConsoleLogs`). [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/scenarios.tsx)
- Four suites reuse these generators: `input.test.tsx`, `select.test.tsx`, `textarea.test.tsx` and `checkbox.test.tsx`, and the checkbox suite passes a `defaultChecked` wrapper into `commonFormScenarios` so the control has a value to reset. [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/scenarios.tsx)
- Given a control with `name="foo"` inside a form, when rendered, then an element with `[name=foo]` exists in the document. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/scenarios.tsx: "should render native (hidden) form elements for the control")
- Given a control with `name="foo"` and a submit button inside a form, when the button is clicked, then the submitted `FormData` has a `foo` entry. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/scenarios.tsx: "should submit the form with all the data")
- Given a disabled control named `bar` alongside a hidden input named `foo` inside a form, when the form is submitted, then the `FormData` entries are only the `foo` pair, so a disabled control contributes nothing. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/scenarios.tsx: "should not submit the data if the control is disabled")
- Given a control inside a `Field` in a form with submit and reset buttons, when the form is submitted, the control is changed, submitted again, reset, and submitted a third time, then the second submission differs from the first and the third matches the first exactly. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/scenarios.tsx: "should reset the control when the form is reset")

### Animation and presence

- `sleep(ms?)` awaits a frame, a `setTimeout` of `ms`, drains the host scheduler outside a real browser, then awaits another frame. The default delay is 150ms in a real browser and 4ms otherwise, and the comment records that a few milliseconds remain load-bearing for interactions such as hiding a dialog by clicking outside. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/sleep.ts`)
- `settle()` is the cheap intra-interaction wait: two animation frames with a microtask flush between them, and no wall-clock delay, on the theory that components schedule per-step work through `queueMicrotask` and `requestAnimationFrame`. Every helper settles between its sub-steps and calls the real `sleep()` once at the end. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/__utils.ts`)
- `flushScheduler(maxTurns = 10)` installs a `MutationObserver` over the whole document and yields host macrotasks (`setImmediate`, else `MessageChannel`, else `setTimeout`) until two consecutive mutation-free turns, because React 18 can split one commit across scheduler tasks under CI load. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/__utils.ts`)
- `waitFor(callback, options?)` re-exports Testing Library's `waitFor` wrapped in the package's async batching, for retrying an assertion until it stops throwing. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/wait-for.ts`)

- `reportChanges(key, onChange)` polls the `key` function once per `requestAnimationFrame`, calls `onChange` whenever the value differs from the previous frame, and returns a dispose function that cancels the loop; the two frameworks share the file byte for byte. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/report-dom-node-changes.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/report-dom-node-changes.ts)
- `executeTimeline(element, steps)` renders the element, then watches `document.body.innerHTML` frame by frame through `reportChanges` and pushes a full DOM snapshot plus a nanosecond `process.hrtime.bigint()` timestamp on every observed change, which is what makes transition classes observable per frame. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts)
- Each step in `executeTimeline` returns a list of durations, one per expected stage, where `null` means "this stage happens in the next frame" and a number means "this stage takes at least this many milliseconds". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts)
- After each step `executeTimeline` waits one frame, then waits the summed duration of the step's numeric stages, then waits one more frame, purely so the test itself outlives the transition; the recording is independent of this waiting. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts)
- `executeTimeline` throws "We could not record any changes" when no DOM change was observed at all, so a transition that never runs fails loudly instead of producing an empty snapshot. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts)
- `executeTimeline` drops snapshots identical to their predecessor, then annotates each remaining one with the milliseconds elapsed since the previous snapshot, derived from the nanosecond timestamps. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts)
- The React version additionally discards outlier snapshots whose gap to the previous snapshot is smaller than the previous gap; Vue keeps every unique snapshot. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts)
- The returned snapshot string is one block per render, labelled `Render <n>:`, followed by a `snapshot-diff` of that render against the previous one with `contextLines: 0`, so only changed lines appear. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts)
- Each render block whose expected duration is a number gets the suffix `Transition took at least <n>ms (yes)` or `(no, it took <actual>ms)`, where "yes" means the measured gap is within one frame of the expected duration. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts)
- The frame tolerance used for that yes/no verdict is measured live: a `requestAnimationFrame` loop keeps a running frames-per-second estimate and that number is used as the millisecond buffer on both sides, and the loop is cancelled in an `afterAll` hook. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts)
- The diff output is scrubbed before comparison: the `snapshot-diff` header, the `__REMOVE_ME__` annotation lines and top-level `@@` hunk markers are stripped, intermediate `@@` markers become `---`, and every line is re-indented to a common minimum, so the committed snapshots do not churn on cosmetic diff changes. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts)
- `executeTimeline.fullTransition(duration)` is the canonical three-stage timeline: add base and from classes in the next frame, swap from for to classes in the next frame, then remove to and base classes after `duration` milliseconds. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts)
- The React timeline calls each step synchronously while the Vue timeline awaits it, so Vue steps can await `nextTick` before returning their durations. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts)
- `createSnapshot()` returns a recorder with a `use()` hook that clones the rendered element's parent into a snapshot list during layout effect, plus `latest` and `firstChild` getters, which lets a test inspect the DOM as it looked at a specific render rather than at assertion time. [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/snapshot.ts)

### SSR and hydration

- The `./react` entry exports `render(ui, options?)` which wraps Testing Library's `render`, flushes microtasks, awaits a frame, flushes microtasks again, and returns `{ unmount, rerender }` where `rerender` is async and repeats that flush. `options.strictMode` wraps the tree in `StrictMode`; every other Testing Library render option except `queries` is accepted. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/react.tsx`)
- Every helper runs inside `wrapAsync`, which sets `IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT` to `false` for the duration of the outermost call and restores it afterwards, with a depth counter so nested helpers do not restore early. Simulated events therefore run outside `act`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/__utils.ts`)

- `renderSSR(ui, options)` sets the library environment flag to `server`, renders the tree to an HTML string, and mounts that string into a container as raw inner HTML, so the first assertion pass sees exactly the server markup with no client code having run. [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/ssr.tsx)
- The React SSR result carries `type: 'ssr'`, the server HTML string, the testing-library render result, and a `hydrate()` function, and `renderHydrate` is the composition of the two. [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/ssr.tsx)
- React `hydrate()` cleans up, removes the container, creates a fresh container seeded with the server HTML, flips the environment flag to `client`, and re-renders with `hydrate: true`, returning a result of `type: 'hydrate'` whose `contents` is the post-hydration inner HTML, which is what lets a test diff server markup against hydrated markup. [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/ssr.tsx)
- Passing `strict: true` to the React SSR helper wraps the tree in `React.StrictMode`, so double-invoked renders and effects are exercised during hydration. [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/ssr.tsx)
- Vue `renderSSR(component, rootProps)` sets the environment flag to `server`, renders through `createSSRApp` and `renderToString`, and assigns the result into a container's inner HTML; its `hydrate()` mounts a plain `createApp` onto that container and awaits `nextTick`, and notably does not flip the environment flag back to `client`. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/ssr.ts)
- The Vue SSR result exposes only `contents` and `hydrate`, with no render result or `type` discriminator, so Vue SSR tests compare HTML strings rather than querying a render result. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/ssr.ts)

### Notes and edge cases

- `dispatch` is callable directly as `dispatch(element, event)` and also exposes one method per Testing Library event name, plus `auxClick` which Testing Library's map lacks. The `doubleClick` alias is excluded because it has no `createEvent` counterpart, so only `dblClick` is exposed. Each returns a promise resolving to `false` when the default was prevented. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.ts`)
- `click`, `auxclick` and `contextmenu` are constructed as `PointerEvent`, which is what browsers dispatch, falling back to `MouseEvent` in an environment without `PointerEvent` (jsdom before v27), and the pointer members are assigned either way. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.ts`, `packages/ariakit-test/src/__init-event.ts`)
- `initEvent` reassigns event members as configurable getters after construction, so the event reports the values the caller asked for rather than whatever the environment's constructor stored. It runs the clipboard, input, UI, composition, keyboard, mouse, and pointer initializers in that order, gated on interface tests resolved against the target's own realm so an event built for a node inside a same-origin iframe uses that frame's constructors. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/__init-event.ts`)
- Pointer defaults for a device that reports no geometry: `width` and `height` default to 1 and `altitudeAngle` to π/2. Supplying only `tiltX`/`tiltY` derives `altitudeAngle`/`azimuthAngle` and vice versa, using the conversion algorithm from the Pointer Events spec. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/__init-event.ts`)
- Mouse defaults: `pageX`/`pageY` are derived from client coordinates plus the target window's scroll offset, `which` is `button + 1`, `x`/`y` alias `clientX`/`clientY`, and the layout-dependent `offsetX`/`offsetY` keep the environment's values. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/__init-event.ts`)
- `getModifierState` is backed by a `Set` of pressed modifier names rather than an object literal, so an unrecognized name such as `constructor` reports false instead of resolving through `Object.prototype`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/__init-event.ts`)
- `modifierHyper` and `modifierSuper` are deliberately not reported: the comment records that Chromium 151, Firefox 153 and WebKit 26.5 all answer false for them and that jsdom is the outlier in reporting them. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/__init-event.ts`)
- Ariakit runs its DOM tests on happy-dom rather than jsdom because it is roughly twice as fast for this simulation layer, and `shims.ts` normalizes happy-dom's spec divergences. Individual test files can opt into another environment with a `// @vitest-environment <name>` file comment, which is what the `*.jsdom.test.ts` files do. (ariakit: `vitest.config.ts`)
- Shims applied in any non-browser DOM environment: `HTMLElement.prototype.focus` becomes a no-op for non-focusable elements; `Element.prototype.getClientRects` returns `[]` for an element that is disconnected, `hidden`, `display: none`, `visibility: hidden`, or has such an ancestor, and `[{width: 1, height: 1}]` otherwise; `scrollIntoView`, `hasPointerCapture`, `setPointerCapture` and `releasePointerCapture` are stubbed when missing; `ClipboardEvent` is polyfilled when missing. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/shims.ts`)
- happy-dom-only shims: `MouseEvent.prototype.getModifierState` and the `x`/`y` aliases are polyfilled; `KeyboardEvent` is wrapped in a `Proxy` (not subclassed, so `document.createEvent("KeyboardEvent")` still passes `instanceof`) that records the `modifier*` init members in a `WeakMap` because happy-dom drops them, and `getModifierState` is patched to match exact UI Events names, read `AltGraph` from its own member rather than from `altKey`, and throw a `TypeError` when called with no argument; `window.alert` is stubbed; `FormData` is subclassed to blank the names of disabled `select` and `textarea` controls during construction because happy-dom wrongly includes them; `Selection.prototype.removeAllRanges` is patched to defer `selectionchange` to a task instead of dispatching it synchronously; `requestAnimationFrame` is replaced with a batching implementation that runs a frame's callbacks with one shared timestamp and defers callbacks added during the flush to the next frame. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/shims.ts`)
- The keyboard-modifier shim probes the environment's behavior rather than sniffing the environment, so it retires itself once happy-dom conforms. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/shims.ts`)
- happy-dom drops scripted clicks on disabled buttons and inputs, contrary to spec, jsdom and browsers. `dispatch` bypasses that by calling `EventTarget.prototype.dispatchEvent` directly, applying checkbox/radio activation before listeners run, reverting only the activation-owned changes when the click is prevented, and firing `input` then `change` only when the value actually committed (always for a checkbox, only for a not-already-selected radio). (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.ts`)
- Radio-group activation snapshots all same-name radios from the root node rather than from `radio.form`, because happy-dom may group form-associated radios by root. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.ts`)
- happy-dom omits `window.event`, which makes React 18 assign native-listener updates default rather than discrete priority, so `withWindowEvent` exposes the event being dispatched on `window.event` for the duration of the dispatch and restores the previous value afterwards so nested events behave like jsdom and browsers. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/__utils.ts`, `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.ts`)
- `isHappyDOM()` is per-window and returns false for a same-origin iframe window created in happy-dom, which is called out as a known limitation for callers that must cover iframe realms. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/__utils.ts`)
- happy-dom caches `select.selectedOptions` and does not invalidate it when only `option.selected` changes, so `click` reaches into the prototype chain for a symbol described `clearCache` and calls it before dispatching events. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/click.ts`)
- happy-dom clicks `input[type=image]` submitters without running submit activation, so `press` falls back to calling `HTMLFormElement.prototype.requestSubmit` for that one case. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/press.ts`)
- Given a form with a control named `document`, when `dispatch.click` builds the event, then the realm is still resolved correctly and a `PointerEvent` is built, because a form exposes its controls as named properties that shadow built-ins. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.test.ts`: "dispatch.click builds a PointerEvent for a form with a control named document")
- Given `getOwnerWindow`, when a form's named control shadows `ownerDocument`, when a document has no default view, when a document answers its default view with another realm's window, or when it answers with an element, then it resolves the owning window in the first case and reports none in the other three. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/__utils.test.ts`: "getOwnerWindow resolves a form whose control answers the owner document", "getOwnerWindow reports no window for a document with no view", "getOwnerWindow reports no window when a document answers its default view with another realm's window", "getOwnerWindow reports no window when a document answers its default view with an element")
- Given nested `wrapAsync` calls, when the inner one finishes, then the act environment is not restored early; only the outermost call restores it. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/__utils.test.ts`: "wrapAsync does not reapply the act environment when nested")
- Given `click`, `auxclick` and `contextmenu`, when dispatched by name, then they are built as `PointerEvent` and accept pointer properties, defaulting to `pointerType: "mouse"`, and a caller-supplied contact size is preserved. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.test.ts`: "dispatch builds the click-family events as PointerEvent", "dispatch.click defaults to a mouse pointer", "dispatch.click keeps the contact attributes the caller passes")
- Given `dispatch`, when its event methods are enumerated, then `dblClick` is present and the unbuildable `doubleClick` alias is not. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.test.ts`: "dispatch exposes only buildable double-click events")
- Given a listener that prevents the default, when `dispatch.auxClick` resolves, then it resolves `false`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.test.ts`: "dispatch.auxClick reports a prevented default")
- Given every mouse-derived event name (wheel, drag, dragend, dragenter, dragleave, dragover, dragstart, drop), when dispatched by name, then the `MouseEventInit` and modifier init members are all applied even though the environment's class does not derive from `MouseEvent`, and omitted members report the browser defaults (`screenX`/`screenY` 0, `relatedTarget` null, `detail` 0, `buttons` 0). `dragExit` is deliberately excluded because browsers never fire it. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.test.ts`: "dispatch.%s applies the MouseEventInit and modifier init members")
- Given `dispatch.wheel` and `dispatch.drop`, when dispatched, then the members only `WheelEvent` and only `DragEvent` define are preserved. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.test.ts`: "dispatch.wheel keeps the members only WheelEvent defines", "dispatch.drop keeps the member only DragEvent defines")
- Given `dispatch.mouseDown`, when dispatched, then the computed mouse members are reported: `pageX`/`pageY` from client coordinates plus scroll, `which` from `button`, `x`/`y` aliasing client coordinates. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.test.ts`: "dispatch.mouseDown reports the computed mouse members")
- Given `dispatch.pointerDown` with nothing supplied, when dispatched, then it reports the `PointerEventInit` defaults for contact (`width`/`height` 1), pressure (0), and primary pointer (false unless set), and `altitudeAngle` π/2. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.test.ts`: "dispatch.pointerDown reports the PointerEventInit defaults for the contact, pressure, and primary pointer", "dispatch.pointerDown reports the transducer angles of a perpendicular pointer")
- Given explicit pointer values, when `dispatch.pointerDown` runs, then they are preserved, including a zero contact size and explicit transducer angles. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.test.ts`: "dispatch.pointerDown preserves provided pointer values", "dispatch.pointerDown preserves a zero contact size", "dispatch.pointerDown preserves provided transducer angles")
- Given only `tiltX`/`tiltY`, when `dispatch.pointerDown` runs, then `altitudeAngle`/`azimuthAngle` are derived from them; given only the spherical pair, the tilt pair is derived; given both pairs, both are preserved unchanged, matching Chromium and Firefox. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.test.ts`: "dispatch.pointerDown derives transducer angles from tilt", "dispatch.pointerDown derives tilt from transducer angles", "dispatch.pointerDown preserves both provided orientation pairs")
- Given `altitudeAngle: 0`, when the azimuth is 0, π/2, π, 3π/2, π/4, 3π/4, 5π/4 or 7π/4, then the derived tilt is respectively (90,0), (0,90), (-90,0), (0,-90), (90,90), (-90,90), (-90,-90), (90,-90). (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.test.ts`: "dispatch.pointerDown derives boundary tilt at azimuth %s")
- Given a rounded tilt of negative zero, when the pointer event is built, then it is normalized to positive zero. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.test.ts`: "dispatch.pointerDown normalizes rounded tilt to positive zero")
- Given `compositionstart`, `compositionupdate` or `compositionend` dispatched by name, then `data` defaults to the empty string, `detail` to 0 and `view` to null, and supplied values are preserved, even though happy-dom aliases `CompositionEvent` to `Event`. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.test.ts`: "dispatch.%s reports the CompositionEvent defaults", "dispatch.%s preserves the provided CompositionEvent members")
- Given `dispatch.input` with an explicit `inputType`, when dispatched, then it is preserved. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.test.ts`: "dispatch.input preserves provided inputType")
- Given a button inside a same-origin iframe, when `dispatch.keyDown` or `dispatch.mouseDown` targets it, then the event is an instance of the iframe's `UIEvent` and not the ambient one, `getModifierState("CapsLock")` is true, `getModifierState("Hyper")` is false (jsdom is the only environment that reports Hyper), `view` is null and `detail` is 0. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.jsdom.test.ts`: "dispatch.keyDown initializes an event dispatched inside an iframe", "dispatch.mouseDown initializes an event dispatched inside an iframe")
- Given an iframe `document` or `window` as the dispatch target, when `dispatch.keyDown` runs, then the realm is still resolved to that frame. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.jsdom.test.ts`: "dispatch.keyDown initializes an event dispatched at an iframe document", "dispatch.keyDown initializes an event dispatched at an iframe window")
- Given an iframe window scrolled to (40, 50), when `dispatch.mouseDown` fires with client coordinates (11, 12), then `pageX`/`pageY` are 51 and 62, derived from the target window rather than the top one. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.jsdom.test.ts`: "dispatch.mouseDown derives page coordinates from the target window")
- Given a button inside a same-origin iframe, when `dispatch.pointerDown` or `dispatch.click` targets it with `pointerType: "pen", tiltX: 30`, then the event is an instance of the iframe's `PointerEvent`, `altitudeAngle` is π/2 − π/6, `azimuthAngle` 0, `width` and `height` 1, `pointerType` "pen", `tiltX` 30, `detail` 0. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.jsdom.test.ts`: "dispatch.pointerDown initializes an event dispatched inside an iframe", "dispatch.click initializes an event dispatched inside an iframe")
- Given `dispatch.copy`, `dispatch.cut` or `dispatch.paste` with a caller-supplied `clipboardData`, when dispatched, then the listener receives that exact object and the dispatch resolves true. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.jsdom.test.ts`: "dispatch.copy delivers caller-supplied clipboardData", "dispatch.cut delivers caller-supplied clipboardData", "dispatch.paste delivers caller-supplied clipboardData")
- Given jsdom, which ships no `DragEvent` and whose `WheelEvent` already derives from `MouseEvent`, when `dispatch.wheel` or `dispatch.dragStart` runs, then both still get the `MouseEventInit` and modifier init members applied. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch.jsdom.test.ts`: "dispatch.wheel applies the MouseEventInit and modifier init members", "dispatch.dragStart applies the MouseEventInit and modifier init members")
- Given an environment with no `PointerEvent` constructor at all, when the click family is dispatched, then it is built from the closest available interface, pointer members are still initialized, and implicit form submission (which builds its click by hand) still works. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/dispatch-without-pointer-event.test.ts`: "runs in an environment with no PointerEvent constructor", "keeps the click family on the closest interface available", "submits a form implicitly, which builds its click by hand", "initializes pointer events built without the constructor")
- Given jsdom, when a `ClipboardEvent` is constructed from a `ClipboardEventInit`, then the shim is not needed and the native class is used; likewise the mouse-member and modifier-state shims leave a conformant environment alone. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/shims.jsdom.test.ts`: "constructs clipboard events from ClipboardEventInit", "leaves an environment that already implements mouse event members alone", "leaves an environment with a conformant modifier state alone")
- Given a required `input`, `select` or `textarea`, when it is disabled, then `validationMessage` is empty; when re-enabled it is non-empty; `setCustomValidity` replaces it and clearing custom validity restores the native message. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/shims.test.ts`: "preserves native validation messages for input controls", "preserves native validation messages for select controls", "preserves native validation messages for textarea controls")
- Given the package is imported, when any test runs, then the browser shims are already applied for the whole environment and remain applied after an interaction settles. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/shims.test.ts`: "applies the browser shims at import, for the whole environment", "keeps the browser shims applied after an interaction settles")
- Given several `requestAnimationFrame` callbacks registered in one turn, when the frame runs, then they all run as one batch with a single shared timestamp, callbacks registered during the flush are deferred to the next frame, and a callback can still cancel another not-yet-run callback in the same frame. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/shims.test.ts`: "runs animation frame callbacks as a spec-compliant batch", "cancels a not-yet-run animation frame callback within the same frame")
- Given mouse, pointer and keyboard events, when listeners read them, then they report the browser's exact modifier state and `x`/`y` aliases, and the keyboard-event constructor keeps its contract while patched (including throwing a `TypeError` when `getModifierState` is called with no argument). (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/shims.test.ts`: "gives mouse and pointer events the browser's modifier state and x/y", "gives keyboard events the browser's exact modifier state", "keeps the keyboard event constructor's contract while patching it")
- Given a dispatch in progress, when a listener reads `window.event`, then it is the event being dispatched, and a nested dispatch restores the outer value afterwards. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/shims.test.ts`: "exposes the dispatched event on window.event while listeners run", "restores window.event around a nested dispatch")
- Given a disabled button, when a click is dispatched on it, then the listener still runs, matching the spec, jsdom and browsers rather than happy-dom. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/shims.test.ts`: "runs the listener for a click dispatched on a disabled button")
- Given a disabled checkbox, when a scripted click is dispatched, then it toggles in either direction, its `indeterminate` state is cleared, and both are reverted if a listener prevents the click. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/shims.test.ts`: "toggles a disabled checkbox in either direction for a scripted click", "reverts a disabled checkbox toggle in either direction when a click listener prevents it", "clears and restores a disabled checkbox's indeterminate state on a scripted click")
- Given a disabled radio, when a scripted click is dispatched, then it becomes selected and `input`/`change` fire only when the selection actually changed; if a listener prevents the click, the whole group is restored, including a group linked by the `form` attribute rather than by nesting. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/shims.test.ts`: "selects a disabled radio on click and fires events only when it changes", "restores a disabled radio group when a click listener prevents the selection", "restores a disabled radio group linked by the form attribute when prevented")
- Given a prevented click on a disabled radio whose listener also changed another radio, when the revert runs, then only the activation's own changes are reverted and the listener's changes to other radios are preserved. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/shims.test.ts`: "reverts only the activation's changes, preserving listener changes to other radios")
- Given a disabled submit or reset control, when a click is dispatched on it, then the form is neither submitted nor reset. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/shims.test.ts`: "doesn't submit or reset a form from a click on a disabled submit/reset control")
- Given the `FormData` and select shims, when ancestor APIs are used, then form and select proxy identity is preserved, a proxied form reports itself as `currentTarget` while an event bubbles, and a select nested in a form reports its own descendants as contained. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-test/src/shims.test.ts`: "preserves form and select proxy identity across ancestor APIs", "reports a proxied form as currentTarget while an event bubbles", "reports a select nested in a form as containing its own descendants")

- `suppressConsoleLogs(cb, type)` replaces one console method with a jest mock for the duration of the callback and restores it in a `finally`, and it awaits the callback's promise so async tests stay covered; the default suppressed method is `console.error` in React but `console.warn` in Vue. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/suppress-console-logs.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/suppress-console-logs.ts)
- `mockingConsoleLogs(cb, type)` does the same but hands the spy to the callback, so a test can assert on the exact warning text rather than merely silencing it. [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/suppress-console-logs.ts)
- `html` and `jsx` are tagged-template helpers that just join the template strings, existing only so editors syntax-highlight Vue template literals. [vue only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/html.ts)
- The Vue suite ships its own testing-library replacement built on `@vue/test-utils` `mount`: it appends a fresh `div` inside another `div` under `document.body` and mounts into the inner one, so `container` is always a real parent element. [vue only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/vue-testing-library.ts)
- The Vue `render` helper returns `unmount`, a `container` getter, a `debug` logger and an `asFragment()` that clones the container's inner HTML through a `template` element, which is the shape `executeTimeline` depends on. [vue only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/vue-testing-library.ts)
- The Vue render helper tracks every mounted wrapper in a module-level set and registers an `afterEach` that unmounts them all, swallowing unmount errors, and then clears `document.body.innerHTML`, so leaked portals cannot bleed into the next test. [vue only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/vue-testing-library.ts)
- `createRenderTemplate(defaultComponents)` returns a render function that accepts either a raw template string or a component options object and merges a fixed set of components into it, which is how each Vue component suite gets one-line template rendering with its own components pre-registered. [vue only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/vue-testing-library.ts)
- `assertComboboxList` rewrites its error stack using `assertCombobox` rather than itself, so a failure inside it reports the wrong assertion name in both frameworks. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `mouseDrag` also rewrites its error stack using `click`, in both frameworks. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)

## dialog

### Roles and attributes

- Given a closed dialog that stays mounted, when it is inspected, then both the dialog element and its backdrop carry the `hidden` attribute; opening removes it from both and closing puts it back on both. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-backdrop-7344/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-backdrop-7344/test.ts`: "backdrop carries the hidden attribute along with the dialog")
- Given an open dialog, when its backdrop is queried, then the backdrop is exposed with role `presentation` and carries `data-backdrop="<dialog id>"` linking it to the dialog. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-backdrop-7335/test.ts`: "backdrop toggle keeps the contents of a modal dialog")
- Given an open dialog, when a leave transition runs, then the dialog element carries `data-leave="true"` while it is still attached, and `data-enter="true"` while it is entering. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-3403/test-browser.ts`: "dialog with explicit store waits for leave transition before unmount"; `app/src/sandbox/dialog-5057/test-browser.ts`: "data-enter is re-added when dialog with render wrapper reopens")
- Given a nested non-portalled dialog, when the parent dialog is queried, then the parent has no `dialog` role while the nested one is open and is matched only by the generic `none` role query, which is how the suite distinguishes a portalled from an inline nested dialog. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-nested-variants/test.ts`: "show nested no portal dialog and hide with escape")

- Given a `Dialog.Title`, `Dialog.Panel`, `DialogOverlay` or `DialogBackdrop` rendered without a parent `Dialog`, when it mounts, then it throws a descriptive error. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.ts`: "should error when we are using a <%s /> without a parent <Dialog />")
- Given a `Dialog`, when it renders, then it does so without crashing. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.ts`: "should be possible to render a Dialog without crashing")
- Given an explicit `role`, when it is `dialog` or `alertdialog`, then that role is used; an invalid role falls back to `dialog`. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.ts`: "should be able to explicitly choose role=dialog", "should be able to explicitly choose role=alertdialog", "should fall back to role=dialog for an invalid role")
- Given a `Dialog` with a missing `open` or `onClose` prop, when it renders, then it complains: React errors when both are missing, when `open` is given without `onClose`, when `onClose` is given without `open`, when `open` is not a boolean, or when `onClose` is not a function. Vue complains when `open` is missing and when `open` is not a boolean. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.tsx`: "should complain when the `open` and `onClose` prop are missing", "should complain when an `open` prop is provided without an `onClose` prop", "should complain when an `onClose` prop is provided without an `open` prop", "should complain when an `open` prop is not a boolean", "should complain when an `onClose` prop is not a function"; `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.ts`: "should complain when an `open` prop is missing", "should complain when an `open` prop is not a boolean")
- Given a render prop, when `Dialog`, `Dialog.Title` or `Dialog.Description` renders through it, then the slot receives the component's state and the output is rendered. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.ts`: "should be possible to render a Dialog using a render prop", "should be possible to render Dialog.Title using a render prop", "should be possible to render Dialog.Description using a render prop", "should be possible to render DialogTitle using a render prop", "should be possible to render DialogDescription using a render prop")
- Given extra props passed to the `Dialog` itself, when it renders, then they reach the element. [vue only] (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.ts`: "should be possible to pass props to the Dialog itself")
- Given a `DialogOverlay` with a render prop, when it renders, then the slot output is used. [vue only] (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.ts`: "should be possible to render DialogOverlay using a render prop")
- Given a `DialogBackdrop` used without a `DialogPanel`, when it renders, then it throws; with a `DialogPanel` present it does not, and the backdrop is portalled. [vue only] (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.ts`: "should throw an error if a DialogBackdrop is used without a DialogPanel", "should not throw an error if a DialogBackdrop is used with a DialogPanel", "should portal the DialogBackdrop")
- Given a `DialogBackdrop` or `DialogPanel`, when a ref is attached, then it resolves to the rendered element. [vue only] (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.ts`: "should be possible to access the ref on the DialogBackdrop", "should be possible to access the ref on the DialogPanel")
- Given a dialog with an explicit `aria-label`, when it opens, then it carries that `aria-label` and no `aria-labelledby` at all, so the component's generated label reference is suppressed rather than duplicated. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/aria-labelledby-aria-label/test-chrome.ts`: "dialog with aria-label has no aria-labelledby")

### Keyboard

- Given a closed dialog, when the disclosure is activated by click, Enter, or Space, then the dialog opens and focus lands on its first focusable element. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-core-interactions/test.ts`: "opens from the disclosure with click", "opens from the disclosure with Enter", "opens from the disclosure with Space"; `app/src/sandbox/dialog-details-enhancement/test.ts`: "show on disclosure click", "show on disclosure enter", "show on disclosure space")
- Given an open dialog, when Escape is pressed, then it closes and focus returns to the disclosure. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-core-interactions/test.ts`: "closes with Escape and restores disclosure focus"; `app/src/sandbox/dialog-details-enhancement/test.ts`: "hide on escape")
- Given an open dialog whose only focusable element is one button, when Tab or Shift+Tab is pressed, then focus stays on that button, because the modal dialog traps focus. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-core-interactions/test.ts`: "keeps focus on the only dialog button with synthetic Tab"; `app/src/sandbox/dialog-details-enhancement/test.ts`: "focus trap")
- Given an open dialog with a dismiss button, when that button is activated by click, Enter, or Space, then the dialog closes and focus returns to the disclosure. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-core-interactions/test.ts`: "closes from the dismiss button with click", "closes from the dismiss button with Enter", "closes from the dismiss button with Space"; `app/src/sandbox/dialog-details-enhancement/test.ts`: "hide on dismiss button click", "hide on dismiss button enter", "hide on dismiss button space")
- Given an open dialog containing a combobox with an open listbox, when Escape is pressed, then the combobox popup closes first and the dialog stays open; a second Escape closes the dialog. This holds when the child is rendered inline, through an Ariakit Portal, or through a React portal. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-5179/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-5179/test.ts`: "lets a child handle Escape before the dialog", "lets a Ariakit Portal child handle Escape before the dialog", "lets a React portal child handle Escape before the dialog")
- Given a dialog whose ancestor installs a capture-phase keydown handler that stops Escape, when Escape is pressed inside it, then neither the child popup nor the dialog closes. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-5179/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-5179/test.ts`: "lets an ancestor capture handler own Escape")
- Given an open dialog and focus on an element outside it, when Escape is pressed there and nothing claims it, then the dialog closes. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-5179/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-5179/test.ts`: "closes on an unclaimed Escape outside the dialog")
- Given an ancestor capture handler that stops Escape, when Escape is pressed outside the dialog, then the dialog stays open. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-5179/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-5179/test.ts`: "lets an ancestor capture handler own Escape outside the dialog")
- Given a dialog whose own bubble-phase handler stops Escape, when Escape is pressed, then the inner popup closes on the first press and the dialog closes on the second: the dialog's own handler does not lock it open. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-5179/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-5179/test.ts`: "hides after its own bubble handler stops Escape")
- Given a dialog whose own capture-phase handler stops Escape, when Escape is pressed, then the dialog still closes. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-5179/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-5179/test.ts`: "hides after its own capture handler stops Escape")

### Focus management

- Given a dialog whose content is replaced while it is open, when a persistent element outside is focused, then the dialog stays open, so the dialog tracks its element identity rather than a captured node. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-persistent-elements/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-persistent-elements/test.ts`: "keeps persistent elements after replacing an open dialog node")
- Given a dialog with `autoFocusOnShow={false}` that has therefore never held focus, when a persistent element outside it is clicked or right-clicked, then the dialog stays open. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-persistent-elements/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-persistent-elements/test.ts`: "stays open when interacting with a persistent element before the dialog is focused", "stays open on right-clicking a persistent element before the dialog is focused")
- Given a dialog that has already been focused, when a persistent outside element is clicked, then it still stays open. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-persistent-elements/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-persistent-elements/test.ts`: "keeps the documented behavior after the dialog has been focused")
- Given a dialog that was focused inside, then closed and reopened, when a brand-new element outside gains focus, then the dialog closes, because reopening resets the "was focused inside" flag. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-reopen-focus-state/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-reopen-focus-state/test.ts`: "resets outside-interaction focus tracking when reopened")
- Given a form control literally named `activeElement` that shadows the document's own property, when the dialog closes, then focus is still restored to the disclosure. Real-browser only, because happy-dom implements no document named getter. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-form-named-active-element/test-browser.ts`: "restores dialog focus past a named activeElement form")
- Given the same named-`activeElement` form, when focus escapes to another element inside the dialog, then the dialog's queued auto-focus does not pull it back. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-form-named-active-element/test-browser.ts`: "keeps escaped focus past a named activeElement form")
- Given a nested confirm dialog, when it closes, then focus returns to the control inside the parent dialog that opened it, not to the parent's own first focusable element. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-nested-cart/test.ts`: "show confirm dialog", "hide confirm dialog by pressing escape")
- Given a nested confirm dialog closed by an outside click, when it closes, then the parent dialog is visible again but the opening control is not refocused. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-nested-cart/test.ts`: "hide confirm dialog by clicking outside")
- Given a dialog with a `details`/`summary` progressive-enhancement disclosure, when the `details` element is opened before JavaScript runs, then after hydration the dialog is visible and its first button is focused. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-details-enhancement/test-browser.ts`: "show before JavaScript enhancement")
- Given nested non-portalled dialogs, when Shift+Tab is pressed twice from the first focusable element, then focus returns to that same element, so the trap wraps within the innermost dialog even without a portal. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-nested-variants/test.ts`: "show nested no portal dialog and hide with escape", "show nested no portal portal dialog and hide with escape")

- Given a dialog with a long body, when it opens, then the action is focused without scrolling the body. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/ariakit-ui-dialog/test-chrome.ts`: "focuses the action after a long body without scrolling the body")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a dialog whose `open` prop is controlled and never set to false, when Escape is pressed or the outside is clicked, then it stays open and keeps focus on its button. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-controlled-open/test.ts`: "keep dialog open when pressing escape", "keep dialog open when clicking outside")
- Given a controlled dialog with no explicit store, when it is closed, then it still waits for its leave transition before unmounting, the same as one with an explicit store. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-3403/test-browser.ts`: "dialog with explicit store waits for leave transition before unmount", "controlled dialog without explicit store waits for leave transition before unmount")
- Given a route-driven dialog without `unmountOnHide`, when Escape is pressed, then the element stays attached but becomes not visible. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-3403/test-browser.ts`: "route dialog without unmountOnHide preserves close behavior")
- Given a dialog whose backdrop prop toggles between falsy and truthy while it is open, when the toggle flips either way, then only the backdrop mounts or unmounts: the dialog element identity, its form values, and its internal state all survive. This is asserted for a modal dialog and for an inline non-modal one. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-backdrop-7335/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-backdrop-7335/test.ts`: "backdrop toggle keeps the contents of a modal dialog", "backdrop toggle keeps the contents of an inline dialog")
- Given a dialog whose backdrop only changes appearance (staying truthy), when the class changes, then the contents are likewise preserved; this is the control case that isolates the falsy/truthy boundary from an ordinary re-render. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-backdrop-7335/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-backdrop-7335/test.ts`: "changing the backdrop's appearance keeps the contents")
- Given losing the backdrop, when the backdrop is removed, then it is unmounted rather than left mounted and hidden, verified by querying `[data-backdrop="<id>"]` directly instead of by role. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-backdrop-7335/test.ts`: "backdrop toggle keeps the contents of a modal dialog")

### Forms

- Given a dialog containing a form whose control is named `self`, when the disclosure is clicked, then the dialog opens. A second control named `document` makes the form answer the document lookup with that control, which the dialog must also survive, and closing then restores focus. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-form-7201/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-form-7201/test.ts`: "opens a form dialog whose control is named self", "opens a form dialog whose controls are named self and document")
- Given a dialog with a dirty form and a `hideOnEscape`/`hideOnInteractOutside` guard, when Escape is pressed, the backdrop is clicked, or the dismiss button is clicked, then a confirmation dialog opens with its Save button focused and the original dialog becomes inert but stays visually present; Escape or an outside click on the confirmation returns to the original with the textbox refocused; confirming closes both and returns focus to the original disclosure. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-hide-warning/test.ts`: "try to hide the dialog with Escape after filling in the form", "try to hide the dialog by clicking outside after filling in the form", "try to hide the dialog by clicking on the dismiss button after filling in the form")
- Given the same dialog with an empty form, when the dismiss button is clicked, then it closes without a confirmation. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-hide-warning/test.ts`: "open/hide dialog without filling in the form")
- Given the hide-warning example, when it is built with an explicit store or with `unmountOnHide`, then it passes the identical suite, which both sandboxes import verbatim. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-hide-warning-store/test.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-hide-warning-unmount/test.ts`)

- Given a form inside a dialog, when it is submitted, then the submission goes through. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.ts`: "should be possible to submit a form inside a Dialog")

- Given a form inside the dialog, when it is submitted, then the dialog closes with the new name; cancelling keeps the previously saved name. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/ariakit-ui-dialog/test-chrome.ts`: "submits the form and closes the dialog with the new name", "keeps the saved name when the form is canceled")

### Dismissal and layering

- Given a modal dialog, when it opens, then the page scroll is locked and, where `scrollbar-gutter` is supported, the lock lands on the `html` element as `scrollbar-gutter: stable` plus `overflow-x: hidden` plus `overflow-y: hidden`, leaving the body styles and `--scrollbar-width` untouched; closing restores the page's own inline `overflow-y: scroll` exactly and removes the rest. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-4345/test.ts`: "scroll lock preserves the html element's inline overflow-y"; `app/src/sandbox/dialog-nested-variants/test.ts`: "show dialog and hide with escape")
- Given an environment where `CSS.supports` returns false, when a modal dialog opens, then the fallback lock sets `--scrollbar-width` on `html`, sets `overflow: hidden` and `padding-right` on the body, and additionally hides the `html` overflow when the page scrolls through `html`; closing removes all of it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-4345/test.ts`: "fallback scroll lock also hides the html overflow"; `app/src/sandbox/dialog-nested-variants/test.ts`: "fall back to body padding without scrollbar-gutter support")
- Given a real browser with the page scrolled down, when a modal dialog opens, then a wheel event does not move the page, the scroll position is preserved, and after closing the page scrolls again. The `html`-level lock is required because the page scrolls through `html`, so a body-only lock would not block it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-4345/test-browser.ts`: "locks the page scroll and preserves the html inline overflow-y")
- Given a stack of nested modal dialogs, when each layer is open, then the body cannot be scrolled, and only after the last one closes does scrolling work again. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-nested-variants/test-browser.ts`: every "hide ... by pressing Escape" and "hide ... by clicking outside" case)
- Given nested dialogs, when a child is open, then the parent dialog is removed from the accessibility tree by an `[inert]` ancestor while remaining visually present, and it is restored when the child closes. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-nested-variants/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-nested-variants/test.ts`: the nested and sibling Escape matrices; `app/src/sandbox/dialog-5238/test-browser.ts`: "keeps the frontmost initially open sibling dialog interactive")
- Given two sibling dialogs that both start open, when the page loads, then the one behind is already inside `[inert]` and the frontmost one is not. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-5238/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-5238/test.ts`: "keeps the frontmost initially open sibling dialog interactive")
- Given sibling dialogs rendered inside an open shadow root, when they mount, then the same inert layering applies within the shadow tree and the frontmost one stays interactive. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-5238/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-5238/test.ts`: "keeps initially open sibling dialogs interactive in a shadow root")
- Given an open modal dialog, when a document event arrives whose `target` is a non-Node `EventTarget` (window, an XHR, and similar third-party dispatches), then the interact-outside click/focusin/contextmenu listeners and the Escape keydown listener all handle it without throwing, and the dialog stays open. A recorded foreign `mousedown` target must also not make a later genuine outside click close it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-5156/test-browser.ts`: "does not throw when a document event has a non-Node target")
- Given a modal dialog, when a persistent element inside a shadow root is clicked, focused, or dragged from, then the dialog stays open; when an unrelated shadow-root element, an outside shadow field, an outside shadow button with no focus behavior, or a same-id dialog in another root is clicked, then the dialog closes. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-persistent-elements/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-persistent-elements/test.ts`: "stays open when interacting with a persistent shadow element", "stays open when dragging from persistent shadow content", "closes when interacting inside an unrelated shadow root", "closes on a no-focus outside shadow click", "closes when interacting with a same-id dialog in another root")
- Given a focus event fired by a shadow element that is not connected to the document, when it arrives, then the dialog ignores it and stays open. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-persistent-elements/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-persistent-elements/test.ts`: "ignores focus events from disconnected shadow elements")
- Given a dialog whose element was replaced while open, when an outside element inserted after the replacement is clicked, then the dialog still closes. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-persistent-elements/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-persistent-elements/test.ts`: "closes on a newly inserted outside element after replacing the dialog", "still closes when interacting outside before the dialog is focused")
- Given descendants of a persistent `form` element, when one of them is clicked, then they count as inside the dialog context and the dialog stays open. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-persistent-elements/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-persistent-elements/test.ts`: "keeps descendants of a persistent form inside the dialog context")
- Given a combobox popover and a persistent element, when the persistent element is clicked, then the popover stays open and the click still reaches the element's own handler. - Given a dialog with a persistent notification region, when the notification's close button is activated from inside the modal dialog, then the notification is removed and the dialog stays open, so persistent content stays interactive under a modal. - Given a popover in an iframe, when focus moves to the parent document, then it hides; when a sibling iframe is clicked, a sibling frame reuses the disclosure id, or a bodyless (SVG-only) frame document is clicked, then it also hides; when a contained iframe inside the popover is clicked, then it stays open. - Given a popover inside an iframe with its disclosure in the parent document, when the parent disclosure is clicked twice, then the popover toggles; when the disclosure is dragged to a parent element, then the popover stays open.
