### Animation and presence

- Given a closing dialog with a leave transition, when it closes, then it stays attached with `data-leave="true"` and only then unmounts, so the leave transition is not cut short. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-3403/test-browser.ts`: "dialog with explicit store waits for leave transition before unmount", "controlled dialog without explicit store waits for leave transition before unmount")
- Given a dialog wrapped by a `render` prop that nests the dialog element inside another div, when it closes, then `data-enter` is removed even though the dialog element itself has no CSS transition, and it is re-added when the dialog reopens so the enter animation replays. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-5057/test-browser.ts`: "data-enter is removed when dialog with render wrapper closes", "data-enter is re-added when dialog with render wrapper reopens")
- Given a dialog where only the backdrop is animated, when it closes, then focus returns to the disclosure immediately while the backdrop gets `data-leave="true"` and stays visible for its own 500ms exit transition before its `display` becomes `none`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-backdrop-6339/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-backdrop-6339/test.ts`: "backdrop fades out on close when only the backdrop is animated")
- Given a backdrop with a 2s transition and a panel with a 150ms one, when the dialog closes, then the backdrop keeps `data-leave` and stays visible past 250ms and only hides when its own transition ends, so the shorter panel timeout does not stop the shared animation state. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-backdrop-6339/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-backdrop-6339/test.ts`: "backdrop finishes its longer fade out when the panel has a shorter transition")
- Given the animated-dialog variant matrix (Transition, TransitionBackdrop, TransitionUnmount, TransitionNoModal, TransitionNoLeave, Animation, AnimationBackdrop, AnimationUnmount, AnimationNoModal, AnimationLeave, AnimationUnmountLeave), when each opens, then the dialog becomes visible and its Close button is focused; when Enter closes it, then focus returns to the trigger and, for every variant that has a leave phase, the dialog remains in the document without the `hidden` attribute and without `display: none` while leaving, becoming inert (so it is matched only by the `hidden` query variant) before finally unmounting. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-animated-variants/test.ts`: "Transition", "TransitionBackdrop", "TransitionUnmount", "TransitionNoModal", "TransitionNoLeave", "Animation", "AnimationBackdrop", "AnimationUnmount", "AnimationNoModal", "AnimationLeave", "AnimationUnmountLeave")
- Given a dialog with a leave transition in a real browser, when it closes, then focus returns to the disclosure while the dialog is still visible for the duration of the transition. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-animated/test-browser.ts`: "show/hide preserves the leave transition")
- Given nested dialogs with animated dismissal, when each layer opens, then the layer beneath becomes not visible while the stack keeps the scroll locked, and Escape from the innermost restores focus all the way to the original disclosure and unlocks scrolling. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-nested-variants/test-browser.ts`: "nested dismiss animated", "sibling dismiss animated", "sibling dismiss animated unmount"; `app/src/sandbox/dialog-nested-variants/test.ts`: "show nested dismiss dialog and hide with escape", "show sibling dismiss dialog and hide with escape", "show sibling dismiss unmount dialog and hide with escape")

- Given a `static` prop, when the dialog renders, then it is always rendered, with focus trapping enabled or disabled according to `open`. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.ts`: "should be possible to always render the Dialog if we provide it a `static` prop (and enable focus trapping based on `open`)", "should be possible to always render the Dialog if we provide it a `static` prop (and disable focus trapping based on `open`)")
- Given the `unmount` render strategy, when the dialog closes, then the alternative strategy is honored. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.ts`: "should be possible to use a different render strategy for the Dialog")
- Given a `Transition` wrapping the dialog, when the transition shows or hides, then the dialog opens and closes accordingly. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.ts`: "should be possible to open the Dialog via a Transition component", "should be possible to close the Dialog via a Transition component")

- Given `prefers-reduced-motion`, when a dialog opens, then neither the dialog nor the backdrop animation runs. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/ariakit-ui-dialog/test-chrome.ts`: "runs no dialog or backdrop animation when the user prefers reduced motion")

### SSR and hydration

- Given a Next.js App Router route-driven dialog, when the link is clicked, then the URL changes, the dialog becomes visible, and the email field is focused; Escape restores the URL, hides the dialog, and refocuses the link; going back reopens it; clicking outside closes it and restores the URL and focus. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-nextjs-app-router/test-chrome-firefox.ts`: "opens and closes the route-driven dialog")
- Given direct navigation to the dialog's URL, when the page loads, then the dialog is open with the email field focused, and back, forward, and reload all keep the state consistent; Enter submits and returns to the base URL with the link focused. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-nextjs-app-router/test-chrome-firefox.ts`: "supports direct navigation and browser history")
- Given a link-driven dialog, when the link is clicked or activated with Enter, then the dialog opens with the textbox focused; clicking the dismiss link or pressing Enter on the refocused disclosure closes it and keeps focus on the link. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-route-state/test.ts`: "show/hide on disclosure click with mouse", "show/hide on disclosure click with keyboard", "hide on escape", "hide on click outside")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given a modal dialog with no dismiss element of its own, when it opens, then a fallback "Dismiss popup" button is rendered next to the dialog rather than inside it, so a dialog whose role does not allow a `button` among its owned elements still gets one; the dialog itself contains no button. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-hidden-dismiss/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-hidden-dismiss/test.ts`: "modal dialog without a dismiss element gets a hidden one")
- Given the fallback dismiss button, when it is activated, then the dialog closes and focus returns to the disclosure, even though the button lives outside every "inside the dialog" check. The browser test dispatches the click directly because the modal backdrop absorbs a pointer click on it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-hidden-dismiss/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-hidden-dismiss/test.ts`: "hidden dismiss closes the dialog and restores focus")
- Given a dialog that never took focus, when the fallback dismiss button is focused, then the dialog does not treat that as an outside interaction and stays open. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-hidden-dismiss/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-hidden-dismiss/test.ts`: "hidden dismiss doesn't count as outside a dialog that never took focus")
- Given a modal dialog that already has its own dismiss element, when it opens, then no fallback button is rendered. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-hidden-dismiss/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-hidden-dismiss/test.ts`: "modal dialog with a dismiss element gets no hidden one")
- Given a dismiss button that belongs to a nested popover or submenu rendered inline inside the dialog, when the dialog opens, then the fallback button is still rendered because that dismiss only closes the nested popup, and it stays rendered while the nested popup is open and after it closes. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-hidden-dismiss/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-hidden-dismiss/test.ts`: "dismiss owned by a nested popup doesn't replace the hidden one", "dismiss owned by a submenu doesn't replace the hidden one")
- Given a dialog that owns a dismiss element appearing after a nested popup's in document order and wrapped in another element, when it opens, then no fallback button is rendered. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-hidden-dismiss/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-hidden-dismiss/test.ts`: "dialog owning a dismiss after a nested popup's gets no hidden one")
- Given a dialog that gains a dismiss control while it is open (async content load), when the control mounts, then the fallback is removed; given one that loses its dismiss control while open, when it unmounts, then the fallback comes back. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-hidden-dismiss/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/dialog-hidden-dismiss/test.ts`: "dismiss mounted while the dialog is open replaces the hidden one", "dismiss unmounted while the dialog is open brings the hidden one back")
- Given nested dialogs, when the child opens, then the parent's fallback dismiss button becomes hidden from assistive technology along with everything else outside the child, and it is exposed again when the child closes, verified through a real accessibility-tree read rather than by attribute. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-hidden-dismiss/test-chrome.ts`: "nested dialog disables the hidden dismiss and restores it", using `app/src/test-utils/accessibility.ts`'s `createDismissAccessibilityReader`)

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a `DialogDisclosure` whose `render` prop passes `onClick={undefined}`, when it is clicked, then the internal click handler still runs and the dialog opens, so prop merging does not let an explicit undefined overwrite it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-disclosure-5224/test-chrome-firefox.ts`: "dialog opens when render prop has onClick={undefined}")
- Given `className="base"` and `render={<a className={undefined}>}`, when the element is rendered, then its class attribute is exactly `base`, with no `undefined` appended. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-disclosure-5224/test-chrome-firefox.ts`: "className does not include falsy values from render prop")
- Given a combobox inside a dialog with `autoSelect`, when text is typed that overflows the input and then narrows the result list, then the input's `scrollLeft` stays greater than zero, so the virtual-focus dance that runs on an async item change does not reset the scroll position. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-combobox-4825/test-browser.ts`: "combobox input preserves scroll position when results change")
- Given a command-menu dialog built from a dialog plus combobox, when it opens by click, then the dialog is visible, the combobox is focused, the first option is the active item, and the group heading is visible; Escape returns focus to the trigger and unmounts the dialog. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-combobox-command-menu/test.ts`: "open dialog with click and hide with esc")
- Given the command menu, when the outside is clicked, then it closes and focus is not restored to the trigger. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-combobox-command-menu/test.ts`: "open dialog with click and hide by clicking outside")
- Given the command menu opened with Enter, when Tab moves focus to the Esc button and Enter activates it, then the dialog closes. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-combobox-command-menu/test.ts`: "open dialog with enter and hide by pressing enter on esc button")
- Given the command menu, when ArrowDown and ArrowUp are pressed, then the active option moves while DOM focus stays on the combobox (virtual focus), and ArrowUp past the first option stops there rather than wrapping. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-combobox-command-menu/test.ts`: "navigate through items with keyboard")
- Given the command menu, when an option is hovered, then it becomes the active item while DOM focus stays on the combobox; hovering outside the list leaves the active item unchanged, and clicking the combobox also leaves it unchanged. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-combobox-command-menu/test.ts`: "navigate though items with mouse")
- Given the command menu, when a query is typed, then the results group appears with the best match active, narrowing the query narrows the option count, a query with no matches renders zero options plus a "No results found" message, and deleting back to empty restores the original active option. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-combobox-command-menu/test.ts`: "search")
- Given the tabbed command-menu variants (Simple, With Tabs, With Tabs 2 columns, With Tabs 3 columns), when each opens, then the first option is focused with `data-active-item` and without `data-focus-visible`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-combobox-tab-command-menu/test.ts`: "open command menu when button is clicked and focus on the first option")
- Given any command-menu variant, when Escape is pressed, the outside is clicked, or the Esc button is clicked, then the dialog unmounts. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-combobox-tab-command-menu/test.ts`: "close command menu when Escape key is pressed", "close command menu when clicking outside", "close command menu when clicking on the esc button")
- Given any command-menu variant, when a query is typed, then the option count drops to 5, the first match becomes active, and it now carries `data-focus-visible` as well as `data-active-item`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-combobox-tab-command-menu/test.ts`: "filter options when typing")
- Given any command-menu variant, when it is closed and reopened, then the filter is reset: the full option list returns and the combobox value is empty. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-combobox-tab-command-menu/test.ts`: "closing and reopening the command menu should reset filter")
- Given a tabbed command menu, when it opens, then the first tab has `aria-selected="true"`, does not have `data-active-item`, and its panel is visible. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-combobox-tab-command-menu/test.ts`: "the first tab is selected by default")
- Given a tabbed command menu, when Tab is pressed, then the next tab is selected (`aria-selected` flips, the previous panel unmounts, the new tab gains `data-active-item`), Shift+Tab moves back, and Tab past the last tab moves focus to the Esc button with `data-focus-visible` while the last tab keeps `aria-selected="true"` and `data-active-item` but loses focus and `data-focus-visible`; Shift+Tab from the Esc button returns focus to that tab and restores `data-focus-visible`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-combobox-tab-command-menu/test.ts`: "pressing Tab key should select tabs", "pressing Tab key past the last tab should move focus to the Esc button")
- Given focus on a tab in a command menu, when ArrowRight and ArrowLeft are pressed, then the selected tab changes and the panels swap. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-combobox-tab-command-menu/test.ts`: "change tabs with arrow keys after pressing Tab key")
- Given a grid-layout command menu, when ArrowRight moves within the grid and ArrowUp is pressed from the first row, then focus leaves the grid and lands on the currently selected tab, which gains `data-active-item` and `data-focus-visible` while the option loses both. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-combobox-tab-command-menu/test.ts`: "pressing arrow keys moves focus between grid items and tabs", "move horizontally to wrap lines")
- Given a grid-layout command menu with a filter applied, when arrow keys move through the filtered grid, then `focusShift` lands on the expected item; the test tolerates one extra ArrowDown, which records that the exact row shape depends on the filtered result count. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-combobox-tab-command-menu/test.ts`: "focusShift")
- Given a dialog and a menu inside it, when the menu button is clicked twice, then the menu toggles closed and open again, and the menu element itself holds DOM focus each time it opens. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-menu-interactions/test.ts`: "show/hide menu"; `app/src/sandbox/dialog-menu-interactions/test-browser.ts`: "open/close menu by clicking on menu button")
- Given a `Dialog` that keeps its element mounted while closed, when the Safari-specific effect that tracks the last mousedown resolves the document at mount, then Safari reaches the realm helpers before the dialog is ever opened, which is why the named-control regression is reproducible without opening the dialog. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-form-7201/test-browser.ts`: file comment)
- Given the nested-dialog browser matrix, when it runs on WebKit, then the suite reuses one browser context per worker rather than opening a new one per test, recorded as a WebKit stability workaround. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/dialog-nested-variants/test-browser.ts`: `test.use({ reuseContext: true })`)

- Given a dialog opened from inside a `Popover`, when it opens and then closes, then both behave correctly together. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/dialog/dialog.test.ts`: "should be possible to open a dialog from inside a Popover (and then close it)")

## menu

### Roles and attributes

- Given a menu, when it opens, then it has role `menu`, its items have role `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox`, or `menuitemradio`, and separators inside it have role `separator`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-core-interactions/test.ts`: "show/hide on click"; `app/src/sandbox/menu-context-interactions/test-chrome.ts`: "context menu keeps a dismiss button outside the menu")
- Given a menu, when it opens, then `aria-labelledby` on the menu points at its disclosure's id, and when the disclosure is replaced by a different element the stale `aria-labelledby` is removed rather than left pointing at a gone id. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-7315/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/menu-7315/test.ts`: "does not keep the previous disclosure label")
- Given a menu button whose menu contains a combobox, when the menu opens, then the button's `aria-haspopup` stays `dialog` and does not flip to `menu`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-nested-combobox/test-browser.ts`: "MenuButton aria-haspopup should not change when menu with combobox is opened")
- Given a submenu button whose submenu contains a combobox, when inspected, then it has `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, and clicking it does not close the parent menu. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-nested-combobox/test-browser.ts`: "clicking submenu button with combobox should not close parent menu")
- Given a disabled menu button built either through `MenuButton` props or through a `render` prop, when inspected, then it has `aria-disabled="true"` and does not have the `disabled` attribute, so it stays focusable. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-button-disabled/test-browser.ts`: "disabled menu button with render remains accessible", "disabled rendered button does not open menu with arrow keys")
- Given a `menuitemcheckbox`, when toggled, then `aria-checked` flips between `"true"` and `"false"`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-checkbox-interactions/test.ts`: "check/uncheck menu item on click", "check/uncheck menu item on enter", "check/uncheck menu item on space")
- Given a `menuitemradio` with a default value, when the menu opens, then that item has `aria-checked="true"` and the others `"false"`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-radio-interactions/test.ts`: "default checked menu item")
- Given menu values wired to boolean item state, when the menu opens, then each `menuitemcheckbox` reflects the store value in `aria-checked` and the serialized store reads `{"showSidebar":true,"minimap":true}`. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-item-checked/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/menu-item-checked/test.ts`: "syncs boolean item checked state with menu values")
- Given a `menuitemradio` with `defaultChecked`, when rendered, then `aria-checked` is `"true"` and the `defaultChecked` prop is not leaked onto the DOM element as `data-default-checked-prop`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-item-checked/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/menu-item-checked/test.ts`: "does not leak defaultChecked to the rendered menu item")
- Given a menu, when an item becomes the active item, then it carries `data-active-item`, and when the active item was reached from the keyboard it also carries `data-focus-visible`, which is absent when it was reached by hover. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-core-interactions/test.ts`: "show/hide on enter", "navigate through items with mouse"; `app/src/sandbox/menu-combobox-interactions/test.ts`: "move through items with mouse and keyboard")
- Given a menu popup, when a positioning pass is in flight, then the popup element carries `data-placing`, and it is removed only when the pass finishes. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-placing-pass/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/menu-placing-pass/test.ts`: "keeps the popup unplaced while a custom updatePosition is still working")
- Given a menu with `autoFocusOnShow` as a callback, when the menu opens, then the item the callback picks carries `data-autofocus-on-show-callback="true"`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-5899/test-browser.ts`: "Callback autoFocusOnShow false calls the callback")
- Given an open submenu, when its parent item is inspected, then `aria-expanded` is `"true"`, and it returns to `"false"` when the submenu closes. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-nested-search-interactions/test.ts`: "open/hide with search submenu"; `app/src/sandbox/menubar-7410/test.ts`: "arrow keys open and close the menus of a vertical menubar")

- Given a `Menu.Button`, `Menu.Items` or `Menu.Item` rendered without a parent `Menu`, when it mounts, then it throws. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/menu/menu.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/menu/menu.test.tsx`: "should error when we are using a <%s /> without a parent <Menu />")
- Given a closed `Menu`, when it renders, then the button and items satisfy `assertMenuButton` and `assertMenu` for the closed state, and nothing crashes. Vue also renders with no children at all. ### Keyboard

- Given a closed menu, when Enter or Space activates the menu button, then the menu opens with its first item as the active item and `data-focus-visible` set. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-core-interactions/test.ts`: "show/hide on enter", "show/hide on space")
