### Focus management

- Given a menu opened by click, when it becomes visible, then DOM focus is on the `menu` element itself rather than on any item; opened by keyboard, focus lands on an item. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-core-interactions/test.ts`: "show/hide on click", "show/hide on enter")
- Given a modal menu, when its disclosure button is inspected, then only that button joins the modal context and stays outside the `inert` subtree, so the menu's `aria-labelledby` can still resolve; every other outside element gets `inert=""` and refuses focus, which keeps focus inside the menu even when something calls `focus()` outside. Chromium only for the real accessibility-tree read. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-4270/test-chrome.ts`: "modal menu keeps the accessible name from its menu button"; `app/src/sandbox/menu-4270/test.ts`: "modal menu keeps its menu button exposed to assistive technology")
- Given a modal menu with `getPersistentElements`, when Shift+Tab is pressed twice, then focus goes first to the menu button and then to the persistent element the prop returned. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-modal-persistent-elements/test-browser.ts`: "shift tab moves focus from modal menu to persistent disclosure", "keeps persistent elements the prop returns")
- Given a caller that returns different persistent elements over time and sets its own tree-snapshot key, when a menu item adds a new persistent element, then it loses `inert` and becomes reachable by Shift+Tab, so the menu carries the caller's key along instead of replacing it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-modal-persistent-elements/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/menu-modal-persistent-elements/test.ts`: "caller's tree snapshot key still refreshes persistent elements")
- Given an open modal menu whose disclosure is swapped for a different element, when the swap happens, then the new disclosure joins the modal context, the old one becomes inert, and Chromium's accessibility tree reports the menu's name flipping from the old label to the new one. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-modal-persistent-elements/test-chrome.ts`: "swapping the disclosure keeps the menu named"; `app/src/sandbox/menu-modal-persistent-elements/test.ts`: "swapping the disclosure moves it into the modal context")
- Given a focused menu item whose DOM node is replaced while the popup is still positioning, when the replacement mounts, then it carries `data-active-item` and takes focus, and the deferred scroll lands once positioning finishes. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-placing-pass/test-browser.ts`: "presents a focused item after its node is replaced"; `app/src/sandbox/menu-placing-pass/test.ts`: "restores focus after a focused item is replaced")
- Given a focused menu item that is blurred to the body before being replaced, when the replacement mounts, then it becomes the active item but does not take focus, and no scroll happens. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-placing-pass/test-browser.ts`: "abandons a replaced item after focus leaves"; `app/src/sandbox/menu-placing-pass/test.ts`: "leaves focus outside after a focused item is replaced")
- Given an item that was blurred and then refocused before being replaced, when the replacement mounts, then it takes focus and the scroll lands. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-placing-pass/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/menu-placing-pass/test.ts`: "restores focus when a refocused item is replaced")
- Given a popup whose custom `updatePosition` is still running, when the menu opens, then the popup is marked `data-placing`, focus stays on the button rather than entering the menu, and a programmatic move to the last item does not scroll the document; once positioning completes, `data-placing` is removed and the held-back scroll lands. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-placing-pass/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/menu-placing-pass/test.ts`: "keeps the popup unplaced while a custom updatePosition is still working")
- Given a custom `updatePosition` that throws after the supplied default already positioned the popup, when it fails, then `data-placing` is removed and the deferred scroll lands, because the popup is somewhere real. Browser-only, because the rejection also surfaces as an unhandled rejection that would fail a Vitest run. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-placing-pass/test-browser.ts`: "publishes the popup as placed when a custom updatePosition fails after positioning it")
- Given a custom `updatePosition` that throws before positioning anything, when it fails, then the popup keeps `data-placing` and never takes focus. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-placing-pass/test-browser.ts`: "keeps the popup unplaced when a custom updatePosition fails before positioning it")
- Given an already open popup that re-anchors itself, when the new positioning pass starts, then `data-placing` comes back and a move to the last item defers its document scroll until the pass finishes. Browser-only, because happy-dom stubs `scrollIntoView`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-placing-pass/test-browser.ts`: "keeps the popup unplaced while an open popup repositions itself")
- Given a popup that mounts only after its store is already open, so no `Popover` was mounted to publish the show transition, when it mounts, then it still carries `data-placing` and focus stays on the trigger until the pass finishes. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-placing-pass/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/menu-placing-pass/test.ts`: "keeps focus out of a popup that mounts after its store is open")
- Given a menu inside a dialog, when the menu is toggled closed by its button, then focus returns to the menu button and the dialog stays open. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-dialog-close/test-browser.ts`: "open/close menu by clicking on menu button", "menu button receives focus after menu closes")
- Given a non-interactive text node that was clicked before a dialog is opened programmatically by keyboard shortcut, when the dialog closes, then focus returns to the original disclosure, because a non-focusable mousedown target is filtered out and does not hijack the disclosure. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-dialog-close/test-browser.ts`: "clicking non-interactive element before programmatic open does not hijack disclosure")
- Given rendered items whose focus element is unchanged, when the items are refreshed, then the items component re-renders but the menu component does not. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-initial-focus-render/test-browser.ts`: "does not re-render when rendered items keep the same focus element")

- Given an open menu, when a menu item receives focus, then it becomes the active item; a disabled item cannot be focused. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/menu/menu.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/menu/menu.test.tsx`: "should be possible focus a menu item, so that it becomes active", "should not be possible to focus a menu item which is disabled")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given controlled menu checkbox values, when items are clicked, then only the parent's accepted values are applied and the change callback reports the controlled result; clicking an already-selected item clears it to an empty array. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-values-interactions/test.ts`: "interact with checkboxControlled items")
- Given uncontrolled menu checkbox values, when items are clicked, then the DOM state accumulates in DOM order while the callback reports them in click order, and clicking again removes them. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-values-interactions/test.ts`: "interact with checkboxUncontrolled items")
- Given checkbox values owned by a parent store, when items are clicked, then the parent's value wins and the callback reports it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-values-interactions/test.ts`: "interact with checkboxParent items")
- Given controlled radio values, when a click would not change the controlled value, then no change callback fires at all; only a click that the controller accepts produces a callback. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-values-interactions/test.ts`: "interact with radioControlled items", "interact with radioParent items")
- Given uncontrolled radio values, when items are clicked, then the value follows each click, and clicking a disabled (hidden-query-only) item changes nothing and fires no callback. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-values-interactions/test.ts`: "interact with radioUncontrolled items")
- Given the values example at first render, when the state is read, then the defaults are exactly `{checkboxControlled: ["Banana"], checkboxParent: ["Orange"], checkboxUncontrolled: ["Banana","Grape"], radioControlled: "Banana", radioParent: "Orange", radioUncontrolled: "Banana"}`, both in the DOM and in the change callback. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-values-interactions/test.ts`: "default values")
- Given a controlled radio value reset from outside the menu, when the reset button is clicked, then the external value becomes empty and reopening the menu shows the item unchecked with its check icon gone. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-values-interactions/test.ts`: "reset radioControlled externally")
- Given a menu with disabled items, when ArrowDown walks the list, then disabled items are skipped, and typeahead also skips them. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-values-interactions/test.ts`: "navigate with keyboard ignoring disabled items")
- Given a menu button whose label reflects checkbox state, when an item is unchecked, then the button's accessible name changes. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-checkbox-interactions/test.ts`: "update menu button label on menu item check")
- Given sixty independent menu stores on one page, when the last button is clicked, then only that menu opens and its items render. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-maximum-update-depth/test.ts`: "renders and independently opens sixty menu stores")
- Given many menus on a page, when the React island hydrates, then no "Maximum update depth exceeded" error (or its minified react.dev/errors/185 form) is logged, an `alwaysVisible` menu registers its three items even though its store is closed, and a closed menu still renders its items once opened. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-3214/test-chrome.ts`: "renders many menus without exceeding React's update depth")

- Given the `close` function exposed on the `Menu` and `Menu.Item` slots, when it is called, then the menu closes. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/menu/menu.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/menu/menu.test.tsx`: "should be possible to manually close the Menu using the exposed close function")
- Given a menu button, when `.click()` is invoked programmatically, then the menu opens. [react only] (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/menu/menu.test.tsx`: "should be possible to open a menu programmatically via .click()")
- Given a wrapping `OpenClosed` provider, when it reports open or closed, then `MenuItems` is always open or always closed accordingly, and the state is readable from inside. [vue only] (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/menu/menu.test.tsx`: "should always open the MenuItems because of a wrapping OpenClosed component", "should always close the MenuItems because of a wrapping OpenClosed component", "should be possible to read the OpenClosed state")

### Dismissal and layering

- Given a modal menu, when it opens, then the menu owns only its own items: it contains no `button`, the fallback "Dismiss popup" button is rendered next to the menu rather than inside it, and Chromium's accessibility tree reports the menu's children as exactly three `menuitem`s. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-4270/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/menu-4270/test.ts`: "modal menu exposes only its items to assistive technology")
- Given a modal menu inside a dialog composition, when Escape is pressed with focus on the menu's disclosure, then only the menu closes and the modal dialog stays open even after 300ms. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-modal-composition/test-chrome.ts`: "keeps the modal open when Escape closes a menu from its disclosure")
- Given a modal dialog opened from a menu item, when the dialog is open, then the dialog takes focus, the parent menu is no longer exposed to assistive technology, and whether the parent menu is still visually present depends on `hideOnClick`. This is asserted for eleven menu-item shapes: Nested, Sibling, Sibling (hideOnClick), Slot, Slot - Nested, Slot - Sibling, Slot - Sibling (hideOnClick), Slot (bubblesVirtually), Slot (bubblesVirtually) - Nested, Slot (bubblesVirtually) - Sibling, Slot (bubblesVirtually) - Sibling (hideOnClick), each via mouse and via keyboard. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-modal-composition/test-chrome.ts`: "interact with modal by clicking on the Nested menu item with a mouse" and its 21 siblings)
- Given a modal dialog opened from a menu, when a tooltip anchor inside it is hovered or tabbed to, then the tooltip shows; Escape hides the tooltip without closing the modal. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-modal-composition/test-chrome.ts`: the "interact with modal by clicking on the ... menu item" matrix)
- Given a menu opened inside a modal dialog with a submenu, when the submenu item is hovered or reached with ArrowRight, then the submenu opens; clicking the modal body closes the menu but keeps the modal; clicking outside the modal closes it and reveals the parent menu again with the originating item focused. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-modal-composition/test-chrome.ts`: the same matrix)
- Given a menu whose item opens a modal from inside a submenu, when the dialog closes with Escape, then both the parent menu and the submenu become visible again unless `hideOnClick` closed them. Chromium only, across three prefixes (plain, Slot, Slot (bubblesVirtually)) times four item kinds. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-modal-composition/test-chrome.ts`: "interact with modal by clicking on the Nested menu item" and its 11 siblings)
- Given a menu opened in a popup browser window, when Escape is pressed, the outside is clicked, or an item is clicked, then the menu closes and, on item click, focus returns to the trigger in that window. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-4904/test-chrome.ts`: "menu in popup window closes on Escape", "menu in popup window closes on click outside", "menu in popup window restores focus to trigger on close")
- Given a menu with a `Motion`-driven leave animation, when it closes by click, Enter, Space, Escape, or an outside click, then focus returns to the trigger (or not, for the outside click) while the menu is still present, and it unmounts only after the animation ends. The suite runs under jsdom rather than happy-dom, recorded as a workaround for happy-dom rejecting `Animation.cancel()`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-motion-transitions/test.ts`: "show/hide on click", "show/hide on enter", "show/hide on space", "hide on esc", "hide on click outside")
- Given a menu with Motion transitions in Chromium at a 480x480 viewport, when it opens and ArrowDown focuses the first item, then the item's computed `opacity` is 1 and the menu is positioned below its button. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-motion-transitions/test-chrome.ts`: "show/hide with click")
- Given a menu with a tooltip on its button, in five variants (default, portal, modal, unmount portal, unmount modal), when the button is hovered, then the tooltip shows, and hovering away hides it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-tooltip-variants/test.ts`: "show/hide tooltip on hover")
- Given a visible tooltip on a menu button, when the button is clicked, then the menu opens with focus, and the tooltip is removed. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-tooltip-variants/test.ts`: "hide tooltip by clicking on menu button")
- Given an open menu whose button is hovered again, when the pointer re-enters without ever leaving, then the tooltip does not come back. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-tooltip-variants/test.ts`: "do not show tooltip on hover after clicking on menu button")
- Given an open menu, when the pointer leaves the button and comes back, then the tooltip shows again for the non-modal variants but stays hidden for the modal ones. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-tooltip-variants/test.ts`: "but show tooltip on hover after clicking on menu button and then hovering outside unless it's modal")
- Given an open menu, when Escape closes it, then the tooltip is shown again. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-tooltip-variants/test.ts`: "show tooltip again after closing menu with esc")
- Given a non-modal menu closed and reopened, when the cycle repeats, then the tooltip is hidden each time the menu opens. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-tooltip-variants/test.ts`: "tooltip closes when re-opening the menu")
- Given a tooltip with a 200ms timeout, when the menu button is clicked before the tooltip appears, then the tooltip never appears even after the timeout elapses and even after a pointer move within the anchor; it only appears after the pointer leaves and re-enters. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-tooltip-variants/test.ts`: "do not show tooltip with timeout after clicking on menu button before the tooltip is shown")
- Given a menu button composed from `VisuallyHidden`, `TooltipAnchor`, and `MenuButton`, when inspected and hovered, then the visually hidden span carries the accessible name, the tooltip shows on hover and hides on leave, and clicking opens the menu with focus while removing the tooltip. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-tooltip-variants/test.ts`: "compose VisuallyHidden, TooltipAnchor, and MenuButton")

### Positioning

- Given a menu whose button is the anchor, when the menu opens, then the menu's portal wrapper is the button's immediate next sibling in the DOM. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-core-interactions/test.ts`: "https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/issues/3342")
- Given a vertical menubar, when a menu opens, then it is placed beside its menubar item (the popover's left edge is at or past the item's right edge). Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-7410/test-chrome.ts`: "menus open beside their vertical menubar item")
- Given a right-to-left vertical menubar with an explicit placement, when a menu opens, then the explicit placement wins and the popover sits to the left of its item. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-7410/test-chrome.ts`: "an explicit placement wins in a right-to-left menubar")
- Given a submenu in a vertical menubar, when it opens, then it follows its parent menu rather than the menubar, and ArrowLeft walks back one level at a time. Chromium only for the geometry. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-7410/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/menubar-7410/test.ts`: "submenus keep following their parent menu")
- Given a slide-navigation menu, when a submenu item is clicked, then the wrapper's `scrollLeft` advances by exactly one `clientWidth` per level, and a "Back to parent menu" item scrolls it back and hides the submenu. Chromium and WebKit only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-slide-navigation/test-chrome-safari.ts`: "show/hide with click")
- Given a slide-navigation menu driven by keyboard, when typeahead plus Enter, ArrowRight, and Space are used, then the wrapper scroll advances and retreats one pane at a time and the "Back to parent menu" item is focused on arrival. Chromium and WebKit only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-slide-navigation/test-chrome-safari.ts`: "show/hide with keyboard")
- Given a slide-navigation menu two levels deep, when a horizontal wheel scroll of -200 is applied, then one pane closes per wheel and the parent item is refocused. WebKit only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-slide-navigation/test-safari.ts`: "hide with wheel")

### Animation and presence

- Given a `static` prop on `Menu.Items`, when the menu is closed, then the items are still rendered; the `unmount` strategy can be swapped for a different one. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/menu/menu.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/menu/menu.test.tsx`: "should be possible to always render the Menu.Items if we provide it a `static` prop", "should be possible to always render the MenuItems if we provide it a `static` prop", "should be possible to use a different render strategy for the Menu.Items", "should be possible to use a different render strategy for the MenuItems")
- Given `Menu.Items` wrapped in a `Transition` or a `Transition.Child`, when the menu toggles, then the transition drives the items and inherits the menu's state. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/menu/menu.test.tsx`: "should be possible to wrap the Menu.Items with a Transition component", "should be possible to wrap the Menu.Items with a Transition.Child component"; `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/menu/menu.test.tsx`: "should be possible to render a TransitionChild that inherits state from the Menu")
- Given the `transition` prop, when the menu closes, then the closing transition runs and the menu ends up closed. [react only] (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/menu/menu.test.tsx`: "should be possible to close the Menu when using the `transition` prop")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a menu with a combobox inside (a dialog-flavored menu), when the button is clicked, then the dialog is visible, the dialog element itself does not take focus, the combobox does, and no option is active; clicking the button again closes it and returns focus. Asserted for both the Provider and the Store composition. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-combobox-interactions/test.ts`: "show/hide on click")
- Given the same combobox menu opened by Enter, Space, ArrowDown, or ArrowUp, when it opens, then the combobox takes focus and the first (or, for ArrowUp, the last) option becomes active; Shift+Tab returns to the button and pressing the same key again closes it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-combobox-interactions/test.ts`: "show/hide on enter", "show/hide on space", "show on arrow down", "show on arrow up")
- Given a combobox menu, when characters are typed, then the option list filters progressively and the active option follows the best match; Escape closes it and reopening resets the input value to empty. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-combobox-interactions/test.ts`: "type on combobox")
- Given a combobox menu with a typed query, when Backspace is pressed, then the query shortens one character at a time and the active option follows back up to the unfiltered first option. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-combobox-interactions/test.ts`: "backspace on combobox")
- Given a combobox menu, when ArrowDown walks the list and then a typeahead query jumps to a match, then subsequent ArrowDowns continue from the match; Escape then ArrowDown restarts from the first option. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-combobox-interactions/test.ts`: "move through items with keyboard")
- Given a combobox menu, when an option is reached by ArrowDown, then it carries `data-focus-visible`; when reached by hover, it does not; a subsequent ArrowUp restores `data-focus-visible`. DOM focus stays on the combobox input throughout. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-combobox-interactions/test.ts`: "move through items with mouse and keyboard")
- Given a combobox menu with `autoSelect`, when a query is typed in a real browser, then the first matching option gets `data-active-item`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-combobox-interactions/test-browser.ts`: "auto select first option with Provider", "auto select first option with Store")
- Given a combobox menu opened and the page then scrolled to the bottom, when a click outside closes it, then the trigger is not scrolled back into the viewport. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-combobox-interactions/test-browser.ts`: "https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/issues/4324")
- Given a search-menu (combobox in a dialog) example, when the button is clicked or activated with Enter, then the dialog opens with the search combobox focused, and Escape returns focus to the button. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-nested-search-interactions/test.ts`: "open/hide menu", "open/hide menu with keyboard")
- Given a search menu, when a query is typed, then the matching option becomes active with `data-active-item="true"` and ArrowDown walks the filtered results in order. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-nested-search-interactions/test.ts`: "filter actions")
- Given a search menu with a query, when it is closed by an outside click and reopened, then the query is reset to empty. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-nested-search-interactions/test.ts`: "reset filter on hide")
- Given a search submenu with `blurOnHoverEnd={false}`, when its parent option is hovered, then `aria-expanded` starts `"false"` and becomes `"true"` once the submenu appears, and moving the pointer away keeps the option active and the submenu open; ArrowRight moves into the submenu's own combobox with its first option active, ArrowLeft closes it and restores `aria-expanded="false"`, and Escape from inside closes the whole stack. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-nested-search-interactions/test.ts`: "open/hide with search submenu")
- Given an open search submenu, when Tab is pressed, then focus moves to the submenu's combobox without activating an option, and Shift+Tab returns to the parent option while the submenu stays open. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-nested-search-interactions/test.ts`: "tab in/out search menu")
- Given a search menu that sets a block type, when a `menuitemradio` is activated, then `aria-checked` becomes `"true"`, the menu closes, and the page reflects the new block type; reopening and typing shows the previously selected option as checked and the new one as not checked. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-nested-search-interactions/test.ts`: "set block type")
- Given a menu containing dialogs, when items and buttons are activated, then Tab cycles through the menu's own items including the "Dismiss popup" fallback, the create-list dialog opens with its dismiss button focused, submitting an empty form shows a validation message that clears once a character is typed, and submitting a valid name closes the dialog, returns to the menu with the new `menuitemcheckbox` focused, and updates the trigger's label count. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-dialog-transitions/test-chrome.ts`: "interact with menu", "show/hide create list dialog", "create list")
- Given nested dialogs opened from a menu, when they are opened and closed ten times in a row, then each cycle focuses the dialog's dismiss button and returns focus to the opening button. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-dialog-transitions/test-chrome.ts`: "show/hide manage lists dialog", "show/hide information dialog", "repeatedly showing/hiding manage lists dialog", "repeatedly showing/hiding information dialog")

## menubar

### Roles and attributes

- Given a composite menubar, when rendered, then it has `role="menubar"` and `aria-orientation="horizontal"` by default, `aria-orientation="vertical"` when configured vertical, and no `aria-orientation` at all when both orientations are allowed. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-composite-orientation/test-chrome.ts`: "renders role and orientation attributes for composite menubars")
- Given `composite={false}`, when the menubar renders, then it has neither a `role` nor an `aria-orientation` attribute and is not matched by a `menubar` role query. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-composite-orientation/test-chrome.ts`: "omits menubar role and orientation when composite is false")
- Given a menubar item with an open menu, when inspected, then it has `aria-expanded="true"`, and `"false"` once the menu closes. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-interactions/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/menubar-interactions/test.ts`: "ArrowDown follows vertical RTL menubar order from the menu container"; `app/src/sandbox/menubar-7410/test.ts`: "arrow keys open and close the menus of a vertical menubar")

### Keyboard

- Given a menubar item, when Enter or Space activates it, then its menu opens with the first item focused; pressing the key again on that item closes the menu and returns focus to the menubar item. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-interactions/test.ts`: "show/hide on enter", "show/hide on space")
- Given an open menubar menu, when Shift+Tab moves focus back to the menubar item, then the menu stays open and pressing Enter or Space from there closes it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-interactions/test.ts`: "show/hide on enter", "show/hide on space")
- Given a horizontal menubar with an open menu, when ArrowRight or ArrowLeft is pressed, then the adjacent menubar item takes focus, its menu opens, and the previous menu closes. Inside a menu, ArrowUp and ArrowDown move the active item, and ArrowRight on a submenu button opens the submenu while ArrowLeft closes it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-interactions/test.ts`: "show/hide on key down")
- Given a vertical menubar, when ArrowRight opens a menu from a menubar item, then ArrowDown/ArrowUp move within the menu and ArrowLeft returns to the menubar item and closes the menu; ArrowDown/ArrowUp on a menubar item then move between menubar items without opening their menus. Chromium only for the geometry half. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-7410/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/menubar-7410/test.ts`: "arrow keys open and close the menus of a vertical menubar")
- Given a right-to-left vertical menubar, when ArrowLeft is pressed on a menubar item, then its menu opens and ArrowRight closes it, mirroring the LTR direction. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-7410/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/menubar-7410/test.ts`: "an explicit placement wins in a right-to-left menubar")
- Given typeahead started on a menubar item whose menu is open, when characters are typed after Shift+Tab put focus back on the item, then typeahead continues to target items inside the menu. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-interactions/test.ts`: "typeahead from menu button continues after focus moves to menu")
- Given an open submenu in a menubar, when Escape is pressed, then the whole stack closes and focus returns to the menubar item; ArrowRight from there moves to the next menubar item without opening its menu, and after Escape hovering another item no longer opens its menu. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-interactions/test.ts`: "hide on escape")
- Given a menubar with an open menu, when ArrowRight or ArrowLeft is pressed from the menu container, from a menu item, or from a text field at its caret edge, then the menubar traverses to the adjacent item, the old menu closes, and the new popup (a `menu` or a `dialog` depending on the item) opens. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-interactions/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/menubar-interactions/test.ts`: "ArrowRight traverses the menubar from menu", "ArrowRight traverses the menubar from item", "ArrowRight traverses the menubar from input edge", and the three ArrowLeft cases)
- Given a vertical right-to-left menubar, when ArrowDown or ArrowUp is pressed from the menu container or from a horizontal menu item, then the next or previous menubar item takes focus, its menu opens with `aria-expanded="true"`, and the previous menu is hidden. Chromium only for the browser copy. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-interactions/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/menubar-interactions/test.ts`: "ArrowDown follows vertical RTL menubar order from the menu container", "ArrowUp follows vertical RTL menubar order from the menu container", "ArrowDown follows vertical RTL menubar order from the horizontal menu item", "ArrowUp follows vertical RTL menubar order from the horizontal menu item")
- Given a reopened submenu, when Shift+Tab is pressed, then focus returns to the parent menu with the submenu button as active item while both menus stay visible, and a following ArrowDown closes the submenu and moves to the next parent item. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-interactions/test-browser.ts`: "re-open submenu and shift-tab back to the parent menu")
- Given a hover-driven navigation menubar, when Tab walks the page, then it steps through every menubar item and every item of the currently open menu in order, opening each menubar item's menu as it arrives and closing the previous one; Shift+Tab reverses it. WebKit needs `Alt+Tab` instead of `Tab`, which the test encodes. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-navigation/test-browser.ts`: "show menus by tabbing through items")
- Given a hover-driven navigation menubar, when ArrowRight walks the menubar, then each item takes focus and opens its menu while the previous closes; the last item has no menu. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-navigation/test-browser.ts`: "show menus by focusing on items")
- Given a menubar menu opened by click, when ArrowDown is pressed repeatedly, then the items take focus in order. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-navigation/test-browser.ts`: "moving between menu items with arrow keys")
- Given a menu store shared through a menubar provider, when arrowing into the menu records a move, then navigating away to another menubar item unmounts the menu and returning with ArrowRight re-opens it with focus on the menubar item rather than replaying the stale container-focus request. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-navigation/test-browser.ts`: "keeps focus on the menu item when the shared menu is mounted again")

### Pointer

- Given a menubar item, when it is clicked, then its menu opens and the menu element takes focus with no item active; clicking an item closes the menu and returns focus to the menubar item; clicking the menubar item twice closes it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-interactions/test.ts`: "show/hide on click")
- Given a closed menubar, when an item is merely hovered, then its menu does not open; but once one menu is open, hovering another menubar item switches to that menu. Hovering a submenu item then returning to a sibling menubar item switches back. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-interactions/test.ts`: "show/hide on hover")
- Given a hover-driven navigation menubar, when items are hovered, then their menus open and close without moving DOM focus away from `body`, and hovering outside closes the open menu. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-navigation/test-browser.ts`: "show menus by hovering over items without moving focus")
- Given a hover-driven navigation menubar, when a submenu item is hovered and then a sibling menubar item, then focus is not moved onto the item, the previous menu closes, and the new one opens; hovering outside for 750ms closes it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-navigation/test-browser.ts`: "show menus by hovering over items and subitems")
- Given a menubar menu reached by hovering a submenu item, when ArrowRight is pressed, then the current menu stays open and no sibling menubar item is focused or opened. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-navigation/test-browser.ts`: "moving between menus with arrow keys after hovering over subitems")
- Given menu items that are links, when one is clicked, then the URL hash changes and the menu stays open; clicking another navigates and closes the first menu; arrowing back and pressing Enter navigates again and focuses the first submenu item (except on Firefox, where the focus assertion is skipped); Escape closes the menu and focuses the menubar item, and Enter from there does not reopen it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menubar-navigation/test-browser.ts`: "click on menuitem links")

## context-menu

### Keyboard

- Given an open context menu with focus on the menu element, when ArrowDown is pressed, then the first item takes focus, a second ArrowDown the next, Home returns to the first, and End jumps to the last. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-context-interactions/test.ts`: "navigate through context menu with keyboard")

### Pointer

- Given a context-menu target, when it is right-clicked, then the menu opens and takes focus; right-clicking again keeps it open; Escape closes it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-context-interactions/test.ts`: "show context menu and hide it with escape")
- Given an open context menu, when the page outside is clicked, then it closes. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-context-interactions/test.ts`: "show context menu and hide it by clicking outside")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given a context menu whose modal context names the focused control as a fallback disclosure, when it opens, then that captured control does not join the modal context (it cannot be assumed to close the menu), the fallback "Dismiss popup" button renders next to the menu rather than inside it, the menu contains no `button`, and Chromium's accessibility tree reports the menu's children as `menuitem, menuitem, menuitem, separator, menuitem, menuitem` with the dismiss button still exposed. The test comment records that Safari reaches the capture through a different branch because it leaves `BODY` as the active element for a native button with no explicit tabindex. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/menu-context-interactions/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/menu-context-interactions/test.ts`: "context menu keeps a dismiss button outside the menu")

## composite

### Roles and attributes

- Given a composite item that is the active item, when inspected, then it carries `data-active-item`, and `data-focus-visible="true"` only when the move came from the keyboard. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-navigation/test.ts`: "navigates a non-looping composite", "moves focus-visible state to the next item")
- Given a virtual-focus composite with no active item, when the dialog containing it opens, then the composite element has no `aria-activedescendant` and no option has `data-active-item`; ArrowDown then sets both. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-dialog-virtual-focus/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-dialog-virtual-focus/test.ts`: "opens the dialog without highlighting an option")
- Given a grid whose rows carry `aria-posinset`, when cells render, then each cell derives `aria-posinset` from its row-level value (21, 22, 23, 24) and `aria-setsize="100"`. Chromium only for the browser copy. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-row-6334/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-row-6334/test.ts`: "cells compute their position from row-level aria-posinset")
- Given an item disabled only accessibly (`accessibleWhenDisabled`), when inspected, then it has `aria-disabled="true"`, no `disabled` attribute, and `data-truly-disabled="false"`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-item-tabbable/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-item-tabbable/test.ts`: "moves to an accessible disabled item inherited through composition", "moves to an accessible disabled item resolved below it")
- Given a truly disabled item, when inspected, then it has the `disabled` attribute. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-item-tabbable/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-item-tabbable/test.ts`: "skips a disabled item resolved below it")

### Keyboard

- Given a non-looping composite, when Tab enters it, then the active item takes focus; ArrowDown/ArrowUp and ArrowRight/ArrowLeft move the active item and stop at the ends instead of wrapping. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-navigation/test.ts`: "navigates a non-looping composite")
- Given a right-to-left composite with no active item, when it is focused and ArrowLeft is pressed, then the first item in reading order takes focus and a second ArrowLeft advances; when ArrowRight is pressed first instead, then the last item takes focus and a second ArrowRight moves back inward. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-6299/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-6299/test.ts`: "enters an RTL composite from the composite element with ArrowLeft", "enters an RTL composite from the composite element with ArrowRight")
- Given a grid without focus shifting, when ArrowDown, ArrowRight and ArrowUp are pressed, then movement stays within the column or row and ArrowUp from a short row lands in the same column of the row above (`0A1` to `0B1` to `0B2` to `0C2` to `0C3` to `0A3` to `0C3`). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-navigation/test.ts`: "navigates a grid without focus shifting")
- Given a grid with focus shifting, when the same keys are pressed across uneven rows, then the active cell shifts to the nearest cell in the target row (`1A1` to `1B1` to `1B2` to `1C2` to `1C3` to `1B2` to `1A2` to `1A3` to `1B2` to `1C2`). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-navigation/test.ts`: "navigates a grid with focus shifting")
- Given a composite where an arrow key is pressed with Alt held, when focus moves, then the new item gets `data-focus-visible="true"` even though the previous interaction was a pointer click. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-navigation/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-navigation/test.ts`: "moves focus-visible with an Alt-modified navigation key")
- Given the last item of a non-looping composite, when Alt+ArrowDown is pressed so nothing moves and no focus event fires, then the item itself still gains `data-focus-visible="true"` from its own keydown handling. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-navigation/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-navigation/test.ts`: "shows focus-visible on the item when an Alt-modified navigation key doesn't move focus")
- Given a grid cell reached by click, when Ctrl+Home is pressed, then the first cell takes focus with `data-focus-visible="true"`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-navigation/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-navigation/test.ts`: "moves focus-visible with Ctrl+Home on a grid")
- Given a modified key that is not a navigation key (Ctrl+C), when it is pressed after a pointer click, then no `data-focus-visible` appears and the global focus modality stays pointer, which is observable on the next element to receive focus. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-navigation/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-navigation/test.ts`: "keeps pointer modality on a modified non-navigation key")
- Given the deprecated focus-order prop that includes the composite element, when ArrowRight moves past the last item, then the composite element itself takes focus. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-navigation/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-navigation/test.ts`: "updates focus order through the deprecated prop")
- Given a composite inside a same-origin iframe whose document is the scroller, when PageDown is pressed, then paging uses the iframe's own 220px viewport (landing on Item 7 with 50px items) rather than the much taller outer page viewport. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-iframe-6312/test-browser.ts`: "PageDown pages by the iframe's own scroller, not the outer page")
- Given two composites on one page, when a typeahead buffer is built in the first and a single character typed in the second immediately afterwards, then the second composite matches on that character alone, so the typeahead buffer is per-instance rather than global. The jsdom copy uses fake timers to keep the first buffer alive; the browser copy relies on back-to-back keypresses inside the 500ms cleanup window. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-typeahead-buffer/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-typeahead-buffer/test.ts`: "keeps typeahead characters scoped to each composite instance")
- Given an item accessibly disabled (through composition, resolved below it, or with an active `Focusable` below it), when ArrowRight moves onto it, then it takes focus. Given an item truly disabled, disabled with an inactive `Focusable`, disabled with an inactive `Focusable` below it, directly disabled with an inactive accessible `Focusable`, or inherited-disabled with an inactive accessible `Focusable`, then ArrowRight skips it. Chromium only for the browser copy. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-item-tabbable/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-item-tabbable/test.ts`: "moves to an accessible disabled item inherited through composition", "moves to an accessible disabled item resolved below it", "moves to an accessible disabled item with an active Focusable below it", "skips a disabled item resolved below it", "skips a disabled item with an inactive Focusable", "skips a disabled item with an inactive Focusable below it", "skips a directly disabled item with an inactive accessible Focusable", "skips an inherited disabled item with an inactive accessible Focusable")
- Given a `CompositeItem` wrapped in a `MenuProvider`, when ArrowRight is pressed from the preceding sibling, then it is reached, because it registers in the outer composite store rather than the menu's own; the same holds after ArrowDown moves to the second row. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-menu-3768/test-browser.ts`: "composite items merged with menu buttons are reachable via arrow keys")

- Given `getTextValue`, the helper that backs typeahead, when it reads an element, then it returns the element's text; it strips out emojis, hidden elements, `aria-hidden` elements and `role="img"` elements; it prefers the element's own `aria-label` (even when the element also has content); and it resolves `aria-labelledby`, reading either the referenced element's `aria-label` or its contents, including when several ids are referenced. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/get-text-value.test.ts`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/utils/get-text-value.test.ts`: "should be possible to get the text value from an element", "should strip out emojis when receiving the text from the element", "should strip out hidden elements", "should strip out aria-hidden elements", "should strip out role="img" elements", "should be possible to get the text value from the aria-label", "should be possible to get the text value from the aria-label (even if there is content)", "should be possible to get the text value from the element referenced by aria-labelledby (using `aria-label`)", "should be possible to get the text value from the element referenced by aria-labelledby (using its contents)", "should be possible to get the text value from the element referenced by aria-labelledby (using `aria-label`, multiple)", "should be possible to get the text value from the element referenced by aria-labelledby (using its contents, multiple)")

### Pointer

- Given a toolbar with virtual focus, when an item is hovered, then the events fire in exactly this order: `mouseenter` on the toolbar (target the item), `mouseenter` on the item, `focus` on the toolbar (target toolbar), `focus` on the item (relatedTarget toolbar), `focus` on the toolbar (target the item, relatedTarget toolbar); afterwards the toolbar and the item both carry `data-focus-visible` and the item carries `data-active-item`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-hover-virtual-focus-events/test.ts`: "dispatches hover and virtual focus events in order")
- Given a hovered item in a virtual-focus toolbar, when ArrowLeft is pressed, then the events are keydown on the item, keydown on the toolbar, blur on the item (relatedTarget the new item), blur on the toolbar, focus on the new item, focus on the toolbar, keyup on the new item, keyup on the toolbar, and `data-focus-visible` plus `data-active-item` move to the new item. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-hover-virtual-focus-events/test.ts`: "dispatches hover and virtual focus events in order")
- Given a keyboard-activated item, when a different item is hovered, then blur events fire for the old item and only `mouseenter` for the new one, and the new item gets `data-active-item` without `data-focus-visible`; a following ArrowRight then emits the focus pair before the keydown pair and restores `data-focus-visible`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-hover-virtual-focus-events/test.ts`: "dispatches hover and virtual focus events in order")
- Given a virtual-focus toolbar, when an item is clicked, then the toolbar loses `data-focus-visible`, the clicked item gains `data-active-item` without `data-focus-visible`, and only blur/focus pairs fire. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-hover-virtual-focus-events/test.ts`: "dispatches hover and virtual focus events in order")
- Given a virtual-focus toolbar entered by Tab, when the events are logged, then the order is focus on the toolbar, focus on the first item (relatedTarget toolbar), focus on the toolbar (target the item), keyup pair, keydown pair, blur pair on the item, and blur on the toolbar targeting itself. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-virtual-focus-events/test.ts`: "dispatches virtual focus events in order")
- Given a virtual-focus toolbar, when an item is clicked from outside the toolbar, then focus fires on the item, then on the toolbar with target toolbar and relatedTarget the item, then on the toolbar with target the item; clicking a second item fires blur on the old item and the toolbar followed by focus on the new item and the toolbar. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-virtual-focus-events/test.ts`: "dispatches virtual focus events in order")

### Focus management

- Given composite items focused with `preventScroll`, when keyboard navigation reaches an item below the fold, then the composite scrolls the document to reveal it, verified by `window.scrollY` increasing rather than by a scrollable wrapper. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-navigation/test-browser.ts`: "scrolls the page to reveal the item reached with the keyboard")
- Given an inline virtual-focus composite whose active item is below the fold, when the composite element is focused without scrolling, then DOM focus stays on the composite element but the page scrolls to bring the active item into view. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-page-scroll/test-browser.ts`: "scrolls the page to present the active item of an inline composite")
- Given an inline composite scrolled to its last item, when Home is pressed, then the first item becomes the active item and the page scrolls to reveal it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-page-scroll/test-browser.ts`: "scrolls the page while navigating an inline composite")
- Given `move(null)` targeting a composite element that cannot take focus, when it runs, then the page is not scrolled at all and no document scroll event fires. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-page-scroll/test-browser.ts`: "does not scroll to a composite that cannot take focus")
- Given a composite with `virtualFocus` and a non-focusable composite element, when arrow keys move the active item, then focus is not redirected to the composite element, each item gets `data-focus-visible="true"` in turn, and a single console warning is emitted: "A composite widget with `virtualFocus` enabled requires a focusable composite element. Set the `focusable` prop to `true` or the `virtualFocus` option to `false`." (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-item-tabbable/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-item-tabbable/test.ts`: "does not redirect focus to a non-focusable virtual focus owner")
- Given a move that has no item to land on, when a late item mounts after focus has already left the composite, then the late item is not focused and focus stays where the user put it. This holds for a roving-tabindex composite and for a virtual-focus one. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-late-item-focus/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-late-item-focus/test.ts`: "does not refocus a late item after focus leaves the composite", "does not refocus a late item after focus leaves a virtual focus composite")
- Given two rapid unresolved moves, when the late items mount with focus still inside the composite, then only the latest requested item takes focus. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-late-item-focus/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-late-item-focus/test.ts`: "only focuses the latest item after rapid unresolved moves")
- Given a generic (unresolved) item that mounts while focus is outside, when it appears, then the composite's scroll position stays at 0, so an unresolved item is not presented. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-late-item-focus/test-browser.ts`: "does not present an unresolved generic item")
- Given a rendered generic item marked `autoFocus`, when the composite element is focused, then that item becomes the active item, the composite scrolls to it, and the composite element keeps DOM focus. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-late-item-focus/test-browser.ts`: "presents a rendered generic autofocus item")
- Given a pending move that targeted an item, when the composite is later hidden and shown, then the move is not redirected to the composite element; given a pending move that targeted the composite, it is not redirected to an item. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-late-item-focus/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-late-item-focus/test.ts`: "does not redirect a pending item move to the composite", "does not redirect a pending composite move to an item")
- Given a pending move whose active id has since cycled to something else and back, when the composite reappears, then the stale move is not replayed, for both the composite target and the item target. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-late-item-focus/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-late-item-focus/test.ts`: "does not replay a pending composite move after the active id cycles", "does not replay a pending item move after the active id cycles")
- Given a move queued before the composite has ever mounted, when the composite first mounts, then it is not redirected: an item move does not become a composite move, a composite move does not become an item move, and the same holds for a derived composite such as a tab list. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-late-item-focus/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-late-item-focus/test.ts`: "does not redirect an item move before the first composite mount", "does not redirect a composite move before the first composite mount", "does not redirect a derived composite move before the first mount")
- Given a toolbar with no recorded move, when it unmounts and remounts (or its `composite` prop is switched off and back on), then focus and the page position are left alone and no document scroll fires. These are the harness control cases. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-7360/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-7360/test.ts`: "keeps focus and page position when an untouched toolbar comes back", "keeps focus when an untouched toolbar comes back", "keeps focus and page position when untouched composite behavior comes back", "keeps focus when untouched composite behavior comes back")
- Given a toolbar whose active item was moved with the keyboard, when it is collapsed and expanded again (once or three times in a row), or when composite behavior is handed off and taken back, then the recorded move is not replayed: focus stays on the collapse/expand control and the page does not scroll. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-7360/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-7360/test.ts`: "keeps focus and page position when the toolbar comes back after a move", "keeps focus and page position through repeated remounts", "keeps focus and page position when composite behavior comes back"; `app/src/sandbox/composite-7360/test.ts`: "keeps focus when the toolbar comes back after a move", "keeps focus through repeated remounts", "keeps focus when composite behavior comes back")
- Given a move recorded while composite behavior is handed off, when it is taken back, then that pending move is carried out and its item takes focus, because nothing could carry it out meanwhile. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-7360/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-7360/test.ts`: "focuses a newly moved item when composite behavior comes back")
- Given an explicit focus command on the composite element, when the toolbar is expanded, then the toolbar takes focus and is scrolled into view; when it is collapsed or handed off at the time of the command, then the request stays pending and is carried out once the toolbar is back. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-7360/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-7360/test.ts`: "focuses the toolbar when a focus command runs while it is expanded", "focuses the toolbar when a focus command runs while it is collapsed", "focuses the toolbar when a focus command runs while it is handed off")
- Given a request for a tool that has not loaded, when the tool finally registers, then it takes focus and is scrolled into view; the request also survives composite behavior being handed off and taken back in between. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-7360/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-7360/test.ts`: "focuses a tool that loads after being asked for", "focuses a tool that loads after composite behavior comes back")
- Given a pending request that is abandoned by picking a different tool, when composite behavior later comes back, then nothing moves: an abandoned request is spent rather than still waiting. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-7360/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-7360/test.ts`: "keeps focus and page position when composite behavior comes back after an abandoned request", "keeps focus when composite behavior comes back after an abandoned request")
- Given a pending request that the composite element itself takes over by being focused, when composite behavior is handed off and taken back, then nothing moves, because the take-over spent the request. - Given the superseded-move fixture's control cases, when composite behavior is handed off and taken back with no move behind it, then focus stays put; when a tool loads after being asked for, it takes focus; and a handoff in between does not spend the pending request. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-superseded-move/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-superseded-move/test.ts`: "keeps focus when untouched composite behavior comes back", "focuses a tool that loads after being asked for", "focuses a tool that loads after composite behavior comes back")
- Given a panel dismissed in a later task, dismissed by the same handler that focused it, dismissed synchronously, or that hides itself when tabbed into, when the panel is reopened and a new item registers while DOM focus is inside it, then nothing moves focus on its own. - Given a reopened panel whose active item is already set, when the panel is focused or a programmatic move targets it, then the active item is presented (the panel's `scrollTop` becomes greater than 0) and the panel holds focus, so refusing to present does not outlive the panel. - Given a presentation parked while a popup is being positioned, when the popup closes, then the presentation is abandoned and the document scroll offset stays exactly where it was, with no document scroll event. ### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a composite whose page number becomes `NaN` while the user clears a spinbutton, when the field is emptied, then the app does not crash, the current page's items stay rendered, and typing a new page number renders that page. Chromium and Firefox only for the browser copy. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-6335/test-chrome-firefox.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-6335/test.ts`: "clearing the page field does not crash the app")

### SSR and hydration

- Given composite items before hydration with JavaScript disabled, when Tab is pressed repeatedly, then every item is reachable in document order, including items belonging to virtual-focus composites whose composite element is not published yet. Chromium with JS disabled. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-item-tabbable/test-chrome-js-disabled.ts`: "keeps items tabbable before hydration")
- Given a hydrated page with several composites, when Tab is pressed, then each composite contributes exactly one tab stop: a store with no composite element keeps roving tabindex on its items, virtual-focus options are never tab stops so the composite element is the stop, and the final roving item is its own stop. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-item-tabbable/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-item-tabbable/test.ts`: "keeps a single tab stop per composite once hydrated")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a composite inside a same-origin iframe, when an arrow key moves the active item, then the keyboard event forwarded to the item is a `KeyboardEvent` built by the frame's own window, and the blur event delivered to the previous item is a `FocusEvent` built by the frame's own window. This fixture has no happy-dom duplicate because happy-dom shares constructors between a frame and its parent. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-iframe-event-realm-7193/test-browser.ts`: "forwards the keyboard event built by the frame's own window", "blurs the previous item with an event built by the frame's own window")
- Given a virtualized composite renderer measured by a `ResizeObserver`, when the whole list is scrolled through, when items are re-rendered to new nodes under the same ids, and when the list is unmounted, then the count of observed-but-detached nodes stays 0. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-renderer-6215/test-browser.ts`: "does not retain detached item nodes that are no longer rendered")
- Given a vertical renderer containing a horizontal group of five 140px columns rendered one row tall, when layout is computed, then the group's height is read from the rendered element (40px) so the group sits at `top: 80px` and the row after it at `top: 120px`, rather than summing the columns' widths to 700px. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-renderer-6216/test-browser.ts`: "vertical renderer measures a horizontal group's height along the parent axis")
- Given a nested cross-oriented group whose columns are 28px and 36px tall, when sized from metadata alone, then its height is the largest child extent (36px), putting the next row at `top: 76px` instead of 320px. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-renderer-6216/test-browser.ts`: "nested cross-oriented group is sized by its largest child extent")
- Given a virtualized renderer whose active descendant lies outside the rendered window, when the window is computed, then the active item's ancestor item is rendered alongside it so all three items render in index order. Asserted for five id-resolution shapes: a generated descendant without nested metadata, a generated descendant with partial nested metadata, an explicit nested item id, an exact item after a matching ancestor prefix, and the closest ancestor after a shallower prefix. Chromium only for the browser copy. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/composite-renderer-active-ancestor/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/composite-renderer-active-ancestor/test.ts`: "renders active item ancestor for generated descendant without nested metadata", "... with partial nested metadata", "... for explicit nested item id", "... for exact item after matching ancestor prefix", "... for closest ancestor after shallower prefix")

## toolbar

### Roles and attributes

- Given a vertical toolbar, when inspected, then it has `aria-orientation="vertical"`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/toolbar-container-focus/test-browser.ts`: "vertical toolbar moves with up and down arrows only")
- Given toolbar separators with an explicit orientation, when inspected, then a column divider has `aria-orientation="vertical"`, a row divider `"horizontal"`, and a plain divider defaults to `"vertical"`. Chromium only for the browser copy. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/toolbar-separator-6302/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/toolbar-separator-6302/test.ts`: "honors explicit toolbar separator orientation")

### Keyboard

- Given a toolbar, when ArrowRight, End, Home and ArrowDown are pressed, then the active item moves right, jumps to the last item, jumps back to the first, and ArrowDown does nothing in a horizontal toolbar. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/toolbar-keyboard-navigation/test.ts`: "moves through toolbar items with keyboard commands")
- Given a toolbar whose configured active item is disabled, when Tab enters it, then focus lands on the next enabled item and Tab out then Shift+Tab back returns to that same item. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/toolbar-keyboard-navigation/test.ts`: "enters a toolbar whose active item is disabled")
- Given a toolbar whose active item is removed from the DOM, when Shift+Tab re-enters the toolbar, then focus lands on a surviving item and ArrowLeft continues from there. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/toolbar-keyboard-navigation/test.ts`: "recovers when the active toolbar item is removed")
- Given a `ComboboxSelect` composed into a toolbar, when End moves to it and ArrowDown opens the list, then options become active in turn, Enter selects one and updates the select's text, and ArrowLeft returns to the previous toolbar item. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/toolbar-keyboard-navigation/test.ts`: "composes a ComboboxSelect with toolbar navigation")
- Given a vertical toolbar, when ArrowRight or ArrowLeft is pressed, then nothing moves; ArrowDown and ArrowUp move between items. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/toolbar-container-focus/test-browser.ts`: "vertical toolbar moves with up and down arrows only")
- Given a `ToolbarContainer` whose inner input is closed, when Tab reaches it, then the container itself takes focus and the input does not; typing a character opens it and focuses the input; Escape returns focus to the container; Enter opens it again and a second Enter closes it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/toolbar-container-focus/test-browser.ts`: "ToolbarContainer keeps its inner input out of the tab order until opened")
- Given an empty `ToolbarContainer` field, when Backspace or Delete is pressed while the container holds focus, then focus moves into the input and the next typed character lands in it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/toolbar-container-focus/test-browser.ts`: "keeps focus in the field after Backspace on an empty container field", "keeps focus in the field after Delete on an empty container field")
- Given a filled `ToolbarContainer` field, when Backspace is pressed once, then the field is cleared and focus stays on the container; a second Backspace moves focus into the input, and the next character lands there. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/toolbar-container-focus/test-chrome.ts`: "keeps focus in the field after Backspace clears the field first")
- Given a `ToolbarItem` rendered as an input, when ArrowRight is pressed with the caret inside the text, then the caret moves; when the caret is already at the end, then focus moves to the next toolbar item. ArrowLeft mirrors it, moving focus to the container when the caret is at 0. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/toolbar-container-focus/test-browser.ts`: "ToolbarItem rendered as input navigates only at text boundaries")
- Given a `ToolbarItem` input in the parent document and an identical one inside a same-origin iframe, when ArrowRight and ArrowLeft are pressed, then the caret moves one character at a time and only a press at the text boundary moves focus to the adjacent toolbar item. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/toolbar-iframe-6316/test-browser.ts`: "ToolbarItem input navigates at text boundaries in the parent document", "ToolbarItem input navigates at text boundaries inside iframes")
- Given a text field in a toolbar during IME composition, when Enter is pressed with `isComposing` set, then focus stays in the field; the same holds for Safari's composing Enter, which reports `keyCode` 229 rather than `isComposing`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/toolbar-container-focus/test.ts`: "keeps focus in the field on composing Enter", "keeps focus in the field on Safari composing Enter")
- Given a real IME composition committed through Chrome DevTools Protocol, when Enter commits it, then the field keeps its value and its focus. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/toolbar-container-focus/test-chrome.ts`: "keeps focus in the field on composing Enter")

### SSR and hydration

- Given a toolbar rendered with `activeId` undefined and with `activeId` null, before hydration with JavaScript disabled, when Tab is pressed repeatedly, then every native item is reachable in document order. Chromium with JS disabled. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/toolbar-pre-hydration/test-chrome-js-disabled.ts`: "keeps native items tabbable with undefined and null active IDs")
