### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a `show()` that names no opener while a `PopoverDisclosure` button is mounted, when the popover opens, then the mounted button stays the opener (keeping `aria-expanded="true"`) rather than the element that happened to hold focus, which also anchors the popup to that button. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/popover-disclosure-7087/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/popover-disclosure-7087/test.ts`: "keeps a mounted button as the opener when the open names none")
- Given an open that captured nothing (no focused element), when a later open from a different field happens, then the previously captured field is treated as a stale fallback and replaced, so clicking the new field does not dismiss the popup. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/popover-disclosure-7087/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/popover-disclosure-7087/test.ts`: "replaces the fallback after an open that captured nothing")
- Given the popup's own derived store being replaced when its wrapper remounts, when a new field opens the popup afterwards, then the fallback is still replaced rather than pinned to the original field forever. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/popover-disclosure-7087/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/popover-disclosure-7087/test.ts`: "replaces the fallback after the popup's own store is replaced")
- Given no disclosure button mounted at all, when a field opens the popup, then that field becomes the opener so clicking it is not an outside interaction; clicking a different field dismisses it, and reopening from that other field makes it the new opener. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/popover-disclosure-7087/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/popover-disclosure-7087/test.ts`: "falls back to the focused field when no button is mounted")
- Given an async positioning run that resolves after a newer one has already applied a `top` placement, when the stale run releases, then the stale result is ignored: the placement stays `top` and the wrapper transform is unchanged. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/popover-stale-position/test-browser.ts`: "ignores stale async positioning after a new effect runs")

- Given the `close` function exposed on the `Popover` and on the `Popover.Panel` slots, when it is called, then the popover closes; passing an element or a ref restores focus there instead of to the button; and passing an event is accepted. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/popover/popover.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/popover/popover.test.ts`: "should expose a close function that closes the popover", "should expose a close function that closes the popover and restores to a specific element", "should expose a close function that closes the popover and restores to a ref", "should expose a close function that closes the popover and takes an event")
- Given a wrapping `OpenClosed` provider, when it reports open or closed, then the panel is always open or always closed accordingly, and the state is readable from inside. [vue only] (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/popover/popover.test.ts`: "should always open the PopoverPanel because of a wrapping OpenClosed component", "should always close the PopoverPanel because of a wrapping OpenClosed component", "should be possible to read the OpenClosed state")
- Given nested popovers, when each is toggled, then they are controlled individually. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/popover/popover.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/popover/popover.test.ts`: "should be possible to nest Popover components and control them individually")

### Positioning

- Given a `PopoverAnchor` rendered either before or after the disclosure, when the popover opens, then the anchor in use is the explicit one and the popover's vertical center aligns with the anchor's within 1px. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/popover-anchor-3729/test-browser.ts`: "positions the popover next to PopoverAnchor when rendered disclosure first", "positions the popover next to PopoverAnchor when rendered anchor first"; `app/src/sandbox/popover-anchor-3729/test.ts`: "keeps the explicit anchor when the Disclosure first disclosure is clicked", "keeps the explicit anchor when the Anchor first disclosure is clicked")
- Given an explicit anchor that unmounts, when the popover repositions, then it falls back to the `PopoverDisclosure` and aligns to it; when the disclosure also unmounts, then both the anchor and the disclosure report "none" and the popover stays open. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/popover-anchor-3729/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/popover-anchor-3729/test.ts`: "falls back to PopoverDisclosure when PopoverAnchor unmounts", "falls back to the disclosure when the explicit anchor unmounts", "clears the disclosure fallback when it unmounts")
- Given a disclosure whose callback ref changes, when the ref is swapped, then the store still reports a button disclosure and the popover still opens. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/popover-anchor-3729/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/popover-anchor-3729/test.ts`: "restores the disclosure when a callback ref changes")
- Given a `HovercardAnchor`, when the hovercard is shown by hover, dismissed with Escape, and then reopened from a separate disclosure button by keyboard, then the explicit anchor is preserved and the card stays aligned to it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/popover-anchor-3729/test-browser.ts`: "preserves HovercardAnchor after keyboard activation")
- Given a `MenuAnchor` plus a `MenuButton`, when the menu opens, then the anchor is the explicit one, the disclosure is the button, the menu aligns to the anchor, and Escape returns focus to the button. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/popover-anchor-3729/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/popover-anchor-3729/test.ts`: "keeps MenuButton as the disclosure for MenuAnchor")
- Given a hover-triggered menu whose anchor is separate from its button, when the pointer moves within the `MenuButton`, then the menu stays open past the zero-delay hide timer. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/popover-anchor-3729/test-browser.ts`: "keeps a hover menu open over MenuButton")
- Given a `SelectAnchor`, when the select opens, then the listbox aligns to the anchor and the store reports the explicit anchor. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/popover-anchor-3729/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/popover-anchor-3729/test.ts`: "positions SelectPopover next to SelectAnchor", "preserves SelectAnchor when Select opens")
- Given a combobox with an explicit anchor, with only an input, or with only a disclosure button, when the popover opens, then the anchor in use is respectively the explicit element, the input, or the button, and the reported disclosure is the input except in the disclosure-only case; the popover aligns to whichever is the anchor. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/popover-anchor-3729/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/popover-anchor-3729/test.ts`: "uses the explicit Combobox anchor", "uses the input Combobox anchor", "uses the disclosure Combobox anchor")
- Given an input-anchored combobox whose input unmounts, when it repositions, then both the anchor and the disclosure fall back to the `ComboboxDisclosure` button and the popover realigns to it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/popover-anchor-3729/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/popover-anchor-3729/test.ts`: "uses the input Combobox anchor", "uses ComboboxDisclosure when the combobox input unmounts")
- Given non-composite comboboxes, when they mount, then the anchor is the input in the input case and the explicit element in the explicit case, and the popover aligns accordingly. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/popover-anchor-3729/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/popover-anchor-3729/test.ts`: "uses the non-composite input Combobox anchor", "uses the non-composite explicit Combobox anchor")
- Given a combobox disclosure with descendants, when they read context, then they receive the correct scoped combobox store. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/popover-anchor-3729/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/popover-anchor-3729/test.ts`: "provides the Combobox store to disclosure descendants")
- Given a popover placed `right` with no room, when the viewport narrows and then the page scrolls, then `flip` moves it above the anchor and then below it, each time keeping a non-negative gap. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/popover-flip-placement/test-chrome.ts`: "falls back from right to top and bottom")
- Given an RTL popover with an arrow placed `right`, when scrolling flips it above the anchor, then the arrow's horizontal center still falls inside the anchor's span, because the stale `right: 100%` from the previous placement is cleared. The happy-dom copy asserts the inline styles directly: `right: 100%` is written for the `right` placement, `top: 100%` after switching to `top`, and `right` is then cleared to the empty string. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/popover-arrow/test-browser.ts`: "arrow keeps pointing at the anchor after the popover flips on scroll in RTL", "arrow keeps pointing at the anchor after a placement change in RTL"; `app/src/sandbox/popover-arrow/test.ts`: "clears the arrow's stale static-side inset after a placement change")
- Given a popover whose disclosure element changes while it is open, when the popover is modal, non-portaled, or portaled with `preserveTabOrder` disabled, then the popover does not re-render; when the disclosure is the positioning fallback instead, then it does re-render. Chromium and Firefox for the browser copy. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/popover-disclosure-render/test-chrome-firefox.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/popover-disclosure-render/test.ts`: "does not re-render a modal popover when the disclosure element changes", "does not re-render a plain popover when the disclosure element changes", "does not re-render a portaled popover when preserveTabOrder is disabled", "re-renders when the disclosure positioning fallback changes")

- Given the `anchor` prop on `PopoverPanel`, when the popover opens, then the panel is anchored accordingly. [react only] (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/popover/popover.test.tsx`: "should be possible to use the `anchor` prop on the `PopoverPanel`")

- Given a live popover, when it opens, then it floats away from its disclosure. Visual. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/ariakit-ui-popover/test-browser.ts`: "floats the live popover away from its disclosure @visual", "page @visual")

### Animation and presence

- Given a popover arrow whose theme changes while the popover is closed, when it is reopened, then the arrow picks up the new fill, stroke and stroke width, so the colors are read fresh on open. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/popover-arrow/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/popover-arrow/test.ts`: "arrow takes the new theme colors when the popover opens after a theme switch")
- Given popovers with box-shadow rings of six shapes, when each opens, then the arrow's stroke matches the ring color and its stroke width matches the ring width: a 1px ring gives 2px, a 10px ring gives 20px, a 0.5px fractional ring rounds up to 2px, a Tailwind v3 multi-shadow ring gives 6px (skipping zero-spread placeholders), an inset ring gives 4px without the `inset` keyword leaking into the color, and a ring with an omitted color resolves to the popover's `currentColor` (rgb(220, 38, 38)) rather than its border color. happy-dom returns the declared box-shadow value rather than the browser's normalized serialization, so the widths there are unitless and the file covers the declared-value form while the browser test covers the normalized one. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/popover-arrow/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/popover-arrow/test.ts`: "arrow stroke matches the thin ring box-shadow", "... thick ring ...", "... fractional ring ...", "... tailwind ring ...", "... inset ring ...", "... current color ring ...")

- Given a `static` `Popover.Panel`, when the popover is closed, then the panel is still rendered; the `unmount` strategy can be swapped for a different one. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/popover/popover.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/popover/popover.test.ts`: "should be possible to always render the Popover.Panel if we provide it a `static` prop", "should be possible to use a different render strategy for the Popover.Panel")
- Given a `Popover.Panel` wrapped in a `Transition`, when the popover toggles, then the transition drives the panel. [react only] (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/popover/popover.test.tsx`: "should be possible to wrap the Popover.Panel with a Transition component")
- Given the `transition` prop, when the popover closes, then the closing transition runs and the popover ends up closed. [react only] (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/popover/popover.test.tsx`: "should be possible to close the Popover when using the `transition` prop")

- Given `prefers-reduced-motion`, when a popover opens, then no animation runs. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/ariakit-ui-popover/test-chrome.ts`: "runs no popover animation when the user prefers reduced motion")

## tooltip

### Roles and attributes

- Given a tooltip anchor whose button is only accessibly disabled, when inspected, then it has `aria-disabled="true"` and stays focusable. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test.ts`: "keeps the disabled semantics on accessible disabled anchors")
- Given an accessibly disabled anchor, when Space is held down, then it does not gain `data-active`, so activation suppression also suppresses the pressed state. The browser copy covers only the button-first composition order because a trusted Space on a native button is a native click; the happy-dom copy covers both orders. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test-browser.ts`: "does not put an accessible disabled anchor in the pressed state"; `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test.ts`: "does not put accessible disabled anchors in the pressed state")
- Given a truly disabled anchor, when inspected, then `Focusable` applies `pointer-events: none` so a mouse move cannot reach it at all. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test.ts`: "keeps truly disabled anchors out of pointer reach")
- Given an anchor whose `disabled` state turns truly disabled, when inspected, then it has no `tabindex`, so it drops out of the tab order. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test.ts`: "does not open a delayed tooltip when the anchor turns truly disabled while it is pending")
- Given a tooltip anchor with an explicit `aria-label`, when it renders, then it carries that `aria-label` and no `aria-labelledby`. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/aria-labelledby-aria-label/test-chrome.ts`: "tooltip anchor with aria-label has no aria-labelledby")

### Keyboard

- Given several tooltips where some are held open, when Escape is pressed, then only the live one closes. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/ariakit-ui-tooltip/test-chrome.ts`: "closes the live tooltip on Escape while others are held open")

### Pointer

- Given a tooltip anchor, when it is hovered, then the tooltip shows after its delay; moving the pointer outside hides it, and hovering again reopens it immediately. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-interactions/test.ts`: "shows on hover, hides outside, and immediately reopens")
- Given an instant tooltip (no delay), when its anchor is hovered, then the tooltip shows straight away and hides when the pointer leaves. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-variants/test.ts`: "shows the instant tooltip on hover and focus")
- Given a tooltip used as an accessible label, when its anchor is clicked, then the tooltip stays open, and it hides only when the pointer leaves. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-variants/test.ts`: "keeps the label tooltip open when its anchor is clicked")
- Given two anchors, when a second is hovered while the first tooltip is visible, then the second tooltip shows immediately (within the skip timeout) and the first hides; after leaving and waiting past the skip timeout but less than the show timeout, hovering the first again makes it wait out the full show delay before appearing. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-cross-anchor/test-browser.ts`: "shows another tooltip immediately while one is active")
- Given a mobile viewport, when a tooltip anchor is tapped, then the label tooltip does not appear even after 600ms. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-variants/test-mobile.ts`: "does not show the label tooltip on tap")
- Given an anchor whose disabled button is composed anchor-first, button-first, or with the anchor itself disabled, when it is hovered, then the tooltip shows, so an accessibly disabled anchor still explains itself to pointer users. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test.ts`: "shows the tooltip on hover when the anchor renders the disabled button", "shows the tooltip on hover when the disabled button renders the anchor", "shows the tooltip on hover when the anchor itself is the disabled one", "shows the tooltip on keyboard focus in both composition orders")
- Given a consumer that opts out of hover for disabled anchors, when the anchor is hovered, then the tooltip stays closed; given a callback that returns false for that anchor, the tooltip also stays closed. Both still show on keyboard focus. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test.ts`: "does not show the tooltip on hover when the consumer opts out for disabled anchors", "still shows the tooltip on keyboard focus when hover is opted out", "lets a callback decide whether a disabled anchor shows on hover", "still shows the tooltip on keyboard focus when a callback declines hover")
- Given a rendered element that sets its own `disabled` markup without Ariakit resolving a disabled state, when hovered or focused, then the tooltip shows in both cases, keeping the pointer and keyboard halves in agreement. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test.ts`: "shows the tooltip on hover when the rendered element declares itself disabled", "shows the tooltip on keyboard focus when the rendered element declares itself disabled")
- Given a truly disabled anchor whose `pointer-events` has been restored to `auto`, when it is hovered, then the tooltip stays closed; the same holds when the truly disabled state is resolved below the anchor. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test.ts`: "does not show the tooltip on hover for a truly disabled anchor that keeps pointer events", "does not show the tooltip on hover when the truly disabled state is below the anchor")
- Given a 150ms delayed tooltip, when the anchor is hovered, then the tooltip opens after the delay; but if hovering makes the anchor truly disabled (or drops its `focusable`) while the show is pending, then the tooltip never opens. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test.ts`: "opens a delayed tooltip on hover", "does not open a delayed tooltip when the anchor turns truly disabled while it is pending", "does not open a delayed tooltip when the anchor loses focusable while it is pending")
- Given a rendered button disabled with `focusable={false}` (so its disabled props are inoperative), when hovered or focused, then the tooltip shows in both cases; but given the anchor itself disabled with `focusable={false}` (no tab stop, no focus reveal), then hovering does not show it, so the tooltip never becomes pointer-only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test.ts`: "shows the tooltip on hover when the rendered button is disabled with focusable false", "shows the tooltip on keyboard focus when the rendered button is disabled with focusable false", "does not show the tooltip on hover when the anchor is disabled with focusable false")
- Given a rendered element that emits `data-truly-disabled="false"` for its own styling, when hovered, then the tooltip still shows, because only Ariakit's own stamped value counts. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test.ts`: "shows the tooltip on hover when the rendered element carries the attribute with a false value")
- Given accessibly disabled anchors, when they are clicked (forced past Playwright's actionability check in the browser), then the activation counter stays at 0 while an enabled button's click increments it to 1. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-button-disabled/test.ts`: "does not activate accessible disabled anchors")

- Given an `@ariakit/ui` tooltip anchor, when it is hovered, then the live tooltip opens over the anchor. Chromium only for the behavior half. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/ariakit-ui-tooltip/test-chrome.ts`: "opens the live tooltip on hover"; `app/src/sandbox/ariakit-ui-tooltip/test-browser.ts`: "shows the live tooltip over its anchor on hover @visual", "page @visual")

### Focus management

- Given a tooltip anchor, when it receives keyboard focus, then the tooltip shows, and it hides once focus moves to another element. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-interactions/test.ts`: "shows on focus and hides after focus moves")
- Given a tooltip shown by hover and then keyboard-focused, when the pointer leaves, then the tooltip stays open because focus still holds it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-interactions/test.ts`: "stays open when hover is followed by keyboard focus")
- Given a tooltip shown by Tab (focus-visible), when the pointer moves outside, onto the anchor, and out again, then the tooltip stays open throughout. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-interactions/test.ts`: "stays open after focus-visible and pointer movement")
- Given a tooltip that was shown by hover and then lost keyboard focus, when the pointer re-enters the anchor, then the tooltip waits out the show delay again rather than appearing immediately. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-interactions/test.ts`: "waits again after keyboard focus is lost")
- Given tooltip content that has been clicked into, when Escape is pressed, then the tooltip closes and focus returns to its anchor; the same holds for an animated tooltip. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-interactions/test.ts`: "Escape from tooltip content restores its anchor"; `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-variants/test.ts`: "Escape from animated tooltip content restores the anchor")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given three tooltips forced open at once, when they render, then all three stay visible and at least one forced-close request is recorded, so the re-entrant close loop is broken rather than looping. Chromium only for the pure forced-open flow. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-4894/test-chrome.ts`: "does not loop when multiple tooltips are forced open"; `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-4894/test.ts`: "keeps multiple forced tooltips visible")
- Given two controlled tooltips that accept `setOpen` updates, when the second is opened, then the first closes. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-4894/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-4894/test.ts`: "hides controlled tooltips that accept setOpen updates")
- Given forced-open tooltips plus managed ones, when a second managed tooltip is opened, then the first managed one closes while all three forced ones stay visible. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-4894/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-4894/test.ts`: "keeps managed tooltips active after forced tooltips reopen")

### Dismissal and layering

- Given a tooltip portal, when the tooltip is hovered then unmounted, then exactly one portal container exists while it is mounted and zero afterwards, with no duplicates leaked under React 18 development StrictMode. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-fullscreen-portal/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-fullscreen-portal/test.ts`: "does not leak duplicate tooltip portal containers", "does not leak duplicate tooltip portal containers in StrictMode")
- Given fullscreen transitions, when the page enters fullscreen, exits, and re-enters, then exactly one portal container exists at each step and its parent alternates between the fullscreen element and `document.body`; unmounting the tooltip leaves zero containers. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-fullscreen-portal/test-browser.ts`: "keeps one portal container while moving in and out of fullscreen")
- Given a fullscreen host that is removed from the DOM while the tooltip is open, when fullscreen ends, then the tooltip stays visible and its portal moves to `document.body`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-fullscreen-portal/test-browser.ts`: "moves the portal to body when the fullscreen host is removed")
- Given a tooltip whose anchor is inside the fullscreen element, when it is hovered in fullscreen, then the tooltip renders inside the fullscreen element; after exiting fullscreen it renders back under `document.body`; a tooltip mounted while already in fullscreen also renders inside it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-fullscreen-portal/test-browser.ts`: "tooltip renders inside fullscreen element", "tooltip moves back to body after exiting fullscreen", "tooltip mounted while in fullscreen renders inside it")

### Animation and presence

- Given an animated tooltip shown by hover or by focus, when the pointer leaves or focus moves away, then the tooltip stays mounted and visible through its leave animation (matched only by the `hidden` query variant) before unmounting. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tooltip-variants/test.ts`: "keeps the hover-triggered tooltip mounted during leave", "keeps the focus-triggered tooltip mounted during leave")

## hover-card

### Keyboard

- Given an unfocused hovercard shown by hover, when Escape is pressed, then it closes and focus is not moved to the anchor; given a focused one, Escape closes it and restores focus to the anchor. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/hovercard-interactions/test.ts`: "Escape closes an unfocused hovercard without moving focus", "Escape closes a focused hovercard and restores the anchor")
- Given a hovercard anchor, when Tab reaches it, then the hidden disclosure becomes visible (no longer `height: 1px`) and a second Tab focuses it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/hovercard-disclosure-interactions/test.ts`: "shows and focuses the disclosure with the keyboard")
- Given the hovercard disclosure, when it is activated by click, Enter, or Space, then the card opens and its first link takes focus; Shift+Tab back to the disclosure and activating it again closes the card and returns focus to the disclosure. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/hovercard-disclosure-interactions/test.ts`: "toggles the hovercard disclosure with click", "toggles the hovercard disclosure with Enter", "toggles the hovercard disclosure with Space")
- Given a hovercard opened from the disclosure, when Escape is pressed, then the card closes and focus returns to the anchor link rather than to the disclosure. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/hovercard-disclosure-interactions/test.ts`: "Escape restores focus to the anchor")
- Given the hovercard disclosure visible, when Tab moves focus past it to the next element, then the disclosure goes back to `height: 1px`; Shift+Tab back into the region reveals it again. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/hovercard-disclosure-interactions/test.ts`: "hides the disclosure when keyboard focus leaves")
- Given a nested hovercard whose parent is open, when the nested card is open and focus is on an input outside both, then Escape closes only the nested card and leaves the parent open. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/hovercard-nested-listener/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/hovercard-nested-listener/test.ts`: "closes nested hovercard on Escape when focus is outside")

### Pointer

- Given a hovercard anchor, when the pointer moves onto it, then the card is not visible immediately and appears after the show delay; moving the pointer away keeps it visible briefly and then removes it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/hovercard-interactions/test.ts`: "shows after hovering and hides after hovering outside")
- Given a visible hovercard whose content has been clicked (so it holds focus), when the pointer moves outside and 300ms pass, then the card stays open. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/hovercard-interactions/test.ts`: "stays open while focused")
- Given a visible hovercard, when the pointer leaves for 100ms and returns to the anchor, or leaves and lands on a button inside the card, then the card stays open past the hide timeout. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/hovercard-interactions/test.ts`: "stays open when the pointer quickly returns")
- Given an open hovercard, when the mouse wheel is scrolled by 300px, then the card stays open after 300ms; moving the pointer away still closes it. Chromium and Firefox only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/hovercard-interactions/test-chrome-firefox.ts`: "does not hide an open hovercard on wheel")
- Given a hovercard anchor inside a shadow root, when the pointer moves around within the anchor, then the card's open counter stays at 1; leaving and re-entering increments it to 2. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/hovercard-shadow-open-count/test-browser.ts`: "counts one opening while moving within a shadow anchor")
- Given a hovercard whose content includes a widget inside a shadow root, when the pointer moves onto that widget and 600ms pass (longer than the 500ms hide timeout), then the card stays visible. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/hovercard-shadow-widget-6303/test-browser.ts`: "keeps the hovercard visible when the pointer is over a shadow root widget")
- Given a hovercard anchor, when it is clicked rather than hovered, then the hovercard's keyboard disclosure stays visually hidden (`height: 1px`). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/hovercard-disclosure-interactions/test.ts`: "keeps the disclosure hidden after mouse focus")
- Given a hovercard that was opened through its disclosure and dismissed, when the anchor is hovered again, then the card appears but focus stays on the anchor rather than being pulled into the card. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/hovercard-disclosure-interactions/test.ts`: "hovering after disclosure use does not autofocus the card")

### Dismissal and layering

- Given a parent hovercard with a mousemove listener, when a nested hovercard is mounted and then unmounted, then the parent's listener install count does not change. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/hovercard-nested-listener/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/hovercard-nested-listener/test.ts`: "toggling a nested hovercard does not reinstall the parent mousemove listener")
- Given an open hovercard with a document `focusout` listener, when a `focusout` arrives whose `relatedTarget` is a non-Node `EventTarget`, then no page error is thrown. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/hovercard-5156/test-browser.ts`: "does not throw when a focusout has a non-Node relatedTarget")

### Animation and presence

- Given a hovercard opened by hovering the anchor, when the anchor is hovered before the delay elapses, then the dialog is not yet in the document and appears only after the timeout, so the show delay is observable. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/hovercard-disclosure-interactions/test.ts`: "shows the hovercard after hovering")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given `isPointInPolygon(point, polygon)` and a 2x2 square from (2,2) to (4,4), when every integer point from (0,0) to (5,5) is tested, then only the points inside or on the square return true, and every point outside returns false, including the points level with an edge but beyond it. This is the hit test behind the hovercard's safe-triangle polygon. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-react-components/src/hovercard/utils/polygon.test.ts`: "isPointInPolygon")
- Given a polygon with a slanted apex, when a horizontal ray grazes that apex, then it is not counted as a crossing, so a point level with the apex but outside the shape returns false. Asserted for an upward apex, a leftward apex and a downward apex, which exercise both branches of the vertex guard. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-react-components/src/hovercard/utils/polygon.test.ts`: "isPointInPolygon handles horizontal rays crossing slanted vertices")
- Given a malformed polygon whose vertex array contains an `undefined` entry, when a point inside the nominal shape is tested, then the helper returns false rather than throwing. (ariakit: `packages/ariakit-react-components/src/hovercard/utils/polygon.test.ts`: "isPointInPolygon returns false for malformed polygons")

## form

### Roles and attributes

- Given a form field that fails validation, when validation runs, then the field gets `aria-invalid="true"` and its error message becomes its accessible description; fixing the field flips `aria-invalid` back to `"false"` and drops the description. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form-3607/test-browser.ts`: "show validation errors for nested array fields", "clear error when nested field is filled"; `app/src/sandbox/form-6307/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/form-6307/test.ts`: "a successful submit does not steal focus on later items changes")
- Given a `FormSubmit` button on an invalid form, when the form is invalid, then the button carries `aria-disabled="true"`, and it loses the attribute once the form becomes valid. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form-valid/test.ts`: "submit button is disabled by default", "submit button is disabled when the form resets", "submit button is disabled when the form is submitted", "submit button is disabled when the form becomes invalid")
- Given `FormRadio` inside a `RadioProvider`, when rendered, then every radio in the group carries the form field's `name` (here `color`) rather than the radio store's auto-generated id. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form-radio-3833/test-browser.ts`: "FormRadio uses form field name inside RadioProvider")
- Given a form input with an explicit `aria-label`, when it renders, then it carries that `aria-label` and no `aria-labelledby`. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/aria-labelledby-aria-label/test-chrome.ts`: "form input with aria-label has no aria-labelledby")

### Keyboard

- Given a form, when Tab enters it, then the first input takes focus. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form/test.ts`: "focus on the first input by tabbing"; `app/src/sandbox/form-radio/test.ts`: "focus on the first radio button by tabbing")
- Given a required field, when Tab blurs it while empty, then its "Constraints not satisfied" error appears; tabbing through a second empty field adds a second error. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form/test.ts`: "show error on blur")
- Given a form with errors, when a field's value is typed, then that field's error disappears while the others remain. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form/test.ts`: "fix error on change")
- Given a reset button, when Enter activates it, then the fields are cleared. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form/test.ts`: "reset form on reset")
- Given a filled valid form, when Enter submits it, then the submit handler receives the serialized values (`{"name":"John","email":"john@example.com"}`) exactly once and the fields are reset afterwards. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form/test.ts`: "submit form", "reset form on submit")
- Given a radio form field, when Tab blurs the group with nothing selected, then the group's error appears; selecting with Space clears it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form-radio/test.ts`: "show error on blur", "fix error on change"; `app/src/sandbox/form-radio-3833/test-browser.ts`: "validation error shows after blur")
- Given a radio form, when it is submitted with a selection, then the payload is `{"color":"green"}` and the radios are reset afterwards. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form-radio/test.ts`: "submit form", "reset form on submit")
- Given a select composed into a form, when Tab passes through the select button without ever opening the popover, then the error appears; opening the popover, pressing Escape, reopening with Space, moving with ArrowDown, selecting with Enter, and clicking the empty option all leave the error count at 0 until focus finally leaves both the button and the popover. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form-select/test.ts`: "show error on tabbing through select button", "show error only on blur both the select button and the popover")
- Given a select in a form, when submit runs with nothing selected, then one error appears and focus moves to the select button without opening the popover; once a value is chosen, submitting alerts `{"name":"John","fruit":"Banana"}` and the select's text resets to "Select an item". (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form-select/test.ts`: "submit failed", "submit succeed")
- Given a form with sync and async field validation callbacks, when a field is focused and then blurred, then the queued validation runs and the combined error text "Constraints not satisfied - Field 1 - Field 2 - Abstract Form - Form" appears; submitting produces two instances of the combined submit-error text. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form-callback-queue/test.ts`: "validation on sync input", "validation on async input", "submit")

### Focus management

- Given a failed submit with several invalid fields, when it runs, then focus lands on the first invalid field in document order, not in registration order. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form-6305/test-browser.ts`: "failed submit focuses the first invalid field in document order")
- Given a form that already submitted successfully once, when the email is made invalid again and then a button is activated that mounts a new field (changing the form items), then focus stays on that button and is not stolen by the invalid field. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form-6307/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/form-6307/test.ts`: "a successful submit does not steal focus on later items changes")
- Given a failed submit, when it runs on a text form, then focus lands on the first invalid input; on a radio form, on the first radio. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form/test.ts`: "focus on input with error on submit"; `app/src/sandbox/form-radio/test.ts`: "focus on radio with error on submit", "show error on submit")
- Given `FormPush` on an array with existing items, when it adds an item, then the newly created field takes focus (`tags.2`); on an initially empty array it focuses `emails.0`, then `emails.1`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form-array-focus/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/form-array-focus/test.ts`: "FormPush focuses the field it creates after an existing item", "FormPush keeps auto-focusing fields in an initially empty array")
- Given two arrays where one name is a prefix of the other (`tags` and `tags2`), when `FormPush` or `FormRemove` moves focus, then it stays within the targeted array and never leaks into the prefix sibling. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form-array-focus/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/form-array-focus/test.ts`: "FormPush keeps focus within the target array, not a sibling sharing the name prefix", "FormRemove keeps focus within the target array, not a sibling sharing the name prefix")
- Given an array whose name contains regex metacharacters (`c++`), when `FormPush` adds an item, then building the auto-focus matcher does not throw and focus stays within the array; `FormRemove` on the first item moves focus to `c++.1`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form-array-focus/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/form-array-focus/test.ts`: "FormPush keeps focus within an array whose name has regex metacharacters", "FormRemove moves focus to the next field when the array name has regex metacharacters")
- Given a select in a form, when its label is clicked, then the select button takes focus with `data-focus-visible` and the popover does not open. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form-select/test.ts`: "click on label")

### Forms

- Given a checkbox whose form field name looks like an integer (`123`), when it is clicked, then it toggles correctly, and the same holds for a non-integer-like name. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form-checkbox-integer-like-name/test.ts`: "check checkbox with integer-like name on click", "check checkbox with non integer-like name on click")
- Given `form.names.*` values, when one is rendered as a React child, then no "Cannot convert a Symbol value to a string" error appears; when `Object.prototype.toString` is called on one, then it resolves to an `[object …]` tag instead of throwing. The React-child render path stays browser-only because after the fix React raises its own invalid-child console error, which would trip `failOnConsole` in the happy-dom run. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form-names-6308/test-chrome.ts`: "rendering a raw form.names.* value does not crash with a Symbol coercion error", "inspecting a form.names.* value resolves to an object tag instead of throwing"; `app/src/sandbox/form-names-6308/test.ts`: "inspecting a form.names.* value resolves to an object tag instead of throwing")
- Given an auto-save form whose store `submit()` awaits an animation frame, when the document is hidden so `requestAnimationFrame` stops firing (recreating the real browser's behavior, which Playwright's focus emulation otherwise masks), then the submission still completes through a timeout fallback and the status reaches "Saved" rather than stalling on "Saving". (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form-6309/test-browser.ts`: "auto-save completes while the tab is hidden")
- Given `objectToFormEntries`, the helper that turns a component value into hidden form inputs, when it encodes `{ a: "b" }`, then it produces `[["a", "b"]]`. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/form.test.ts`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/utils/form.test.ts`: "should encode an input of %j to an form data output")
- Given an array value `[1, 2, 3]`, when it is encoded, then the entries are keyed by index as strings: `[["0","1"],["1","2"],["2","3"]]`. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/form.test.ts`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/utils/form.test.ts`: "should encode an input of %j to an form data output")
- Given a nested object `{ id: 1, admin: true, name: { first, last, nickname: { preferred } } }`, when it is encoded, then numbers and booleans stringify (`true` becomes `"1"`) and nested keys use bracket notation: `id`, `admin`, `name[first]`, `name[last]`, `name[nickname][preferred]`. This is the exact serialization every Headless UI component with a complex form value produces. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/form.test.ts`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/utils/form.test.ts`: "should encode an input of %j to an form data output")

## checkbox

### Roles and attributes

- Given a native Ariakit checkbox, when rendered, then it has `type="checkbox"` and `aria-checked="false"` until checked. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/checkbox-interactions/test.ts`: "renders native checkbox semantics and supports Tab and Space")
- Given a checkbox rendered as a `button`, when inspected, then it has `role="checkbox"` and `aria-checked` reflecting its state. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/checkbox-interactions/test.ts`: "supports a checkbox rendered as a button")
- Given a checkbox with a `value`, when inspected, then the `value` attribute is present (here `accept`). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/checkbox-interactions/test.ts`: "supports uncontrolled, controlled, store, and valued checkboxes")
- Given a checkbox group wrapper, when inspected, then it has `role="group"`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/checkbox-interactions/test.ts`: "updates independent values in a checkbox group")
- Given a checkbox whose optional render prop is `undefined`, when it is clicked, then `aria-checked` still flips from `"false"` to `"true"`, so the undefined render prop does not strip the checkbox semantics. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/checkbox-interactions/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/checkbox-interactions/test.ts`: "preserves checkbox semantics when an optional render prop is undefined")

- Given a Checkbox with the indeterminate prop, when it renders, then it has aria-checked="mixed", indeterminate="true", role="checkbox", tabindex="0" and a data-indeterminate attribute. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should be possible to put the checkbox in an indeterminate state")
- Given a Checkbox with defaultChecked, when it renders, then it has aria-checked="true", role="checkbox", tabindex="0" and a data-checked attribute. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should be possible to put the checkbox in an default checked state")
- Given a plain Checkbox, when it renders, then it has aria-checked="false", role="checkbox" and tabindex="0". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should render a checkbox in an unchecked state")
- Given a Checkbox, when it renders, then the checkbox element is in the document (shared rendering scenario). (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should render a control")
- Given a Checkbox with no id prop, when it renders, then it still has an id attribute. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should have an `id` attached")
- Given a Checkbox with id="foo", when it renders, then its id attribute is exactly "foo". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should be possible to override the `id`")
- Given a Checkbox inside a disabled Field, when it renders, then the checkbox is disabled-ish, meaning it carries either disabled or aria-disabled="true". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should mark the control as disabled, if the `Field` is disabled")
- Given a Checkbox and a Label inside the same Field, when they render, then the checkbox's aria-labelledby contains the label's id. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should link a control and a `Label` when inside a `Field`")
- Given a Checkbox and two Label components inside one Field, when they render, then the checkbox's aria-labelledby lists both label ids. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should link a control and multiple `Label` components when inside a `Field`")
- Given a Checkbox and a Description inside one Field, when they render, then the checkbox's aria-describedby contains the description's id. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should link a control and a `Description` when inside a `Field`")
- Given a Checkbox and three Description components inside one Field, when they render, then aria-describedby lists all three description ids. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should link a control and multiple `Description` components when inside a `Field`")
- Given a Checkbox with both a Label and a Description inside one Field, when they render, then aria-labelledby points at the label and aria-describedby at the description. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should link a control with a `Label` and a `Description` when inside a `Field`")

- Given a `@ariakit/ui` card grid of checkboxes, when it renders, then it is a named `group`, and it keeps that group role even when its `role` prop is passed as `undefined`. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/ariakit-ui-checkbox/test-chrome.ts`: "a card grid is a named group of cards", "keeps the group role of a card grid whose role prop is undefined")

### Keyboard

- Given a focused checkbox, when Space is pressed, then it toggles; pressing again toggles back. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/checkbox-interactions/test.ts`: "renders native checkbox semantics and supports Tab and Space")
- Given a checkbox rendered as a button or a custom visually hidden checkbox, when Space or Enter is pressed, then it toggles; both keys work. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/checkbox-interactions/test.ts`: "supports a checkbox rendered as a button", "supports a custom visually hidden checkbox")
- Given twelve checkbox implementations on one page (uncontrolled, controlled, store-backed, valued, two dynamically linked, a button checkbox, one with a forwarded undefined render prop, a custom visually hidden one, and three group members), when Tab is pressed repeatedly, then each one is reached in order, so every implementation stays in the tab order. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/checkbox-interactions/test.ts`: "keeps each checkbox implementation in the tab order")

- Given an uncontrolled Checkbox, when it is focused and Space is pressed, then it becomes checked (aria-checked="true", data-checked), and a second Space returns it to unchecked. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should be possible to toggle a checkbox" under describe.each "Keyboard interactions (Uncontrolled)")
- Given a Checkbox controlled by useState through checked and onChange, when it is focused and Space is pressed, then it toggles to checked and back on a second press. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should be possible to toggle a checkbox" under describe.each "Keyboard interactions (Controlled)")

### Pointer

- Given a checkbox with an associated label, when the label text is clicked, then the checkbox toggles. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/checkbox-interactions/test.ts`: "supports uncontrolled, controlled, store, and valued checkboxes", "supports a custom visually hidden checkbox")

- Given an uncontrolled Checkbox, when it is clicked, then it becomes checked, and a second click returns it to unchecked. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should be possible to toggle a checkbox by clicking it" under describe.each "Mouse interactions (Uncontrolled)")
- Given a controlled Checkbox, when it is clicked, then it becomes checked, and a second click returns it to unchecked. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should be possible to toggle a checkbox by clicking it" under describe.each "Mouse interactions (Controlled)")
- Given a Checkbox and a Label in a Field with focus on the body, when the label is clicked, then the checkbox becomes the active element. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should be possible to click a `Label`, and focus the control when in a `Field`")
- Given a Checkbox and a Label with the passive prop in a Field, when the label is clicked, then focus stays on document.body. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should not be possible to click a `Label`, if the `Label` has the `passive` prop")
- Given a disabled Checkbox with a Label in a Field, when the label is clicked, then focus stays on document.body. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should not be possible to click a `Label` and focus the control, if the control is disabled")
- Given a Checkbox with a Label inside a disabled Field, when the label is clicked, then focus stays on document.body. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should not be possible to click a `Label` and focus the control, if the `Field` is disabled")
- Given a Checkbox with a Label in a Field nested in a disabled Fieldset, when the label is clicked, then focus stays on document.body. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should not be possible to click a `Label` and focus the control, if the `Fieldset` is disabled")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given uncontrolled, controlled, store-backed and valued checkboxes, when each is clicked or toggled with Space, then its checked state follows independently, with the controlled one starting checked and the store-backed one honoring both clicks and Space. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/checkbox-interactions/test.ts`: "supports uncontrolled, controlled, store, and valued checkboxes")
- Given two checkboxes bound to dynamically linked stores, when either is clicked, then both follow the link, and after a decoupling click only the clicked one changes. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/checkbox-interactions/test.ts`: "updates dynamically linked checkbox stores")
- Given a checkbox group holding an array value, when members are toggled by click or Space, then each member's checked state is independent of the others. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/checkbox-interactions/test.ts`: "updates independent values in a checkbox group")

- Given a select-all checkbox, when its children change or it is toggled, then it reflects and toggles their state. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/ariakit-ui-checkbox/test-chrome.ts`: "select all reflects and toggles its children")

### Forms

- Given a Checkbox with name="foo" inside a form, when it renders, then an element with [name=foo] exists in the document, so a native hidden form control backs the checkbox. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should render native (hidden) form elements for the control")
- Given a defaultChecked Checkbox with name="foo" and a submit button in a form, when the submit button is clicked, then the FormData passed to onSubmit has the key "foo". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should submit the form with all the data")
- Given a disabled Checkbox with name="bar" next to a hidden input foo=bar, when the form is submitted, then the entries are only [['foo', 'bar']]. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should not submit the data if the control is disabled")
- Given a defaultChecked Checkbox with name="foo" in a Field with a Label plus submit and reset buttons, when the checkbox is clicked and the form is submitted, then the payload differs from the initial submit, and after clicking Reset the payload matches the initial state again. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should reset the control when the form is reset")
- Given an uncontrolled Checkbox with name="notifications" as the only field in a form, when it is focused and Enter is pressed, then the form submits with {} because the checkbox is off; after clicking it the submit payload is { notifications: 'on' }, and after clicking again the key is gone. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/checkbox/checkbox.test.tsx: "should be possible to use in an uncontrolled way")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a focused checkbox field, when it takes focus, then the ring is drawn on its box. Visual. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/ariakit-ui-checkbox/test-browser.ts`: "draws the ring of a focused field on its box @visual", "page @visual")

## radio-group

### Roles and attributes

- Given a disabled radio group, when inspected, then the group has `aria-disabled="true"`, its native radios report as disabled, and an accessibly-disabled radio carries `aria-disabled="true"` instead. Chromium only for the browser copy. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/radio-group-3851/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/radio-group-3851/test.ts`: "disabled prop disables the group and radios")
- Given two radio groups on one page, when inspected, then every radio inside a group shares one non-empty `name` attribute and the two groups' names differ, which the test records as necessary for native Tab navigation and form submission to treat them as separate groups. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/radio-group-3833/test-browser.ts`: "radios have unique name attributes per group")
- Given unchecked radios, when inspected, then each has `aria-checked="false"`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/radio-selection-events/test.ts`: "selects basic radios by click")

- Given a RadioGroup.Option (Vue: RadioGroupOption) rendered with no RadioGroup ancestor, when it mounts, then it throws "<RadioGroup.Option /> is missing a parent <RadioGroup /> component." (Vue: "<RadioGroupOption /> is missing a parent <RadioGroup /> component."). (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/radio-group/radio-group.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/radio-group/radio-group.test.ts: "should error when we are using a <%s /> without a parent <RadioGroup />")

## button

### Roles and attributes

- Given the whole `Button` / `Command` / `Tab` / `ToolbarItem` / `MenuButton` family, when rendered, then the native `type` attribute is declared before refs run: a default `Tab` is `type="button"`, a submit `Tab` `type="submit"`, a reset `Tab` `type="reset"`, a `Tab` rendered as a div has no `type`, a hook-built tab has no `type`, an `input`-rendered `Command` is `type="submit"`, a default `Command` and a default `Button` are `type="button"`, a submit `Button` `type="submit"`, a reset `Button` `type="reset"`, a div-rendered button has no `type` but has `role="button"` and `tabindex="0"`, a link-rendered button keeps its `href`, and a `ToolbarItem` and a root `MenuButton` are both `type="button"`. The refs report the same resolved type. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/native-button-semantics/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/native-button-semantics/test.ts`: "declares native button types before refs run")
- Given custom-element composition, when inspected, then a focusable div has `tabindex="0"`, a disabled anchor has `tabindex="-1"` and no `disabled` attribute, a disabled button is genuinely `disabled`, and a nested `MenuButton` rendered as a div reports `tagName` DIV with no `type`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/native-button-semantics/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/native-button-semantics/test.ts`: "preserves custom element semantics")

- Given a `Button`, when it renders, then a button element is produced and its `type` defaults to `"button"`. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/button/button.test.tsx`: "should render a button", "should default to `type="button"`")
- Given a `Button` with a render prop or `as={Fragment}`, when it renders, then the slot output is used. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/button/button.test.tsx`: "should render a button using a render prop", "should be possible to render a Button using as={Fragment}")
- Given `autoFocus`, when the button renders, then it carries a `data-autofocus` attribute. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/button/button.test.tsx`: "should map the `autoFocus` prop to a `data-autofocus` attribute")
- Given a `DataInteractive` wrapper, when the element inside is focused or hovered, then the focus and hover data attributes are exposed on it. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/data-interactive/data-interactive.test.tsx`: "should expose focus data attributes on the element", "should expose hover data attributes on the element")

- Given an `@ariakit/ui` avatar slot, when it holds two wide initials, initials from adjacent expressions, or initials inside nested fragments, then they fit inside the slot; large avatar initials stay at the label text size, avatar dimensions survive a normal line height, and an image avatar fills the whole slot. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/ariakit-ui-button/test-browser.ts`: "fits two wide initials inside an avatar slot", "keeps large avatar initials at the label text size", "keeps avatar dimensions with normal line height", "fits initials from adjacent expressions inside an avatar slot", "fits initials inside nested fragments in an avatar slot", "keeps an image avatar at the full slot size")
- Given an avatar whose kind changes, when it re-renders, then the selected avatar color is preserved. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/ariakit-ui-button/test-chrome.ts`: "preserves the selected avatar color when its kind changes")
- Given a `@ariakit/ui` badge, when it renders, then it is phrasing content; single-digit counts stay square while longer counts grow, pills use more side padding and honor explicit padding, and two wide initials fit inside an avatar slot. Chromium only for the phrasing-content assertion. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/ariakit-ui-badge/test-chrome.ts`: "renders a badge as phrasing content"; `app/src/sandbox/ariakit-ui-badge/test-browser.ts`: "keeps single-digit counts square and lets longer counts grow", "uses more side padding for pills and keeps explicit padding", "fits two wide initials inside an avatar slot", "page @visual")

### Keyboard

### Focus management

- Given a focusable div whose `focusable` prop is toggled, when it is turned off, then `tabindex` is removed, and turning it back on restores `tabindex="0"`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/native-button-semantics/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/native-button-semantics/test.ts`: "updates custom focusability")

(ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/native-button-semantics/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/native-button-semantics/test.ts`: "clears submit focus visibility when focusable is disabled")

### Forms

- Given a submit button using React's form status, when Enter submits the form from the button, then the button's text becomes "Pending"; this holds for an Ariakit `Button`, for a `Button` rendered as a native submit, and for a `focusable` `Button`, whose pending state survives losing focus. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/button-form-status-4540/test-browser.ts`: "button shows pending state when submitted with Enter", "rendered submit button shows pending state", "focusable button keeps pending state after losing focus")

(ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/button-form-status-4540/test-browser.ts`: "focusable button prevents activation while pending", "focusable native button prevents activation while pending")

### SSR and hydration

- Given the button-type fixture rendered with `renderToString` and then hydrated, when both phases are inspected, then the server markup declares the same native `type` values as the client (except the div-rendered button, which gains `role` and `tabindex` only on the client), the server render logs no console errors beyond the expected `useLayoutEffect` warning, and hydration logs none at all. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/native-button-semantics/test.ts`: "server markup and hydration use the same native button type")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given React ref cleanup functions on Ariakit `Button`s, plain buttons, portals, connected portals and non-function portals, when each is unmounted, then its cleanup runs: object refs report detached, keyboard shortcuts registered in the ref stop firing (the counters freeze), and the portal reports its cleanup ran while still connected. Chromium and Firefox only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/button-ref-cleanup/test-chrome-firefox.ts`: "preserves React ref cleanup")

- Given a select autofilled by the browser, when the native control's value changes, then the Ariakit trigger gets `data-autofill` and its text follows the new value. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/select-legacy/public-tests/basic.react.test-helper.ts`: "mirrors native autofill and redirects native focus")
- Given a grid-shaped select, when it opens, then its items are `gridcell`s. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/select-legacy/public-tests/composite.react.test-helper.ts`: "moves through the two-dimensional Select composite")

- Given a `Select` inside a `Field`, when they render, then the control is marked disabled when the `Field` is disabled, and it is linked to one or several `Label` components, to one or several `Description` components, and to a `Label` plus a `Description` together. These come from the shared `commonControlScenarios` generator. - Given a legacy `Select` that is closed, when ArrowDown or ArrowUp is pressed, then the value moves to the next or previous item with a value, skipping trailing valueless items, and with `focusLoop` it wraps past the valueless item. The page-freeze variant (two trailing valueless items) is covered only in the browser because the buggy code loops synchronously and would hang the happy-dom worker instead of failing. - Given a grid select, when it opens with a value in the middle, then that cell takes focus, ArrowUp and ArrowLeft move through the grid, and Enter commits the new cell's value. - Given a select whose items render custom values, when ArrowUp changes the value and Escape is pressed, then the original value is restored. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/select-legacy/public-tests/composite.react.test-helper.ts`: "renders custom values and restores a moved value on escape")
- Given a standalone persistent `SelectList` (listbox), when it is focused, then the listbox itself holds focus and no option does; ArrowDown then focuses options in turn with `data-active-item`, `data-focus-visible` and `aria-selected` reflecting the selection; Enter and Space commit the active option. - Given a select composed with a combobox, when it opens, then the search input takes focus, typing filters, the matching option becomes active, and Enter commits it and closes the dialog. - Given a select composed with a combobox and a tab list, when it opens, then the first tab is selected; ArrowRight moves to the next tab, selecting it immediately in the automatic variant and only on Enter in the manual one; ArrowDown then picking an option commits its value. - Given a select inside a toolbar, when End moves focus to it, then ArrowDown twice and Enter commit the third option's value. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/select-legacy/public-tests/compositions.react.test-helper.ts`: "participates in toolbar navigation and selects an option")

### Pointer

- Given a legacy `Select`, when it is clicked, then the listbox opens with the currently selected option focused and `aria-selected="true"`; clicking another option closes the listbox and updates the trigger's text. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/select-legacy/public-tests/basic.react.test-helper.ts`: "opens with the selected item and commits another option")
- Given a multiple select, when an option is clicked, then it becomes `aria-selected="true"`, the listbox stays open, and the trigger's summary count increases. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/select-legacy/public-tests/basic.react.test-helper.ts`: "keeps the list open while toggling multiple values"; `app/src/sandbox/select-legacy/public-tests/compositions.react.test-helper.ts`: "combines ComboboxItem with multi-selectable SelectItem state")
- Given a grouped select, when an option is hovered and then a group label is hovered, then the option loses focus and DOM focus returns to the listbox. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/select-legacy/public-tests/composite.react.test-helper.ts`: "moves focus out of an option when hovering a group label")
- Given a select in a form, when the select is clicked, then the listbox opens with the trigger focused; clicking outside closes it and drops focus; clicking again reopens it. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/form-select/test-browser.ts`: "shows and hides the select with pointer input")
- Given a collapsed select with a side-effectful `focusOnHover` callback that moves the composite, when an option is hovered, then the callback does not run at all: `aria-expanded` stays `"false"`, no option gains `data-active-item`, the value is unchanged, and focus stays on an unrelated control. - Given a `Select` inside a `Field`, when the `Label` is clicked, then the control receives focus; but not when the `Label` has the `passive` prop, not when the control is disabled, not when the `Field` is disabled, and not when an enclosing `Fieldset` is disabled. ## tag

### Roles and attributes

- Given a tag field, when rendered, then the tags live inside a `listbox` (each tag an `option`), the text input is a sibling of that listbox rather than a descendant of it (because the `listbox` role accepts only options as children), the listbox has no `aria-owns`, and a `group` wrapper contains both so the label names all three. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tag/test.ts`: "renders the tags inside the listbox and the input outside it", "labels the control, the tag list and the input", "initial state")
- Given a `TagRemove` inside a `Tag`, when inspected, then the inner remove affordance is `aria-hidden="true"` with `aria-label="Press Delete or Backspace to remove"` and renders a default SVG icon. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag-remove-6330/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tag-remove-6330/test.ts`: "exposes standalone TagRemove with visible text as a named button")
- Given a standalone `TagRemove` with visible text, when inspected, then it is a named button, is not `aria-hidden`, has no `aria-label`, is focusable, and does not duplicate into a second button with the bare tag name. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag-remove-6330/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tag-remove-6330/test.ts`: "exposes standalone TagRemove with visible text as a named button")
- Given a standalone `TagRemove` with an `aria-label`, when inspected, then it carries that label, keeps its visible text, and passes axe's `aria-hidden-focus` rule with no violations. Chromium and Firefox only for the axe run. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag-remove-6330/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tag-remove-6330/test.ts`: "exposes standalone TagRemove with an aria-label")
- Given a `TagRemove` used outside a `Tag`, when inspected, then no default icon is rendered. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag-remove-6330/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tag-remove-6330/test.ts`: "does not render a default icon outside a Tag")
- Given a standalone `TagRemove` whose name comes from a `render` element or from a root `aria-labelledby`, when inspected, then that name is preserved and no `aria-label` is added. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag-remove-6330/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tag-remove-6330/test.ts`: "preserves a standalone render element name", "preserves a standalone root labelledby name")
- Given a tag list or a tag control with an explicit `aria-label`, when it renders, then each carries that `aria-label` and no `aria-labelledby`. The tag-list case queries with `includeHidden` because Playwright filters an initially empty `display: contents` list out of default role queries. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/aria-labelledby-aria-label/test-chrome.ts`: "tag list with aria-label has no aria-labelledby", "tag control with aria-label has no aria-labelledby")

### Keyboard

- Given a tag input, when text ending in a delimiter is typed, then a tag is created and the input is cleared; typing several delimiter-separated values creates several tags. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag/test.ts`: "add tags by typing")
- Given a tag input, when delimiters are typed first and text is then inserted between them with arrow keys, then the tags split at the delimiters in order (`["JavaScript","React","abc def","ghi"]`). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag/test.ts`: "add tags after typing delimiters")
- Given focus in the tag input, when ArrowLeft is pressed, then focus moves into the tag list from right to left, Home jumps to the first tag, End returns to the input, ArrowUp moves left within the list, and ArrowLeft on the first tag does not loop. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag/test.ts`: "move focus between tag list elements", "add tags by typing")
- Given focus on a tag, when characters are typed, then focus moves to the input, the characters land there, and returning with End re-selects the typed text. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag/test.ts`: "move focus between tag list elements")
- Given focus on a tag, when Delete is pressed, then the tag is removed and focus moves to the next tag; Backspace removes it and moves focus to the previous tag. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag/test.ts`: "remove tag by pressing Delete", "remove tag by pressing Backspace on the tag")
- Given focus in an empty tag input, when Backspace is pressed, then the last tag is removed and focus stays in the input. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag/test.ts`: "remove tag by pressing Backspace on the textbox")
- Given tag edits, when Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y are pressed, then removals and typed insertions are undone and redone step by step, the input value is restored alongside the tag list, and redo after a new change is a no-op. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag/test.ts`: "undo/redo removing tags", "undo/redo typing")

### Pointer

- Given a tag, when it is clicked, then it takes focus; when its remove affordance is clicked, then the tag is removed and focus moves to the input. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag/test.ts`: "click on tag", "remove tag by clicking on remove button")
- Given a tag control whose tag list has `display: contents` and generates no box, when the control's padding is clicked, then the input takes focus. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag/test-browser.ts`: "focuses the input when clicking on the control")
- Given non-focusable content inside a `display: contents` wrapper, when it is clicked, then focus moves to the tag input and the page stays responsive (a new tag can still be typed), rather than freezing in `getClosestFocusable`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag-list-6311/test-browser.ts`: "focuses the input and stays responsive when clicking non-focusable content inside a display:contents wrapper")
- Given clipboard text with no delimiter, when it is pasted into the input or with a tag focused, then it lands in the input as text and no tag is created. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag/test-browser.ts`: "paste tag without delimiters", "paste tag without delimiters from tag list")
- Given clipboard text containing delimiters, when it is pasted, then it is split into tags and the input is cleared with focus in it: "abc def ghi" becomes three tags, "abc def, ghi" becomes `["abc def","ghi"]`, "abc def, ghi; jkl" becomes `["abc def, ghi","jkl"]`, and a trailing newline is dropped. Each case is also asserted with a tag focused rather than the input. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag/test-browser.ts`: "paste tags with space", "paste tags with space from tag list", "paste tags with comma and space", "paste tags with comma and space from tag list", "paste tags with semicolon, comma and space", "paste tags with semicolon, comma and space from tag list", "paste tags with a final newline")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a string delimiter containing regex metacharacters, when text is typed with it, then it splits literally: `.` splits "one.two." into two tags, `+` does not throw even though it is an invalid regex on its own, and `|` does not freeze even though it matches the empty string. Chromium and Firefox only for the browser copy. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag-input-6333/test-chrome-firefox.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tag-input-6333/test.ts`: "splits string delimiters with regex metacharacters literally", "does not throw on string delimiters that are invalid regex patterns", "does not freeze on string delimiters that match empty regexes")
- Given IME composition typed through Chrome DevTools Protocol, when the composition is committed, then the intermediate composition text (which contains a space delimiter) does not become a tag and the input holds the committed characters. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag-input-6294/test-chrome.ts`: "does not split IME composition text into tags")
- Given a tag field combined with a combobox, when a suggestion is selected with Enter, then it becomes a tag and the combobox value resets to empty; but removing a tag from the tag list leaves the typed value intact. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag-combobox/test.ts`: "reset the value on selecting a tag from the combobox suggestions", "the value should not reset when removing a tag from the tag list", "initial state")
- Given a tag combobox, when a tag is added, then the suggestion list resets and the previously added tag's option carries `data-active-item` and `aria-selected="true"` after arrow navigation. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag-combobox/test.ts`: "suggestions reset after selecting a tag")
- Given a tag combobox with inline autocomplete, when a query is typed, then the input holds the completed value with the completion selected; after selecting and deselecting a tag, retyping the same query leaves no text selected, the option keeps `data-active-item`, and `aria-selected` follows the tag's presence; arrowing through other options updates the input value without re-selecting text. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tag-combobox/test.ts`: "deselecting a tag should not highlight the input text if it is not the first combobox item")

## tabs

### Roles and attributes

- Given a tab list, when rendered, then the selected tab has `aria-selected="true"` and its panel is visible while the others' panels are not. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tab/test.ts`: "default selected tab")
- Given a tab that becomes the active item through `setSelectedId`, when it is selected, then it has `aria-selected="true"`, carries `data-active-item`, and does not have `tabindex="-1"`, so it is the tab list's tab stop. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tab-select-6346/test-chrome-firefox.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/tab-select-6346/test.ts`: "activates the tab selected by setSelectedId after the popover opens", "activates the tab selected by setSelectedId after the popover toggles")
- Given a tab panel with no tabbable children, when rendered, then it has `tabindex="0"`; a panel that contains tabbable children has no `tabindex` at all. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tab-panel-5692/test-browser.ts`: "panel without tabbable children is focusable", "panel with tabbable children is not focusable after selection")
- Given a panel whose content is unmounted while hidden, when it is selected, then its tabbable children are detected and it drops its `tabindex`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tab-panel-5692/test-browser.ts`: "unmountOnHide panel detects tabbable children on selection")
- Given switching between a tab whose panel has a link and one whose panel is plain text, when the selection changes, then the panel gains `tabindex="0"` when it loses tabbable content and drops it when it gains some; Tab then focuses the panel in the first case and skips it in the second. The browser copy asserts only that focus skips the panel, because Safari skips links when tabbing. ### Notes and edge cases

- Given tab panels whose scroll container is the panel itself, a child of it, or its parent, and with scroll restoration enabled either normally, with `unmountOnHide`, or in single-panel mode, when a panel is scrolled, another tab is selected, and the first is selected again, then the scroll position is restored exactly. Given the matching reset variants, the position returns to `[0, 0]`. This is a 36-case matrix. Chromium and Firefox only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/tab-panel-scroll-restoration/test-chrome-firefox.ts`: "Restore scroll on Default 1" through "Reset scroll on ParentSingleReset 2")
