## portal

### Roles and attributes

- Given a `Portal`, when it renders, then its content appears in the document and is removed when the portal unmounts, coming back when it remounts. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/portal-core-rendering/test.ts`: "renders detached content and removes it when unmounted")
- Given a lazily loaded component inside a portal, when it resolves, then its content appears. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/portal-core-rendering/test.ts`: "renders a lazy component through a portal")

- Given a `Portal`, when it renders, then its content is mounted into the portal root rather than in place; several `Portal` elements can coexist, and multiple portals can render at the same time. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/portal/portal.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/portal/portal.test.ts`: "should be possible to use a Portal", "should be possible to use multiple Portal elements", "should be possible to render multiple portals at the same time")
- Given a `Portal.Group` (Vue `PortalGroup`) with a target, when a portal renders inside it, then the content is forced into that element. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/portal/portal.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/portal/portal.test.ts`: "should be possible to force the Portal into a specific element using Portal.Group", "should be possible to force the Portal into a specific element using PortalGroup")

### Focus management

- Given a dialog with an inline (newly identified on every render) `portalRef`, when text is typed into a field inside it, then the whole string lands in the field and focus stays there, because the portal node is not recreated per keystroke. The same holds for a plain portal. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/portal-dialog-6322/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/portal-dialog-6322/test.ts`: "typing into a dialog with an inline portalRef keeps focus and value", "typing into a portal with an inline portalRef keeps focus and value")

### Dismissal and layering

- Given a document whose `defaultView` is shadowed by a named element, when a portal renders while the page is in fullscreen, then the portal node still lands inside the fullscreen element, and selecting a combobox item works without a page error. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/portal-combobox-7218/test-browser.ts`: "renders a portal inside fullscreen when defaultView is named", "selects a combobox item when defaultView is named")

### SSR and hydration

- Given a `Portal` rendered on the server, when SSR runs, then it does not error. [vue only] (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/portal/portal.test.ts`: "SSR-rendering a Portal should not error")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a `portal` prop that is toggled off, when the content moves back in place, then the `portalRef` cleanup ran while the node was still connected to the DOM, and a new inline `portalRef` is not attached to the removed node. Chromium only for the browser copy. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/portal-toggle-ref-cleanup/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/portal-toggle-ref-cleanup/test.ts`: "detaches portalRef before removing the node when the portal prop is toggled off", "does not attach an inline portalRef to the removed node when the portal prop is toggled off")

- Given the last `Portal` unmounting, when it does, then the portal root element is cleaned up. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/portal/portal.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/portal/portal.test.ts`: "should cleanup the Portal root when the last Portal is unmounted")
- Given external code that tampers with the portal root, when a portal re-renders, then the root is restored correctly. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/portal/portal.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/portal/portal.test.ts`: "should be possible to tamper with the modal root and restore correctly")

## focusable

### Roles and attributes

- Given a `Focusable` rendered as a textarea, when inspected, then it keeps `tagName` TEXTAREA and its `placeholder`, and Tab focus gives it `data-focus-visible="true"`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/focusable-textarea-semantics/test.ts`: "preserves textarea semantics and keyboard focus visibility")

### Pointer

- Given a button, checkbox, radio, submit input, or a checkbox wrapped in another element, when it is clicked, then it receives focus; clicking a checkbox's or radio's label also focuses the control. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/focusable-click-focus/test-browser.ts`: "button receives focus on click", "checkbox receives focus on click", "radio receives focus on click", "checkbox receives focus on label click", "radio receives focus on label click", "submit input receives focus on click", "wrapped checkbox receives focus on click", "wrapped checkbox receives focus on label click")
- Given a plain `Focusable` (not a composite) clicked with the pointer so it has no `data-focus-visible`, when Alt+ArrowDown is pressed, then it gains `data-focus-visible="true"`, so the modality rule is not composite-specific. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/focusable-click-focus/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/focusable-click-focus/test.ts`: "shows focus-visible on a modified navigation key")
- Given an enabled link and an enabled tab rendered as a link, when they are middle-clicked, then the destination opens (in a new tab on Chromium and Firefox, in the current one on WebKit, which the test races). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/focusable-tab-7153/test-browser.ts`: "middle click opens an enabled link", "middle click opens an enabled tab rendered as a link")
- Given a truly disabled link, when it is middle-clicked, then nothing opens, because `pointer-events: none` keeps the gesture from ever reaching it (which is why that case has no hit-target pin). Given an accessibly disabled link or a disabled tab rendered as a link, when middle-clicked (hovered first to keep Playwright's hit-target check honest), then nothing opens and the URL is unchanged. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/focusable-tab-7153/test-browser.ts`: "middle click does not open a disabled link", "middle click does not open an accessible disabled link", "middle click does not open a disabled tab rendered as a link")
- Given the happy-dom copy of the same fixture, when an element is middle-clicked, then a capture-phase `auxclick` listener records exactly one event landing on the element, and its `defaultPrevented` flag says whether activation would have run: true for the enabled link and tab, false for the accessibly disabled link and the disabled tab. The truly disabled link is browser-only because `pointer-events: none` keeps the event away. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/focusable-tab-7153/test.ts`: "middle click activates an enabled link", "middle click activates an enabled tab rendered as a link", "middle click does not activate an accessible disabled link", "middle click does not activate a disabled tab rendered as a link")

### Focus management

- Given a tooltip anchor and a click that drops keyboard modality, when Option+Tab focuses the anchor (the way Safari moves focus when the macOS keyboard navigation setting is off), then the anchor gets `data-focus-visible="true"` and its tooltip shows; clicking the anchor instead leaves `data-focus-visible` absent. WebKit only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/focusable-tooltip-7094/test-safari.ts`: "Option+Tab focuses the anchor as keyboard navigation", "clicking the anchor is still pointer navigation")

## focus-trap

### Keyboard

- Given a region with `FocusTrap` sentinel elements, when Tab walks through it, then the sentinels participate in the tab order (Before, Trap, After in document order). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/focus-trap-elements/test.ts`: "focus trap elements participate in tab order")
- Given `FocusTrap` elements that redirect focus, when Tab reaches one, then focus lands on the redirect target, and Shift+Tab from there lands on the element the redirect skipped. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/focus-trap-elements/test.ts`: "focus trap elements can redirect focus")
- Given a region whose trap is enabled by a checkbox, when Tab walks past the last focusable element inside it, then focus wraps around to the trap toggle; disabling the trap lets Tab continue out to the element after the region. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/focus-trap-navigation/test.ts`: "traps and releases focus in a region")
- Given standalone sentinels around a single button, when Tab and Shift+Tab are pressed, then focus cycles between the toggle and the button; after the trap is disabled, Tab escapes forwards and Shift+Tab walks back out through the toggle to the element before the region. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/focus-trap-navigation/test.ts`: "traps and releases focus with standalone sentinels")
- Given a trap whose first tabbable element holds focus, when Shift+Tab is pressed, then focus wraps to the last tabbable element in the region. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/focus-trap-region/test-browser.ts`: "wraps backward from the first tabbable element")
- Given a trap containing exactly one tabbable element, when Tab or Shift+Tab is pressed, then focus stays on that element. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/focus-trap-region/test-browser.ts`: "keeps focus on a single tabbable element")
- Given an empty but explicitly focusable trapped region, when Tab reaches it, then the region element itself takes focus. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/focus-trap-region/test-browser.ts`: "keeps focus on an explicitly focusable empty region")
- Given the trap's `enabled` flag toggled from a checkbox inside the region, when Space toggles it repeatedly, then focus stays on the checkbox throughout, and Shift+Tab afterwards still wraps to the last element in the region. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/focus-trap-region/test-browser.ts`: "keeps focus when enabled changes inside the region")

### Focus management

- Given a `FocusTrap`, when it mounts, then focus lands on the first focusable element inside it; an `autoFocus` element wins over that; an `initialFocus` element wins over the first focusable one and over an `autoFocus` element. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/focus-trap/focus-trap.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/focus-trap/focus-trap.test.ts`: "should focus the first focusable element inside the FocusTrap", "should focus the autoFocus element inside the FocusTrap if that exists", "should focus the initialFocus element inside the FocusTrap if that exists", "should focus the initialFocus element inside the FocusTrap even if another element has autoFocus")
- Given a `FocusTrap` with no focusable element inside, when it mounts, then a warning is emitted. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/focus-trap/focus-trap.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/focus-trap/focus-trap.test.ts`: "should warn when there is no focusable element inside the FocusTrap")
- Given a `FocusTrap` that unmounts, when it does, then the element focused before entering it is restored. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/focus-trap/focus-trap.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/focus-trap/focus-trap.test.ts`: "should restore the previously focused element, before entering the FocusTrap, after the FocusTrap unmounts")
- Given a trap with exactly one focusable element, when Tab or Shift+Tab is pressed, then focus stays inside. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/focus-trap/focus-trap.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/focus-trap/focus-trap.test.ts`: "should stay in the FocusTrap when using `tab`, if there is only 1 focusable element", "should stay in the FocusTrap when using `shift+tab`, if there is only 1 focusable element")
- Given several focusable elements, when Tab and Shift+Tab are pressed, then focus moves to the next and previous one within the trap. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/focus-trap/focus-trap.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/focus-trap/focus-trap.test.ts`: "should be possible tab to the next focusable element within the focus trap", "should be possible shift+tab to the previous focusable element within the focus trap", "should be possible to tab to the next focusable element within the focus trap", "should be possible to shift+tab to the previous focusable element within the focus trap")
- Given hidden or disabled elements inside the trap, when focus moves, then the initial hidden elements are skipped, later hidden elements are skipped, and disabled elements are skipped. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/focus-trap/focus-trap.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/focus-trap/focus-trap.test.ts`: "should skip the initial "hidden" elements within the focus trap", "should be possible skip "hidden" elements within the focus trap", "should be possible skip disabled elements within the focus trap")
- Given unusual `tabIndex` values inside the trap, when Tab is pressed, then focus cannot escape it. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/focus-trap/focus-trap.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/focus-trap/focus-trap.test.ts`: "should not be possible to escape the FocusTrap due to strange tabIndex usage")
- Given a programmatic `focus()` call on an element outside the trap, when it runs, then focus is pulled back inside, whether or not the trap holds a single focusable element. In React all three of these are `it.skip` (disabled); Vue runs the general case. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/focus-trap/focus-trap.test.tsx`: "should not be possible to programmatically escape the focus trap (if there is only 1 focusable element)" [skipped], "should not be possible to programmatically escape the focus trap" [skipped, twice]; `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/focus-trap/focus-trap.test.ts`: "should not be possible to programmatically escape the focus trap")

## command

### Roles and attributes

- Given a `Command` rendered as a non-button element, when inspected, then it has `role="button"` and `tabindex="0"` and is reachable by Tab. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/command-activation/test.ts`: "renders an accessible command in the tab order")

### Keyboard

- Given a default `Command`, when Enter or Space is pressed, then it activates once per press. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/command-activation/test.ts`: "activates the default command with Enter and Space")
- Given a `Command` with `clickOnEnter` disabled, when Enter is pressed, then nothing activates, while Space still does; with `clickOnSpace` disabled the mirror holds. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/command-activation/test.ts`: "disables only Enter activation", "disables only Space activation")
- Given a non-native `Command` rendered as a div, when Space is held, then it gains `data-active`, and the state is cleared on release even when Meta is held during the release, when the element disables itself mid-press, when a consumer's `onKeyUp` calls `preventDefault`, or when focus leaves the element while Space is still held. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/command-press-state/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/command-press-state/test.ts`: "releasing Space with Meta held clears data-active", "releasing Space clears data-active when the element becomes disabled mid-press", "data-active is cleared when a consumer onKeyUp prevents the default", "data-active is cleared when focus leaves while Space is held")
- Given a non-native `Command` card holding Space when focus moves to a nested button, when the keyup fires on the button and bubbles through the card, then the card does not dispatch a synthetic click on itself (the click counter stays at 0) and its `data-active` is cleared. The browser test also asserts the nested button's own count, because `press.up` in happy-dom synthesizes a click on any focused native button regardless of where the keydown happened. The browser test moves focus by script rather than Tab because WebKit skips native buttons when tabbing under default macOS keyboard settings. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/command-press-state/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/command-press-state/test.ts`: "Space keyup bubbling from a child does not click the command")
- Given a `Command`, when Enter or Space activates it, then the dispatched click is a `PointerEvent` with `pointerId -1` and `pointerType ""`, built by the element's own window, with its own `view` and `composed: true`. Enter comes from the keydown handler and Space from the keyup handler, which are separate code paths. The iframe-realm half is browser-only because happy-dom shares constructors between a frame and its parent. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/command-keyboard-click/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/command-keyboard-click/test.ts`: "Enter dispatches a PointerEvent with no pointer behind it", "Space dispatches a PointerEvent with no pointer behind it", "Enter inside a frame dispatches an event built by the frame's window", "Space inside a frame dispatches an event built by the frame's window", "Enter dispatches a click with its own view that is composed", "Space inside a frame dispatches a click with its own view that is composed")
- Given a `Command` inside a shadow root, when Enter or Space activates it, then the click crosses the shadow boundary and the outer listener counts it. Browser-only, because happy-dom does not reliably reproduce the React portal propagation path. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/command-keyboard-click/test-browser.ts`: "keyboard clicks cross a shadow boundary")

## role

### Roles and attributes

- Given the native `Role` helpers, when rendered, then each produces its native element with props and refs forwarded: `KBD` with a `title`, `HR` with an `aria-label`, `time` with a `datetime`, `TD` with a `colspan`, `fieldset` with `disabled`, and `option` with a `value`; the collected refs report `kbd, hr, time, td, fieldset, option`. Chromium only for the browser copy. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/role-7455/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/role-7455/test.ts`: "renders native Role helpers and forwards refs and props")
- Given a `Role` with a `render` replacement, when rendered, then the replacement element wins (a `SPAN` with its own `title`), the wrapping group still contains it, and the composed ref reports `span`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/role-7455/test-chrome.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/role-7455/test.ts`: "preserves render replacement and framework wrapping")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a `render` prop object with an own `__proto__` key, when the parent re-renders with a fresh payload, then the element is not remounted and the typed input keeps its value. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/role-merge-props-7059/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/role-merge-props-7059/test.ts`: "an own **proto** render prop does not remount the element")
- Given Ariakit React components whose optional props are passed as explicit `undefined`, when they render, then the computed defaults survive: a hovercard's `autoFocusOnShow` stays off, a tab panel stays out of the tab order, Enter stays inert on a native checkbox, a composed hook's later computed default keeps focus on the combobox, a dialog hook and a toolbar-container hook keep their computed `aria-disabled="true"`, a form checkbox keeps `name="newsletter"`, a composed form radio keeps `name="plan"`, and a hook's own undefined sentinel still suppresses a later computed `aria-labelledby`. Explicitly provided values still override the computed defaults in each case. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/react-components-undefined-props/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/react-components-undefined-props/test.ts`: "forwarded undefined autoFocusOnShow keeps focus outside the hovercard", "forwarded undefined focusable keeps the tab panel out of the tab order", "forwarded undefined clickOnEnter keeps Enter inert on a native checkbox", "explicit autoFocusOnShow still overrides the computed default", "explicit focusable still overrides the computed default", "explicit clickOnEnter still overrides the computed default", "a composed hook preserves a later computed default", "a dialog hook preserves its computed disabled state", "a toolbar container hook preserves its computed disabled state", "a form checkbox preserves its field name and external label", "a composed form radio preserves its field name", "a hook's own undefined sentinel still suppresses a later computed value")
- Given a `useStoreRef`-style ref holding a function value, when it is replaced and then restored to its initial value, then the stored value type stays `function` and the restored default behaves like the original. Chromium and Firefox for the browser copy. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/create-ref-6349/test-chrome-firefox.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/create-ref-6349/test.ts`: "resets a function-typed ref to its initial value")
- Given a callback queued with `queueBeforeEvent` and then canceled, when the next event of that type fires, then the canceled callback does not run and the hint region stays pinned. Chromium and Firefox for the browser copy. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/queue-before-event-6350/test-chrome-firefox.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/queue-before-event-6350/test.ts`: "canceling a queued callback keeps it from running on the next event")
- Given a Next.js counter island, when the button is clicked, then the count increments. Chromium only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/counter-nextjs/test-chrome.ts`: "increment count")

## collection

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a collection, when items register, then the uncontrolled store reports 3 items, a controlled store reports 3, and a provider-controlled one reports 3. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/collection-registration/test.ts`: "registers uncontrolled items", "reports controlled store items", "reports controlled provider items")
- Given a `getItem` customization, when an item registers, then the customized item is counted (1). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/collection-registration/test.ts`: "customizes a registered item with getItem")
- Given an item whose registration is disabled, when the collection is read, then that item is excluded (2 of 3 registered). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/collection-registration/test.ts`: "excludes an item when registration is disabled")

### Positioning

- Given a measured renderer and a fixed-size renderer over the same data, when both render, then their item offsets agree with the fixed-size formula `paddingStart + itemSize * index + gap * index` (20px, 62px) and both containers report the same total height (366px). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/collection-renderer-6337/test-browser.ts`: "measured and fixed renderers agree on offsets and total height")

## accessibility-assertions

### Roles and attributes

- Every assertion helper takes the element as an optional last argument and falls back to a document-wide query, so a conformance suite must be able to find each part by role or by id prefix alone. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- Every assertion helper short-circuits with an "element is not null" expectation when the element it was handed (or found) is missing, so a missing element is reported as a missing element rather than as a failed attribute check. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- Every assertion helper wraps its body in try/catch and rewrites the error stack to start at the assertion call site, so failures point at the test line, not inside the helper. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- Almost every assertion accepts an `attributes` bag of name/value pairs and checks each one with an exact attribute match, which is how callers pin `data-headlessui-state`, `data-open`, `data-active`, `data-focus`, `data-hover`, `data-disabled`, `data-selected`, `data-autofocus`, `data-slot` and `aria-*` values; the helpers themselves hard-code no `data-*` expectation except the checkbox ones. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- A null value in the `attributes` bag means the attribute must be absent, since the underlying matcher treats a null expected value as "not present". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- Almost every assertion accepts an optional `textContent` string and, when given, requires the element's text content to contain it (substring match, not equality); the exception is `assertTabs`, which compares text content with strict equality. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- Several assertions accept an optional `tag` string and require the element's lowercased tag name to equal it: `assertMenuItem`, `assertComboboxOption`, `assertComboboxLabel`, `assertListboxOption`, `assertListboxLabel`, `assertSwitch`. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `getLabel` returns the first `label` element or the first element whose id starts with `headlessui-label-`; `getLabels` returns all of them. [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `getDescription` returns the first element whose id starts with `headlessui-description-`; `getDescriptions` returns all of them. [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `getControl` returns the first element whose id starts with `headlessui-control-`, which is the id prefix the `Field` control slot uses. [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `getInput`, `getSelect` and `getTextarea` return the first `input`, `select` and `textarea` element in the document. [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `getCheckbox` returns the first `input[type="checkbox"]` or the first element with `role="checkbox"`, so both the native and the headless checkbox resolve through one getter. [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `CheckboxState` has three members: `Checked`, `Unchecked`, `Indeterminate`. [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `assertCheckbox` in the `Checked` state requires `aria-checked="true"`, `role="checkbox"`, `tabindex="0"` and the presence of a `data-checked` attribute (value not checked), then applies the `attributes` bag. [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `assertCheckbox` in the `Unchecked` state requires `aria-checked="false"`, `role="checkbox"` and `tabindex="0"`, and does not check for any `data-*` attribute, then applies the `attributes` bag. [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `assertCheckbox` in the `Indeterminate` state requires `aria-checked="mixed"`, an `indeterminate="true"` attribute, `role="checkbox"`, `tabindex="0"` and the presence of a `data-indeterminate` attribute, then applies the `attributes` bag. [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `assertLinkedWithLabel` requires the element to have an `aria-labelledby` attribute and requires the whitespace-split id set to contain the id of every label passed (a single label or an array). [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `assertNotLinkedWithLabel` requires the element's whitespace-split `aria-labelledby` id set to contain none of the given label ids, and tolerates the attribute being absent entirely. [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `assertLinkedWithDescription` requires the element to have an `aria-describedby` attribute and requires the whitespace-split id set to contain the id of every description passed. [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `getMenuButton` returns the first `button`, `[role="button"]`, or element whose id starts with `headlessui-menu-button-`; `getMenuButtons` returns every `button` and `[role="button"]`. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)

### Focus management

- `assertActiveElement` requires the given element to be the active element, and on failure retries the comparison against `outerHTML` strings, because a direct object comparison can crash jsdom with "Cannot assign to read only property Symbol(impl) of object DOMImplementation". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `assertActiveElement` resolves the active element through the element's root node in React, so shadow-DOM hosts resolve correctly, while Vue reads `document.activeElement` directly. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `assertContainsActiveElement` requires the given element to contain the active element, so focus may sit on a descendant; React resolves the active element through the root node, Vue through `document.activeElement`. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `assertFocusable` requires the element to match the library's own focusable selector in `FocusableMode.Strict`, so the element itself must be focusable, not merely inside something focusable. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `assertNotFocusable` requires the element to fail the strict focusable check; `document.body` always counts as not focusable. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `assertActiveListboxOption(item, listbox = getListbox())` asserts that the listbox element carries `aria-activedescendant` equal to the given option's `id`, which is how a virtual-focus listbox marks its active option. It bails out with a null check when either the listbox or the option is missing. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts`)
- `assertNoActiveListboxOption(listbox = getListbox())` asserts that the listbox element has no `aria-activedescendant` attribute at all, which is the required state for an open listbox with nothing active. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts`)
- `assertActiveComboboxOption(item, combobox = getComboboxInput())` asserts that the combobox INPUT (not the list) carries `aria-activedescendant` equal to the given option's `id`, so the active option is advertised from the input while DOM focus stays there. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts`)
- `assertNotActiveComboboxOption(item, combobox = getComboboxInput())` asserts the inverse for one specific option: the input's `aria-activedescendant` is not that option's `id`. It is distinct from the no-active assertion because the attribute may still point at a different option. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts`)
- `assertNoActiveComboboxOption(combobox = getComboboxInput())` asserts that the combobox input has no `aria-activedescendant` attribute at all. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts`)
- All five active-option helpers rewrite the thrown error's stack with `Error.captureStackTrace` so a failure points at the calling test rather than at the helper, and all five are byte-identical between the React and Vue files. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts`)

### Dismissal and layering

- `assertInert` requires both `aria-hidden="true"` and a DOM `inert` property of exactly `true`, which is how the suites check that the rest of the page is neutralised behind a modal. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `assertNotInert` only requires the `inert` property to be `undefined` and deliberately does not require `aria-hidden` to be absent, because a non-inert element can legitimately still be aria-hidden. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)

### Animation and presence

- `assertHidden` requires both a `hidden` attribute and a computed `display: none`, so hiding by attribute alone or by style alone fails. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `assertVisible` requires the absence of a `hidden` attribute and requires the computed style not to be `display: none`. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- Every component state enum (`MenuState`, `ComboboxState`, `ListboxState`, `DisclosureState`, `PopoverState`, `DialogState`) uses the same three-value shape, where `Visible` means shown, `InvisibleHidden` means present in the DOM but hidden (the `static`/`unmount={false}` case) and `InvisibleUnmounted` means the node is absent, which is how the suites distinguish unmount-on-close from hide-on-close. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)

### Accessibility tooling

- `assertLabelValue` resolves the accessible name in a fixed order and stops at the first source found: `aria-labelledby` (join the text content of every referenced id with a single space and compare for equality), then `aria-label` (exact attribute match), then a `[for="<element id>"]` element (text-content containment), then the element's own text content (containment). (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `assertDescriptionValue` reads the whole `aria-describedby` attribute as a single id and requires that element's text content to equal the expected value exactly, so it cannot verify a multi-id describedby. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `assertDisabledish` passes when either `disabled` or `aria-disabled` is present with the value `"true"` or the empty string, and throws "Expected element to be disabledish" otherwise, which lets one assertion cover native and aria disabling. [react only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- `getByText` walks the document body with a TreeWalker over elements, skips any element that has element children, and returns the first leaf element whose text content equals the query exactly, or null. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)

## switch

### Roles and attributes

- Given a controlled Switch with checked=true and a render-prop child, when it renders, then the element has role="switch", aria-checked="true", a tabindex of 0 or higher, and the child gets checked=true so the text reads "On". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should be possible to render an (on) Switch using a render prop")
- Given a controlled Switch with checked=false and a render-prop child, when it renders, then the element has role="switch", aria-checked="false", and the child gets checked=false so the text reads "Off". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should be possible to render an (off) Switch using a render prop")
- Given a Switch with as="span" and checked=true, when it renders, then the rendered tag is span and it still carries role="switch" and aria-checked="true". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should be possible to render an (on) Switch using an `as` prop")
- Given a Switch with as="span" and checked=false, when it renders, then the rendered tag is span with role="switch" and aria-checked="false". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should be possible to render an (off) Switch using an `as` prop")
- Given a Switch whose children are a span with text "Enable notifications", when it renders, then the switch's accessible label resolves to that text through aria-labelledby, aria-label or a for-attribute label. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should be possible to use the switch contents as the label")
- Given a Switch with children and no tabIndex prop (React) or an explicit :tabIndex="0" (Vue), when it renders, then tabindex is "0". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should have a default tabIndex of `0`")
- Given a Switch with tabIndex={3}, when it renders, then tabindex is "3", so a positive user value wins. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should be possible to override the `tabIndex`")
- Given a Switch with tabIndex={-1}, when it renders, then tabindex is forced back to "0" so the switch stays reachable by Tab. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should not be possible to override the `tabIndex` to `-1`")
- Given a Switch rendered as its default button element, when it renders, then it gets type="button". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should set the `type` to "button" by default")
- Given a Switch with type="submit", when it renders, then the type stays "submit" and is not overwritten. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should not set the `type` to "button" if it already contains a `type`")
- Given a Switch with as={CustomButton} where the custom component renders a button, when it renders (Vue after one animation frame), then type="button" is applied to the resolved button. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should set the `type` to "button" when using the `as` prop which resolves to a "button"")
- Given a Switch with as="div", when it renders, then no type attribute is added. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should not set the type if the "as" prop is not a "button"")
- Given a Switch with as={CustomButton} where the custom component renders a div, when it renders (Vue after one animation frame), then no type attribute is added. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should not set the `type` to "button" when using the `as` prop which resolves to a "div"")
- Given a SwitchGroup containing a Switch and a SwitchLabel, when it renders, then the switch is labelled by the SwitchLabel's id and the label text resolves to "Enable notifications". - Given a SwitchGroup with a SwitchDescription rendered before the Switch, when it renders, then the switch's aria-describedby points at the description whose text is "This is an important feature". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should be possible to render a Switch.Group, Switch and Switch.Description (before the Switch)")

- Given a SwitchGroup with a SwitchLabel and a SwitchDescription around a Switch, when it renders, then the switch is both labelled by "Label A" and described by "This is an important feature". - Given a SwitchLabel with class="abc", when it renders, then the label keeps that class and still labels the switch. [vue only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should be possible to put classes on a SwitchLabel")
- Given a SwitchDescription with class="abc", when it renders, then the description keeps that class and still describes the switch. [vue only] (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should be possible to put classes on a SwitchDescription")

### Keyboard

- Given a focused controlled Switch that is off, when Space is pressed, then aria-checked flips to "true", and pressing Space again flips it back to "false". - Given a checked Switch with name="option" inside a form that also has a submit button, when the switch is focused and Enter is pressed, then the form is submitted exactly once with the entries [['option', 'on']]. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should submit the form on `Enter`")
- Given a checked Switch with name="option" inside a form with no submit button at all, when the switch is focused and Enter is pressed, then the form is still submitted once with [['option', 'on']]. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should submit the form on `Enter` (when no submit button was found)")

(headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should be possible to tab away from the Switch")

### Pointer

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given an uncontrolled Switch with name="notifications" in a form, when the form is submitted before any interaction, then the payload is empty; after clicking the switch it submits { notifications: 'on' }, and after clicking again the key disappears from the payload. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should be possible to use in an uncontrolled way")

### Forms

- Given a Switch with form="my-form" and name="notifications" rendered outside a form element that has id="my-form", when the switch is toggled through its label and that external form is submitted, then the payload is [['notifications', 'on']], so the hidden input is associated by form id. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should be possible to set the `form`, which is forwarded to the hidden inputs")

(headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should be possible to submit a form with an boolean value")
- Given a controlled Switch with name="fruit" value="apple" inside a form, when the form is submitted while off, then the payload is empty, and after toggling it on the payload is [['fruit', 'apple']]. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should be possible to submit a form with a provided string value")
- Given a checked but disabled Switch with name="fruit" value="apple" next to a hidden input foo=bar, when the form is submitted, then only [['foo', 'bar']] is sent, so a disabled switch contributes no form data. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should not submit the data if the Switch is disabled")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a bare controlled Switch with checked={false} and an onChange handler, when it is rendered, then nothing throws. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/switch/switch.test.tsx: "should be possible to render a Switch without crashing")

## field

### Roles and attributes

- Given a Field wrapping an input, when it renders, then the Field element does not have aria-disabled="true". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should render a `Field` component")
- Given a Field with a render-prop child, when it renders, then the slot serializes to { disabled: false } and the Field element has no aria-disabled="true". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should render a `Field` component with a render prop")
- Given a Field with the disabled prop, when it renders, then the Field element has aria-disabled="true". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should add `aria-disabled` when a `Field` is disabled")
- Given a Field nested inside a disabled Fieldset, when they render, then the fieldset has the disabled attribute and the Field picks up aria-disabled="true" from context. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/field/field.test.tsx: "should inherit the `disabled` state from a parent `Fieldset`")
- Given a Fieldset with default rendering, when it renders, then the element is an HTMLFieldSetElement and it does not get role="group" because the native element already implies it. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should render a `Fieldset` component")
- Given a Fieldset with as="span", when it renders, then the element is an HTMLSpanElement and role="group" is added. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should render a `Fieldset` using a custom component")
- Given a Fieldset with the disabled prop rendered as a native fieldset, when it renders, then the element has the native disabled attribute. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should forward the `disabled` attribute when disabling the `Fieldset`")
- Given a disabled Fieldset with as="span", when it renders, then the element gets aria-disabled="true" instead of the native disabled attribute. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should add an `aria-disabled` attribute when disabling the `Fieldset` when using another element via the `as` prop")
- Given a disabled Fieldset wrapping a plain input, when it renders, then the nested input is itself disabled. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should make nested inputs disabled when the fieldset is disabled")
- Given a Fieldset containing a Legend and an input, when it renders, then the fieldset's aria-labelledby contains the Legend's id. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should link a `Fieldset` to a nested `Legend`")
- Given a Fieldset with a Legend plus a Field containing a Label and an Input, when they render, then the fieldset is labelled only by the Legend and the input is labelled only by the Label. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should not link a `Label` inside a `Field` to the `Fieldset`")
- Given the same Fieldset, Legend, Field, Label and Input tree, when it renders, then the fieldset's aria-labelledby does not contain the Label's id and the input's aria-labelledby does not contain the Legend's id. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should not link a `Label` inside a `Field` to the `Fieldset`")
- Given the same tree, when it renders, then the Field element itself is not labelled by either the Legend or the Label. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/fieldset/fieldset.test.tsx: "should not link a `Label` inside a `Field` to the `Fieldset`")

## label

### Roles and attributes

- Given a component that calls useLabels and spreads the returned id onto aria-labelledby but renders no Label, when it renders, then no aria-labelledby attribute appears at all and the snapshot is just the wrapper with its text. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/label/label.test.tsx: "should be possible to use a LabelProvider without using a Label", packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/label/label.test.ts: "should be possible to use useLabels without using a Label")
- Given a LabelProvider (Vue: useLabels) with one Label child, when it renders, then the wrapper gets aria-labelledby="headlessui-label-1" and the label element gets that same generated id; React renders the label as a div with an empty data-headlessui-state, Vue renders a native label element. ## input

### Roles and attributes

- Given an Input inside a disabled Field, when it renders, then the input is disabled-ish, carrying either disabled or aria-disabled="true". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/input/input.test.tsx: "should mark the control as disabled, if the `Field` is disabled")
- Given an Input and a Label inside the same Field, when they render, then the input's aria-labelledby contains the label's id. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/input/input.test.tsx: "should link a control and a `Label` when inside a `Field`")
- Given an Input and two Label components inside one Field, when they render, then the input's aria-labelledby lists both label ids. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/input/input.test.tsx: "should link a control and multiple `Label` components when inside a `Field`")
- Given an Input and a Description inside one Field, when they render, then the input's aria-describedby contains the description's id. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/input/input.test.tsx: "should link a control and a `Description` when inside a `Field`")
- Given an Input and three Description components inside one Field, when they render, then aria-describedby lists all three description ids. - Given an Input with both a Label and a Description in one Field, when they render, then aria-labelledby points at the label and aria-describedby at the description. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/input/input.test.tsx: "should link a control with a `Label` and a `Description` when inside a `Field`")

- Given an `@ariakit/ui` field, when it renders, then each hint and error message is linked to its field, a field is named from the label wrapping it, a disabled field is disabled, a key hint is kept out of the search trigger's name, and a share link stays read-only. ## render-props

### Roles and attributes

- Given a component whose slot is { a: true, b: false, c: true } and a render-prop child, when it renders, then the element gets data-a="" and data-c="" for the true entries, the false entry produces no attribute, and data-headlessui-state is the space separated list "a c". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/render.test.tsx: "should forward boolean values from `slot` as data attributes")
- Given a slot of { accept: true } rendered as a Fragment whose single child already has data-accept="always", when it renders, then the child keeps data-accept="always" and still gets data-headlessui-state="accept", so a user supplied data attribute wins over the generated one. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/render.test.tsx: "should prefer user provided data attributes over the ones we set automatically")
- Given a Vue component rendered with as="div" and slot { active: true, selected: true }, when it renders, then the element has data-headlessui-state="active selected". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-vue/src/utils/render.test.ts: "as=element")
- Given a Vue component rendered with as="template", class="abc" and slot { active: true, selected: true }, when it renders, then the single child gets both class "abc" and data-headlessui-state="active selected"; the test notes that removing class="abc" makes the state assertion fail. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-vue/src/utils/render.test.ts: "as=template")
- Given the Tailwind plugin and the class ui-open:underline, when Tailwind compiles, then it emits both a self rule `.ui-open\:underline[data-headlessui-state~="open"]` and an ancestor rule `:where([data-headlessui-state~="open"]) .ui-open\:underline`, so any state word in data-headlessui-state becomes a ui-* variant that matches the element itself or any ancestor. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-tailwindcss/src/index.test.ts: "should generate css for an exposed state")
- Given the class ui-not-open:underline, when Tailwind compiles, then it emits `.ui-not-open\:underline[data-headlessui-state]:not([data-headlessui-state~="open"])` plus an ancestor form `:where([data-headlessui-state]:not([data-headlessui-state~="open"])) .ui-not-open\:underline:not([data-headlessui-state])`, so ui-not-* requires a data-headlessui-state to exist but without that word. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-tailwindcss/src/index.test.ts: "should generate the inverse "not" css for an exposed state")
- Given the class ui-focus-visible:underline, when Tailwind compiles, then it emits `:where([data-headlessui-focus-visible]) .ui-focus-visible\:underline:focus`, so the focus ring variant keys off an ancestor's data-headlessui-focus-visible attribute combined with :focus. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-tailwindcss/src/index.test.ts: "should generate the ui-focus-visible variant")
- Given the class ui-not-focus-visible:underline, when Tailwind compiles, then it emits `.ui-not-focus-visible\:underline:focus:where(:not([data-headlessui-focus-visible] .ui-not-focus-visible\:underline))`, matching a focused element that is not inside a data-headlessui-focus-visible ancestor. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-tailwindcss/src/index.test.ts: "should generate the ui-not-focus-visible variant")
- Given the plugin configured with hui({ prefix: 'hui' }) and the class hui-open:underline, when Tailwind compiles, then the same pair of data-headlessui-state rules is emitted under the custom hui- prefix. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-tailwindcss/src/index.test.ts: "should generate css for an exposed state" under describe "custom prefix")
- Given the plugin configured with prefix 'hui' and the class hui-not-open:underline, when Tailwind compiles, then the inverse rules are emitted under the hui-not- prefix. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-tailwindcss/src/index.test.ts: "should generate the inverse "not" css for an exposed state" under describe "custom prefix")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a component built on useRender with defaultTag 'div' and no props, when it renders, then the output is a bare div with no extra attributes. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/render.test.tsx: "should be possible to render a dummy component")
- Given as={Fragment} with className="test-outer" wrapped around a single child that has className="test-inner", when it renders, then the child's class becomes "test-inner test-outer", so Fragment merges the two class lists. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/render.test.tsx: "should be possible to merge classes when rendering")
- Given as={Fragment} with className="test-outer" around a child whose className is the function () => 'test-inner', when it renders, then the function is resolved and the class still merges to "test-inner test-outer". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/render.test.tsx: "should be possible to merge class fns when rendering")
- Given a component whose children is a callback, when it renders, then the callback receives exactly the same slot object the component passed in and its returned span is rendered inside the default div. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/render.test.tsx: "should be possible to render a dummy component with some children as a callback")
- Given ourProps containing a ref and the user passing refName="potato" with as={MyComponent}, when it renders, then the ref is forwarded as a prop named potato instead of ref. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/render.test.tsx: "should be possible to add a ref with a different name")
- Given unknown props a={1} b={2} c={3}, when the component renders, then all three land on the rendered div as attributes a="1" b="2" c="3". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/render.test.tsx: "should be possible to passthrough props to a dummy component")
- Given as="button", when the component renders, then the rendered element is a button instead of the default div. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/render.test.tsx: "should be possible to change the underlying DOM node using the `as` prop")
- Given as="button" together with a function as children, when it renders, then the callback's span is rendered inside the button. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/render.test.tsx: "should be possible to change the underlying DOM node using the `as` prop and still have a function as children")
- Given as={Fragment} with plain text children, when it renders, then only the text appears and no wrapper element is created. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/render.test.tsx: "should be possible to render the children only when the `as` prop is set to Fragment")
- Given as={Fragment} with props a={1} b={1} and a callback child returning a span, when it renders, then both props are forwarded onto that span. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/render.test.tsx: "should forward all the props to the first child when using an as={Fragment}")
- Given as={Fragment} with two span children and no extra props to pass through, when it renders, then both spans render and no error is thrown. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/render.test.tsx: "should not error when we are rendering a Fragment with multiple children when we don't passthrough additional props")
- Given a Vue component with as="template" and class="abc" wrapping a single div, when it renders, then that div gets the class "abc". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-vue/src/utils/render.test.ts: "should forward the props to the first child")
- Given a Vue as="template" component whose child is a functional PassThrough component that itself calls render with as="template", when it renders, then class="abc" still reaches the innermost div#result. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-vue/src/utils/render.test.ts: "should forward the props via Functional Components")
- Given two nested Vue as="template" components with classes "foo" and "bar" and data-test values 123 and 345, whose children come through a <slot />, when they render, then the slotted div gets both foo and bar classes while data-test resolves to the outer "123" (the test leaves a TODO asking whether 345 would be more correct). (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-vue/src/utils/render.test.ts: "should allow use of <slot> as children")

### Animation and presence

- Given RenderFeatures.Static enabled and props show={true} static, when it renders, then the contents are rendered; asserted under both describe "Features.Static" and describe "Features.Static | Features.RenderStrategy". - Given RenderFeatures.RenderStrategy enabled and props show={true} unmount, when it renders, then the div with its contents is present; asserted under both describe "Features.RenderStrategy" and describe "Features.Static | Features.RenderStrategy". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/render.test.tsx: "should be possible to render an `unmount` dummy component (show = true)")
- Given RenderFeatures.RenderStrategy enabled and props show={false} unmount, when it renders, then the wrapper is empty because the element is removed from the DOM; asserted under both describe "Features.RenderStrategy" and describe "Features.Static | Features.RenderStrategy". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/render.test.tsx: "should be possible to render an `unmount` dummy component (show = false)")
- Given RenderFeatures.RenderStrategy enabled and props show={true} unmount={false}, when it renders, then the div with its contents is present and not hidden; asserted under both describe "Features.RenderStrategy" and describe "Features.Static | Features.RenderStrategy". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/render.test.tsx: "should be possible to render an `unmount={false}` dummy component (show = true)")
- Given RenderFeatures.RenderStrategy enabled and props show={false} unmount={false}, when it renders, then the element stays in the DOM but gets hidden="" and style="display: none;"; asserted under both describe "Features.RenderStrategy" and describe "Features.Static | Features.RenderStrategy". (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/render.test.tsx: "should be possible to render an `unmount={false}` dummy component (show = false)")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given as={Fragment} with className="p-12" and two children, when it renders, then it throws an error titled 'Passing props on "Fragment"!' that names the component (<Dummy />), lists the props it needs to pass through (className) and suggests either adding an `as="..."` prop or rendering a single child element. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/render.test.tsx: "should error when we are rendering a Fragment with multiple children")
- Given as={Fragment} with className="p-12" and text children (no element to forward props to), when it renders, then it throws the same 'Passing props on "Fragment"!' error listing className and the two suggested fixes. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/utils/render.test.tsx: "should error when we are applying props to a Fragment when we do not have a dedicated element")
- Given a Vue component with as="template" and class="abc", when it renders, then errorCaptured receives an error titled 'Passing props on "template"!' naming <Dummy />, listing the prop "class" and suggesting an `as="..."` prop or a single child element. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-vue/src/utils/render.test.ts: "should error when using an as="template" with additional props")

## combobox

Environment note for this section: a plain `test.ts` path is Vitest on happy-dom, executed once per framework (React and Solid). Other file names pin the behavior to specific engines and are annotated inline on every bullet: `test-browser.ts` = Playwright on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit; `test-chrome.ts` = Chromium only; `test-chrome-firefox.ts` = Chromium and Firefox only; `test-mobile.ts` = mobile viewport.

### Roles and attributes

- Given the combobox-disclosure sandbox with the popover closed, when the page first renders, then the disclosure button is labelled "Show popup" and has `aria-expanded="false"`. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-disclosure/test.ts: "show and hide popup with disclosure button")
- Given the combobox-disclosure sandbox, when the disclosure button is clicked, then it becomes labelled "Hide popup" and carries `aria-expanded="true"`. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-disclosure/test.ts: "show and hide popup with disclosure button")
- Given an open popover opened from the disclosure, when "Hide popup" is clicked, then the button reverts to "Show popup" with `aria-expanded="false"`. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-disclosure/test.ts: "show and hide popup with disclosure button")
- Given the combobox-disclosure sandbox, when the combobox input itself is clicked, then the separate disclosure button flips to "Hide popup" with `aria-expanded="true"`, so the disclosure reflects store state it did not cause. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-disclosure/test.ts: "show and hide popup with combobox")
- Given a popover opened by clicking the input, when Escape is pressed, then the disclosure button returns to `aria-expanded="false"`. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-disclosure/test.ts: "show and hide popup with combobox")
- Given a `multiple` combobox with a default selection, when the popover is opened, then the option "Bacon" has `aria-selected="true"`. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-multiple/test.ts: "default checked")
- Given an open `multiple` combobox, when "Burger" and "Banana" are clicked, then both options report `aria-selected="true"`. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-multiple/test.ts: "check/uncheck with click")
- Given selected options in a `multiple` combobox, when each selected option is clicked again, then its `aria-selected` becomes `"false"`. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-multiple/test.ts: "check/uncheck with click")
- Given a `multiple` combobox navigated to "Banana" with ArrowDown, when nothing has been chosen yet, then "Banana" has `aria-selected="false"`. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-multiple/test.ts: "check/uncheck with enter")
- Given "Banana" is the active item, when Enter is pressed twice, then `aria-selected` toggles to `"true"` and back to `"false"`. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-multiple/test.ts: "check/uncheck with enter")
- Given a `multiple` combobox filtered by typing "b", when the list re-renders, then the already-selected "Bacon" still carries `aria-selected="true"` inside the filtered list. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-multiple/test.ts: "check/uncheck item after filtering")

- Given the search "ap" in a `multiple` combobox, when ArrowUp then Enter selects "Pineapple", then "Pineapple" reports `aria-selected="true"`. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-multiple/test.ts: "check/uncheck item after filtering")
