- Given an open plain combobox, when the "🍊 Orange" option is clicked, then the input takes focus, holds "Orange", and the listbox unmounts. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox/test.ts`: "set value and hide on item click with mouse")
- Given an open plain combobox, when a point outside is clicked, then the listbox unmounts and the input does not keep focus. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox/test.ts`: "hide listbox by clicking outside")
- Given a plain combobox with an option focused, when the input itself is clicked, then the option loses focus. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox/test.ts`: "clicking on combobox input removes focus from item")
- Given a plain combobox on a mobile viewport, when the input is tapped, then the listbox becomes visible; tapping outside hides it and leaves the input unfocused (mobile viewport). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox/test-mobile.ts`: "show/hide on tap")
- Given a plain combobox on a mobile viewport, when an option is tapped, then the listbox hides and the input is focused (mobile viewport). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox/test-mobile.ts`: "hide when tapping on item")
- Given a plain combobox on a mobile viewport that was opened, dismissed by an outside click, then reopened, when an option is tapped, then the listbox hides and the input is focused (mobile viewport). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox/test-mobile.ts`: "hide when tapping on item after clicking outside")

- Given a `Combobox.Label`, when it is clicked, then the input receives focus (Vue focuses the button); a right click on the label does not focus it. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/combobox/combobox.test.tsx`: "should focus the Combobox.Input when we click the Combobox.Label", "should not focus the Combobox.Input when we right click the Combobox.Label"; `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/combobox/combobox.test.ts`: "should focus the ComboboxButton when we click the ComboboxLabel", "should not focus the ComboboxInput when we right click the ComboboxLabel")
- Given `immediate` mode, when the input receives focus, then the list opens; with `immediate` disabled focusing the input does not open it; with `immediate` enabled but the button disabled it also does not open; and clicking (or clicking while already focused) closes it. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/combobox/combobox.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/combobox/combobox.test.ts`: "should be possible to open the combobox by focusing the input with immediate mode enabled", "should not be possible to open the combobox by focusing the input with immediate mode disabled", "should not be possible to open the combobox by focusing the input with immediate mode enabled when button is disabled", "should be possible to close a combobox on click with immediate mode enabled", "should be possible to close a focused combobox on click with immediate mode enabled")
- Given a closed combobox, when the button is clicked, then the list opens with the selected option active; a right click does not open it; a disabled button does not; clicking again closes it. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/combobox/combobox.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/combobox/combobox.test.ts`: "should be possible to open the combobox on click", "should not be possible to open the combobox on right click", "should not be possible to open the combobox on click when the button is disabled", "should be possible to open the combobox on click, and focus the selected option", "should be possible to close a combobox on click")
- Given a closed combobox, when a click lands outside it, then nothing happens. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/combobox/combobox.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/combobox/combobox.test.ts`: "should be a no-op when we click outside of a closed combobox")
- Given an open combobox, when a click lands outside it, then it closes; this general case is `xit` (disabled) in both frameworks, while the specific variants are enabled: clicking another combobox's button closes this one and opens that one, clicking the combobox's own button closes it, and clicking an element nested inside a focusable element closes it. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/combobox/combobox.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/combobox/combobox.test.ts`: "should be possible to click outside of the combobox which should close the combobox" [skipped], "should be possible to click outside of the combobox on another combobox button which should close the current combobox and open the new combobox", "should be possible to click outside of the combobox which should close the combobox (even if we press the combobox button)", "should be possible to click outside of the combobox, on an element which is within a focusable element, which closes the combobox")
- Given an open combobox, when an option is hovered or the mouse moves over it, then it becomes active (including with `static` options); moving the mouse over an already active or a disabled option is a no-op, a disabled option never becomes active, leaving an option makes it inactive, and leaving a disabled option is a no-op. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/combobox/combobox.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/combobox/combobox.test.ts`: "should be possible to hover an option and make it active", "should be possible to hover an option and make it active when using `static`", "should make a combobox option active when you move the mouse over it", "should be a no-op when we move the mouse and the combobox option is already active", "should be a no-op when we move the mouse and the combobox option is disabled", "should not be possible to hover an option that is disabled", "should be possible to mouse leave an option and make it inactive", "should be possible to mouse leave a disabled option and be a no-op")
- Given an open combobox, when an option is clicked, then the list closes and the value is chosen, including in `immediate` mode; clicking a disabled option is a no-op. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/combobox/combobox.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/combobox/combobox.test.ts`: "should be possible to click a combobox option, which closes the combobox", "should be possible to click a combobox option, which closes the combobox with immediate mode enabled", "should be possible to click a disabled combobox option, which is a no-op")
- Given the `hold` behavior, when the pointer leaves the list, then the last active option is held rather than cleared. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/combobox/combobox.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/combobox/combobox.test.ts`: "should be possible to hold the last active option")

- Given optional hover props, when a suggestion is hovered, then it stays the active item. Chromium and Firefox only. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/ariakit-ui-combobox/test-chrome-firefox.ts`: "keeps the hovered suggestion active with optional hover props")

### Focus management

- Given an `autoSelect` combobox where an option is the active item, when the value is read, then the input keeps DOM focus while the option carries the active-item state, which is the virtual focus contract. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-radix-select/test.ts: "hover over option")
- Given a combobox-select with virtual focus, when ArrowDown moves through options, then DOM focus never leaves the trigger and only `aria-activedescendant` changes. [Chromium, Firefox, WebKit] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-4767/test-browser.ts: "keeps virtual focus on the select while moving through the items")
- Given a combobox-select configured for real focus instead, when it opens, then the selected option takes real DOM focus and the trigger loses it. [Chromium, Firefox, WebKit] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-4767/test-browser.ts: "focuses the selected item when opening in real-focus mode")
- Given a virtualized combobox-select with `autoSelect`, when the popover shrinks because `--popover-available-height` changes the way Floating UI changes it on a visual-viewport resize, then the search input keeps DOM focus, the first option keeps `data-active-item`, and zero `focusin` events land on any option; the bug it pins is Android keyboards resizing the viewport while typing, where every rendered-items change re-ran auto-select, bumped the move counter, and bounced focus off the input, dropping characters. [Chromium only] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-3837/test-browser.ts: "resizing the popover does not bounce focus while auto-selecting")
- Given a combobox-select whose selected option was filtered out, when a Backspace brings it back and it is re-appended to the DOM, then the option does not take focus and the search input keeps it; on iOS Safari an `element.focus()` here would dismiss the keyboard. [Chromium, Firefox, WebKit] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-5047/test-browser.ts: "combobox keeps focus when selected item reappears after filtering")
- Given a combobox where `onFocus` on the input is counted, when six characters are typed, then the count stays at 1, so per-keystroke virtual focus moves do not refire the input's focus handler. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-auto-select-focus/test.ts: "not call the onFocus callback on every key pressed")
- Given the same combobox, when the body is clicked, then the input loses DOM focus, and clicking it again raises the `onFocus` count to exactly 2. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-auto-select-focus/test.ts: "not call the onFocus callback on every key pressed")
- Given a combobox with a separate disclosure button, when text is typed after opening from the disclosure, then the input holds DOM focus. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-disclosure/test.ts: "keep focus on combobox if disclosure button pressed")
- Given an open popover and a focused input, when the "Hide popup" disclosure is clicked, then the input still holds DOM focus after the popover closes. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-disclosure/test.ts: "keep focus on combobox if disclosure button pressed")
- Given a combobox on an `input type="email"`, when "e" is typed and ArrowDown activates an option, then the input keeps DOM focus and no `setSelectionRange` error is thrown, because email inputs do not support selection ranges. [Chromium, Firefox, WebKit] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-input-email/test-browser.ts: "combobox should not throw when input type=email")
- Given a real-focus email combobox where ArrowDown moved DOM focus onto an option, when a printable character "2" is typed, then focus returns to the email input and the value becomes "e2". [Chromium, Firefox, WebKit] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-input-email/test-browser.ts: "moves focus back to the email input when typing on an item")
- Given a combobox-select whose label lives inside the popover, when the popover opens, then the inner "Search fruits" input is visible and takes DOM focus, and the label reaches it through `htmlFor` alone so the browser's own name computation proves the association. [Chromium, Firefox, WebKit] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-label-popover/test-browser.ts: "names the input with the label rendered inside the popover")
- Given that inner label, when the names are computed, then the outer select stays visible with its own name and the popover is still the listbox named "Favorite fruit", so the inner label does not take over the select's names. [Chromium, Firefox, WebKit] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-label-popover/test-browser.ts: "names the input with the label rendered inside the popover")
- Given the same composition in happy-dom, when the select is clicked, then a combobox named "Search fruits" is visible inside the popover. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-label-popover/test.ts: "names the input with the label rendered inside the popover")
- Given a modal combobox popover, when `focus()` is called on the inert outside button, then focus stays on the inner search input because the browser refuses focus on inert content. [Chromium, Firefox, WebKit] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-modal-input/test-browser.ts: "keeps the combobox select interactive while the rest is inert")
- Given a modal combobox popover, when Escape is pressed from the inner input, then the input is hidden and DOM focus returns to the select trigger. [Chromium, Firefox, WebKit] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-modal-input/test-browser.ts: "closes the modal popover with Escape from the input inside it")
- Given a modal combobox popover in happy-dom, when the select is clicked, then the inner search input takes DOM focus, and Escape returns focus to the trigger. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-modal-input/test.ts: "closes the modal popover with Escape from the input inside it")
- Given an open combobox popover whose restoration is queued, when the popover element is focused and then an external button is focused in the same task, then the external button keeps focus and the popover does not steal it back. [Chromium and Firefox only] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test-chrome-firefox.ts: "doesn't steal focus after focus leaves the popover")
- Given the same sequence in happy-dom, when focus moves from the popover to an external button within one microtask, then the external button keeps focus. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test.ts: "doesn't steal focus after focus leaves the popover")
- Given a virtualized combobox-select, when the trigger is clicked, then the search input takes DOM focus before any typing. [Chromium only] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-active-id-3914/test-chrome.ts: "never paints the filtered virtualized list with the previously active item")
- Given a `multiple` combobox filtered by typing, when the results settle, then the input still holds DOM focus. [Chromium, Firefox, WebKit] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-multiple/test-browser.ts: "scroll offscreen item into view after selecting it")
- Given a combobox-select with a scrollable list, when it is opened, then the search input has focus while the list is not focusable, and calling `focus()` on the list leaves it unfocused. [Chromium, Firefox, WebKit] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-list-6868/test-browser.ts: "skips a scrollable list by default")
- Given the same list in happy-dom, when `focus()` is called on it, then it does not take focus. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-list-6868/test.ts: "skips the list by default")
- Given an `autoComplete` combobox showing a completion, when the body is clicked twice so the input blurs, then the previewed value "images_backup.tar.gz" stays as the committed value. (ariakit: app/src/examples/combobox-group/test.ts: "blur input after autocomplete")
- Given a grouped `autoComplete` combobox showing "Avocado", when the body is clicked twice so the input blurs, then the value stays "Avocado". (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-group-basic/test.ts: "blur input after autocomplete")
- Given an open combobox, when an option is chosen with the mouse, then DOM focus returns to the input rather than staying in the popover. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-cancel/test.ts: "clear input with mouse")
- Given an animated combobox popover, when an option is clicked, then the input regains DOM focus while the popover is still running its leave transition. [Chromium only] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-animated/test-chrome.ts: "combobox show/hide animation")
- Given a combobox-select styled after Radix on a mobile viewport, when the trigger is tapped, then the dialog becomes visible and the inner search input takes focus. [mobile viewport] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-radix-select/test-mobile.ts: "keeps the select open when the viewport resizes")

- Given an "Escaping fruit" select whose app moves virtual focus out of the popup while it is positioning, when it opens, then the external button holds focus and still does after the frames settle (Chromium, Firefox and WebKit). ### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given an `autoSelect` combobox with a controlled `activeId`, when a keystroke re-filters the list, then the promoted first option and the highlight reach the screen in the same animation frame, with no frame showing the new first option next to the previously active one. [Chromium only] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-active-id-3914/test-chrome.ts: "never paints the filtered list with the previously active item")
- Given the frame-by-frame ledger over three type-and-Backspace cycles, when the recorded frames are inspected, then both "Andorra" and "Afghanistan" appear as the first option, proving the sampler saw the list on both sides of each filter change. [Chromium only] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-active-id-3914/test-chrome.ts: "never paints the filtered list with the previously active item")
- Given a controlled-`activeId` combobox, when "n" is typed so "Andorra" outranks "Afghanistan", then the first option and the reported active country are both "Andorra", and Backspace restores both to "Afghanistan". [Chromium only] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-active-id-3914/test-chrome.ts: "never paints the filtered list with the previously active item")
- Given a virtualized combobox with a controlled `activeId`, when "a" is typed, then the number of rendered options is above 2 and below 50, so the virtualizer is really windowing the matches while the highlight stays on the first one. [Chromium only] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-active-id-3914/test-chrome.ts: "never paints the filtered virtualized list with the previously active item")
- Given a combobox-select that resets its value on Escape, when a `resetOnEscape` callback returns false, then Escape leaves the preview "Banana" in place. [Chromium and Firefox only] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test-chrome-firefox.ts: "honors a resetOnEscape callback")
- Given the same callback in happy-dom, when Escape is pressed, then the value stays "Banana". (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test.ts: "honors a resetOnEscape callback")
- Given a descendant button inside the popover that handles Escape itself, when Escape is pressed while it has focus, then the popover stays visible and the value stays "Banana", so no reset can have committed. [Chromium and Firefox only] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test-chrome-firefox.ts: "keeps the value when a descendant consumes Escape")
- Given the same descendant in happy-dom, when Escape is pressed, then the listbox stays visible and the value stays "Banana". (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test.ts: "keeps the value when a descendant consumes Escape")
- Given a popover whose Escape-consuming descendant is not in the event path, when Escape is pressed from the input, then the listbox unmounts and the value resets to "Apple". (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test.ts: "still restores when the descendant is out of the event path")
- Given a consumed Escape that left the popover open, when the outside is clicked, then the popover closes and the previewed "Banana" is kept rather than reset. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test.ts: "keeps the previewed value when clicking outside after a consumed Escape")
- Given a descendant that calls stopPropagation on Escape, when Escape is pressed, then the popover stays visible and the value stays "Banana". [Chromium and Firefox only] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test-chrome-firefox.ts: "keeps the value when a descendant stops the Escape propagation")
- Given a descendant that stops Escape propagation in happy-dom, when Escape is pressed and then "Banana" is clicked, then the value is "Banana" both before and after the click. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test.ts: "keeps the value when a descendant stops the Escape propagation")
- Given a combobox-select whose `hideOnEscape` handler calls preventDefault, when Escape is pressed, then the popover still hides and the value still resets to "Apple". [Chromium and Firefox only] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test-chrome-firefox.ts: "still restores when hideOnEscape prevents the default")
- Given the same prevented default in happy-dom, when Escape is pressed, then the listbox unmounts and the value resets to "Apple". (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test.ts: "still restores when hideOnEscape prevents the default")
- Given a consumed Escape followed by toggling the popover closed from its trigger, when the popover closes, then the previewed "Banana" is kept. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test.ts: "keeps the previewed value when the popover is toggled closed after a consumed Escape")
- Given a combobox-select counting resets and closes, when one Escape closes the popover, then the counters read "reset:1 close:1 events:close,reset", so a single keypress produces exactly one close and one reset in that order. [Chromium and Firefox only] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test-chrome-firefox.ts: "runs reset once for one accepted Escape")
- Given the same counters in happy-dom, when one Escape is pressed, then they read "reset:1 close:1 events:close,reset" and the listbox unmounts. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test.ts: "reports one closing Escape per keypress")
- Given a controlled-open combobox-select, when Escape requests a close the controller does not apply, then the popover stays visible, the value resets to "Apple", and the reset counter reads 1. [Chromium and Firefox only] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test-chrome-firefox.ts: "runs reset once for a controlled close request")
- Given the same controlled close in happy-dom, when Escape is pressed, then the listbox stays visible, the value resets to "Apple", and the counter starts with "reset:1". (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test.ts: "reports one reset for a controlled close request")
- Given a descendant that swallows Escape, when Escape is pressed, then the popover stays open and the counters stay at "reset:0 close:0 events:", so nothing is reported at all. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test.ts: "reports nothing when a descendant keeps the popover open")
- Given an `onClose` handler that vetoes the close, when Escape is pressed, then the popover stays visible, the value stays "Banana", and the counters read "reset:0 close:2 events:close,close". [Chromium and Firefox only] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test-chrome-firefox.ts: "doesn't reset when onClose prevents the close")
- Given the same veto in happy-dom, when Escape is pressed, then the listbox stays visible, the value stays "Banana", and the counters read "reset:0 close:2 events:close,close". (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test.ts: "doesn't reset when onClose prevents the close")
- Given an `onClose` that vetoes only the first close, when a second Escape arrives after the fixture reports "ready", then the popover hides and the value resets to the original "Apple" rather than to the intermediate "Banana". - Given the same one-shot veto in happy-dom, when the second Escape arrives, then the listbox unmounts and the value is "Apple". (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test.ts: "preserves the original baseline after a prevented close")
- Given a close vetoed before any item move, when the selection is set to "Banana" from a button, End moves to "Grape", and Escape is pressed, then the popover hides and the value returns to "Banana", so the baseline kept tracking after the veto. - Given the same sequence in happy-dom, when Escape is finally pressed, then the listbox unmounts and the value returns to "Banana". (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test.ts: "keeps tracking the baseline after a close is prevented before moving")
- Given a vetoing `onClose` that also updates the selection synchronously, when End moves to "Grape" and Escape is pressed, then the popover hides and the value returns to the synchronously set "Banana". [Chromium and Firefox only] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test-chrome-firefox.ts: "keeps tracking a synchronous selection update from a vetoing onClose")
- Given the same synchronous update in happy-dom, when Escape is pressed, then the listbox unmounts and the value is "Banana". (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test.ts: "keeps tracking a synchronous selection update from a vetoing onClose")
- Given a descendant that consumes Escape and closes the popover itself, when Escape is pressed, then the popover hides and the value stays "Banana", because that close is not the Escape the reset listens for. - Given the same descendant in happy-dom, when Escape is pressed, then the listbox unmounts and the value stays "Banana". (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test.ts: "doesn't reset for a different close from a consumed Escape")
- Given a controlled-open combobox-select whose close request is not prevented, when Escape is pressed, then the popover stays visible because the controller keeps it open, and the value resets to "Apple". - Given the same controlled composition in happy-dom, when Escape is pressed, then the listbox stays visible and the value is "Apple". (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test.ts: "resets after an unprevented controlled close request")
- Given an Escape that a descendant swallowed, when the popover is later closed by toggling the trigger, then no reset runs, the value stays "Banana", and the counters read "reset:0 close:1 events:close". - Given two open-preview-Escape sessions in a row, when both finish, then each restores "Apple" and the counters read "reset:2 close:2 events:close,reset,close,reset". (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test.ts: "restores independently across open sessions")
- Given a combobox-select counting popover renders, when the selected value is changed from outside while the popover is open, then the trigger shows "Banana" and the popover render count is unchanged. ### Forms

- Given a `multiple` combobox inside a form, when "Apple" and "Orange" are selected, a search string is typed, Escape closes the popover, and Submit is pressed, then the submitted payload is `["apple","orange"]`, so the typed search never leaks into the submission. [Chromium, Firefox, WebKit] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-5058/test-browser.ts: "submits every selected value")
- Given the same form with nothing selected, when Submit is pressed, then the payload is `[]`. [Chromium, Firefox, WebKit] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-5058/test-browser.ts: "does not submit an empty search value")
- Given a `multiple` combobox whose composite behavior is turned off, when the form data is read, then the field holds `["apple"]` and the input's owning form is the one with id "non-composite-form". [Chromium, Firefox, WebKit] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-5058/test-browser.ts: "submits selected values when composite is false")
- Given a combobox whose selected values include an `aria-disabled` one, when the form data is read, then the field is empty and the combobox itself reports as disabled. [Chromium, Firefox, WebKit] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-5058/test-browser.ts: "omits aria-disabled selected values")
- Given a combobox associated with an explicit form by id, when Enter is pressed in the input, then that form submits and its submitter is the "Submit non-composite fruits" button, so implicit submission survives the explicit association. [Chromium, Firefox, WebKit] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-5058/test-browser.ts: "preserves implicit submission with an explicit form")
- Given a `multiple` combobox with "Apple" selected, when the form's Reset button is pressed and then Submit, then the payload is `["apple"]`, so the mirrored controls stay in sync with the store after a reset. [Chromium, Firefox, WebKit] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-5058/test-browser.ts: "keeps selected values in sync after form reset")
- Given a `multiple` combobox in a form, when values are selected, then the visible combobox input itself carries no `name` attribute. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-5058/test.ts: "mirrors every selected value in the form control")
- Given a `multiple` combobox in a form, when "Apple" and "Orange" are selected, then `FormData` for the field "fruits" returns `["apple","orange"]`, one entry per selected value. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-5058/test.ts: "mirrors every selected value in the form control")
- Given a non-composite combobox, when the form data is read, then the field holds `["apple"]` and the input's `form` property points at that form. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-5058/test.ts: "mirrors selected values when composite is false")
- Given a disabled combobox with selected values, when the form data is read, then the combobox is disabled and the field contributes nothing. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-5058/test.ts: "omits aria-disabled selected values")
- Given a single-selection combobox in a form, when the input is inspected, then it keeps its own `name="single-fruit"` rather than delegating to hidden mirrors. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-5058/test.ts: "preserves the name for a single selected value")

- Given a select inside a form with a default value, when the page renders, then the `role=combobox` shows "Apple". (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-form/test.ts`: "default value")
- Given that form, when Submit is clicked, then the submitted value is "Apple". (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-form/test.ts`: "submit form")
- Given that form, when "Orange" is selected and Submit clicked, then the listbox closes, the trigger reads "Orange", and the submitted value is "Orange". (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-form/test.ts`: "select another value")
- Given a disabled select in a form, when the form is submitted, then the submitted value is null. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-form-disabled/test.ts`: "disabled select does not submit value")

### Dismissal and layering

- Given a combobox popover that is open on load, when Escape is pressed, then the listbox is hidden. [Chromium, Firefox, WebKit] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-5518/test-browser.ts: "pressing escape closes the popover")
- Given that same sandbox, when the page loads, then the listbox is already visible and the combobox already has DOM focus. [Chromium, Firefox, WebKit] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-5518/test-browser.ts: "pressing escape closes the popover")
- Given an open popover from the disclosure button, when "Hide popup" is clicked, then the listbox is removed from the document entirely. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-disclosure/test.ts: "show and hide popup with disclosure button")
- Given a popover opened by clicking the input, when Escape is pressed, then the listbox is removed from the document. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-disclosure/test.ts: "show and hide popup with combobox")
- Given a filtered grouped combobox, when an option is clicked, then the listbox leaves the document. (ariakit: app/src/examples/combobox-group/custom-items/test.ts: "filters and selects a custom result, then shows an empty state")
- Given a grouped combobox example in a browser, when Enter commits the hovered option, then the input value becomes "Sarah Davis" and the listbox is no longer visible. [Chromium and Firefox only] (ariakit: app/src/examples/combobox-group/test-chrome-firefox.ts: "keeps the active result highlighted after the pointer leaves")
- Given a `multiple` combobox open from the keyboard, when Escape is pressed, then the listbox unmounts and DOM focus returns to the input. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-multiple/test.ts: "open with keyboard, then try to open again")
- Given a modal combobox popover, when it is open, then everything outside it is inert, and the combobox-select trigger stays interactive as a persistent element of the modal context so clicking it still toggles the popover closed. [Chromium, Firefox, WebKit] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-modal-input/test-browser.ts: "keeps the combobox select interactive while the rest is inert")
- Given an open combobox-select dialog on a mobile viewport, when Escape is pressed, then the dialog hides and the trigger takes focus. [mobile viewport] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-radix-select/test-mobile.ts: "keeps the select open when the viewport resizes")
- Given a combobox-select whose Escape reset ran, when the popover state is inspected, then the popover is hidden in the same Escape that performed the reset, and the ordering is recorded as "close,reset". [Chromium and Firefox only] (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-popover-reset-on-escape/test-chrome-firefox.ts: "runs reset once for one accepted Escape")

- Given an animated select popover, when Escape is pressed, then the select keeps focus, the popover may still be visible while the leave transition runs, and it eventually unmounts (Chromium, Firefox and WebKit). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-animation/test-browser.ts`: "preserves selection across animated show and hide", both fixtures)
- Given an animated select popover, when a point outside is pressed, then the popover unmounts (Chromium, Firefox and WebKit). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-animation/test-browser.ts`: "closes when pressing outside the popover", both fixtures)
- Given an open select, when Escape is pressed, then the listbox unmounts. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-items-unmount/test.ts` via `select-tests.test-helper.ts`: "hide on escape")

- Given an `autoSelect` combobox, when a composition session starts and an isComposing keystroke types a dead key, then no option is added to the document, so filtering waits for the composition to finish. (ariakit: app/src/examples/combobox-group/test.ts: "composition text")

- Given a grouped `autoComplete` combobox, when a dead key is typed while composing, then no option is registered yet. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-group-basic/test.ts: "composition text")
- Given that composition resolves to "á", when `compositionend` fires, then the value becomes "ápple" with "pple" selected and "Apple" becomes the active item. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-group-basic/test.ts: "composition text")
- Given a combobox with a cancel button, when a dead key is typed while composing, then no option becomes active. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-cancel/test.ts: "composition text")
- Given that composition resolves to "á", when `compositionend` fires, then the value is "á" and "Apple" becomes the active item. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-cancel/test.ts: "composition text")
- Given a Korean IME that commits one syllable and immediately starts composing the next within a single keystroke, when `compositionend` is followed by `compositionstart` with no frame in between, then DOM focus stays on the combobox input and the option "사과" does not take focus. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-ime-6663/test.ts: "keeps focus in the combobox between IME composition sessions")
- Given the next syllable is composed and committed, when the final `compositionend` settles, then "사과" becomes the active item. (ariakit: app/src/sandbox/combobox-ime-6663/test.ts: "keeps focus in the combobox between IME composition sessions")
- Given a real macOS Korean 2-set trace replayed through CDP `Input.imeSetComposition`, when the syllable 사 is committed and 고 starts composing, then no `focusin` lands on an option between that `compositionend` and the next `compositionstart`; the focus move is what makes the native macOS IME drop the composed 고 and produce 사ㅏ. - Given that page after selecting "German", when the browser goes back, then the URL returns to `lang=fr` and the select reads "French"; going forward returns it to "German" (Chromium and Firefox only). - Given that hydrated multi-select opened, when the options render, then "Draft" and "Published" report `aria-selected="true"` and "Archived" reports `aria-selected="false"` (Chromium and Firefox only). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-nextjs-app-router/test-chrome-firefox.ts`: "hydrates language and multiple statuses from the URL")
- Given that page with two statuses in the URL, when the page is reloaded, then the select still reads "2 selected" (Chromium and Firefox only). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-nextjs-app-router/test-chrome-firefox.ts`: "selects multiple statuses")
- Given a single-value option opened in a new tab from the App Router page, when the new tab loads, then its "Language" select hydrates to "French" while the original tab stays "English" (Chromium and Firefox only; the new tab is brought to the front so Chrome does not defer Next.js hydration). - Given the page-freeze variant of the valueless-trailing-items bug, when it is tested, then it is covered only in a real browser, because on the buggy code the keydown handler loops forever synchronously and would hang the happy-dom worker instead of failing. - Given assertions about something not happening, when the browser tests need a settle point, then they cross frame checkpoints with `flushFrames` because a prevented scroll, a cancelled presentation or a withheld focus has no positive completion state. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-collapsed-focus/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-programmatic-open/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-selected-value-presentation/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-renderer/test-browser.ts`: many cases)

(ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-animation/test-safari.ts`: "does not scroll with smooth scrolling")
- Given the scroll side of the selected-value presentation, when it is tested, then it lives only in the browser files, and the unit files assert the active item and focus instead. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-default-open/test.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-programmatic-open/test.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-scroll-into-view/test.ts` comments)
- Given the hover-end case in a real browser, when the pointer is teleported onto an element, then Playwright fires the boundary events with no intervening mousemove, so the test first moves inside the option to arm the movement tracker that the previous mouseup reset. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-collapsed-focus/test-browser.ts`: "hover end on a collapsed list keeps the active item")
- Given `aria-haspopup` on a select whose popup is a dialog wrapping a listbox, when it is asserted, then the test reads the attribute once instead of using Playwright's retrying matcher, because retrying would also pass while the value was still the listbox fallback (Chromium, Firefox and WebKit). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select/test-browser.ts`: both "reflects the popup role when opened" cases)
- Given an initially empty `display: contents` tag list, when it is queried by role, then Playwright filters it out of default role queries, so the test passes `includeHidden` (Chromium only). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-tag-tooltip-element-id/test-chrome.ts`: "updates tag relationships when element ids change")
- Given a page-scroll fixture whose composite element lives inside an unmounted popup, when the test asserts it does not exist, then it counts hidden elements too, so the assertion proves absence from the DOM rather than only from the accessibility tree (Chromium, Firefox and WebKit). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-open-page-scroll/test-browser.ts`: "keeps the page in place while the popup is being positioned")
- Given the new-tab cases on the App Router page, when they run under CI load, then they are marked slow because opening a tab may cold-start the preview worker, and the page-event deadline is capped at 60s to stay inside the 90s budget (Chromium and Firefox only). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-nextjs-app-router/test-chrome-firefox.ts`: "opens a single-value option in a new tab", "opens a multi-value option in a new tab")
- Given the "combobox-tabs-old" sandbox, when its test file runs, then it imports `../combobox-tabs/test.ts` wholesale, so all eight combobox-with-tabs cases ("open popover with components tab initially selected, but not active", "move through items and tabs with the keyboard", "move through items and tabs with a mouse", "filter items and change tabs", "filter items until there are no results and change tabs", "clear input with keyboard", "clear input with mouse", "open the popover with arrow down after switching tabs") run again against the older fixture. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-tabs-old/test.ts`)
- Given the "combobox-select-items-unmount" sandbox, when its test file runs, then it calls the shared `testSelect("combobox")` helper, so all seventeen select behaviors are re-run with the combobox as the focus target. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-items-unmount/test.ts` via `select-tests.test-helper.ts`)
- Given the renderer fixture's empty scroller, when its explicit ref is connected, then the connection happens in passive effects with no rendered item to signal completion, so the test crosses frames before loading items (Chromium, Firefox and WebKit). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-renderer/test-browser.ts`: "updates items when an initially empty scroller gains overflow", "disables viewport updates when the scroll element is null", "disables viewport updates when a scroll element ref resolves to null")
- Given the render-count fixture, when the item mounts, then it renders twice by design, once on its own and once when the composite element is published, which is why the settled baseline asserted before opening is "2". (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-selected-value-presentation/test-browser.ts`: "does not re-render inactive items when the popup opens")
- Given React's ordering, when a dialog's natively auto-focused input moves focus away synchronously, then it happens before layout effects and therefore before Dialog can install a DOM listener, which is the quirk this case pins (Chromium, Firefox and WebKit). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-selected-value-presentation/test-browser.ts`: "does not refocus after native auto-focus moves focus into a shadow root")
- Given the "Parked fruit" fixture, when the request has already resolved an item and the active item then moves on by highlight, then nothing abandons the request because highlighting sets the active id without bumping the move counter, and the newly highlighted item is not a presentation target (Chromium, Firefox and WebKit). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-selected-value-presentation/test-browser.ts`: "keeps presenting the item it resolved when the active item moves on")
- Given the collapsed-focus contract, when a move originates outside the widget, then presentation is immediate rather than withheld, so the focus it moves is attributable to that call instead of landing on whoever holds focus when the list next opens. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-collapsed-focus/test.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-collapsed-focus/test-browser.ts`: "a move from outside the widget still presents immediately")
- Given the horizontal-orientation renderer check, when the last option is asserted instead of a middle one, then the assertion stays valid under virtualization because the last index stays rendered. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-renderer/test.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-renderer/test-browser.ts`: "forwards horizontal orientation to the item layout")
- Given `combobox-select-focus-within`, when its cases run, then they are the sandbox copies of `examples/select-combobox-focus-within/test.ts`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-focus-within/test.ts`: "shows and hides the cancel button with popover focus", "tracks focus within the select composition")
- Given `combobox-select-grid`, when its cases run, then they are the sandbox copies of `examples/select-grid/test.ts`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-grid/test.ts`: "uses the center as the default value", "changes an expanded value with the keyboard", "changes a collapsed value with the keyboard", "changes the value on hover", "keeps the moved value when tabbing out")
- Given `combobox-select-menu-filters`, when its cases run, then they are the sandbox copies of `examples/select-menu-default-open/test.ts` and `examples/select-menu-default-open-click/test.ts`. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-menu-filters/test.ts`: "checkbox menu adds an open filter and commits its value", "click menu removes an uncommitted filter on outside click")
- Given the shared select helper, when it is reused, then it lives at `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-items-unmount/select-tests.test-helper.ts` and takes the focus target ("combobox" or "listbox") as its only argument, so each sandbox that imports it re-runs the same seventeen cases against its own focus model. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-items-unmount/test.ts`)
- Given the animated select popover, when it is closed, then it is fully unmounted rather than hidden, which the tests assert by counting zero listbox elements before the first open and after each close (Chromium, Firefox and WebKit). (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-animation/test-browser.ts`: "preserves selection across animated show and hide", both fixtures)
- Given these combobox animation suites, when presence is asserted, then they never read `data-enter` or `data-leave` directly: the enter and leave phases are pinned through element counts, visibility during a timed transition window, `data-placing` on the popup, and polling that outlasts the 1s exit transition. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-animation/test-browser.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/combobox-tabs-animated/test.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-selected-value-presentation/test-browser.ts`)
- Given the typeahead timeout, when two separate typeahead sequences must not merge, then the tests wait 600ms between them, which pins the typeahead reset window. (ariakit: `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-grid/test.ts`: "changes a collapsed value with the keyboard"; `app/src/sandbox/combobox-select-items-unmount/test.ts` via `select-tests.test-helper.ts`: "typeahead open", "typeahead hidden")

- Given an option chosen from the list, when it is selected, then the raw value is placed into `Combobox.Input` when no `displayValue` is given, and the display value when one is; this holds when the bound value is `undefined` (Vue: when the `v-model` is undefined), and conditionally rendering the input allows the display value to change. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/combobox/combobox.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/combobox/combobox.test.ts`: "selecting an option puts the value into Combobox.Input when displayValue is not provided", "selecting an option puts the display value into Combobox.Input when displayValue is provided", "selecting an option puts the display value into Combobox.Input when displayValue is provided (when value is undefined)", "selecting an option puts the display value into Combobox.Input when displayValue is provided (when v-model is undefined)", "conditionally rendering the input should allow changing the display value")
- Given the input value being synced from the outside, when the sync happens, then the caret is moved to the end of the input. The companion behavior, not moving the caret when a custom selection is in place, is `xit` (disabled) in both frameworks, as is the test that the input reflects a changing value while you are typing. (headlessui: `packages/@headlessui-react/src/components/combobox/combobox.test.tsx`, `packages/@headlessui-vue/src/components/combobox/combobox.test.ts`: "should move the caret to the end of the input when syncing the value"; "should not move the caret to the end of the input when syncing the value if a custom selection is made" [skipped], "should reflect the value in the input when the value changes and when you are typing" [skipped])

## transition

### Roles and attributes

- Given a `Transition`, when it renders, then it does not crash and does not steal the ref from its child; forgetting the required `show` prop yells. ## Test infrastructure notes

### Ariakit

- Ariakit runs two test systems side by side: Vitest for DOM and node tests, and Playwright for real-browser tests. One Vitest config defines four projects: `node` (environment `node`, everything not claimed by another project), `dom` (happy-dom, the framework-agnostic packages), `react` (happy-dom plus `@vitejs/plugin-react`, claiming `packages/ariakit-react*/**` plus every `app/src/{examples,sandbox}/<dir>/test.{ts,tsx}` that has an `index.react.tsx` entry) and `solid` (happy-dom plus `vite-plugin-solid`, the same claim for `index.solid.tsx`). A sandbox `test.ts` therefore runs once per framework against the same assertions. (ariakit: `vitest.config.ts`)
- The DOM projects run on happy-dom rather than jsdom, with the config comment recording that it is about twice as fast for the `@ariakit/test` simulation layer and that the shims in that package normalize happy-dom's spec divergences, including React 18 event priority and the missing `window.event`. A single file can opt into another environment with a `// @vitest-environment <name>` comment, which is what the `*.jsdom.test.ts` files and `menu-motion-transitions/test.ts` do. (ariakit: `vitest.config.ts`, `app/src/sandbox/menu-motion-transitions/test.ts`)
- The global setup installs `@testing-library/jest-dom` matchers, turns on `vitest-fail-on-console` so any unexpected `console.error` or `console.warn` fails the run, and overrides `toHaveFocus` so that an element also counts as focused when the document's active element points at it through `aria-activedescendant`. That override is what makes virtual focus assertable with the same matcher as DOM focus. (ariakit: `vitest.setup.ts`)
- Playwright tests are written through `withFramework(import.meta.dirname, ...)`, which derives the sandbox id from the directory, enumerates the frameworks that sandbox has entries for, and produces one test run per framework against the dev-server preview page. The callback receives `{ id, test, framework, query }`, and each test receives a `q` fixture, which is the role-query helper from `@ariakit/test/playwright` bound to the page. (ariakit: `app/src/test-utils/preview.ts`)
- The Playwright helpers include `gotoAndSettle(page, url)`, which waits for `load` and then for a network-idle capped at 5s (with a comment that unbounded `networkidle` can stall past the test timeout under CI contention), and `flushFrames(page, frames = 2)`, which crosses animation frames. The `flushFrames` doc comment instructs authors to prefer a retrying assertion against observable state and to leave a comment explaining why frames are needed, which is why nearly every use of it in the suite carries such a comment. (ariakit: `app/src/test-utils/preview.ts`)
- Other Playwright helpers used across the suite: `createMenuAccessibilityReader(page)` and `createDismissAccessibilityReader(page)` read Chromium's real accessibility tree (names and child roles) rather than DOM attributes, `recordScrollEvents(page)` records which scrollers actually scrolled so a test can assert that the document did not, and `app/src/test-utils/fixtures.ts` provides the `reuseContext` and `headless` options some suites opt into. (ariakit: `app/src/test-utils/accessibility.ts`, `app/src/test-utils/scroll.ts`, `app/src/test-utils/fixtures.ts`)
- The test-file suffix is the whole environment contract, and it is the single most portable idea in this suite: `test.ts` for the fast simulated run in both frameworks, `test-browser.ts` for all three engines, and `test-chrome.ts`, `test-safari.ts`, `test-chrome-firefox.ts`, `test-chrome-safari.ts`, `test-mobile.ts`, `test-ios.ts`, `test-chrome-js-disabled.ts`, `test-public-browser.ts` for everything that is genuinely engine- or environment-specific. Many files carry a header comment explaining exactly why a behavior cannot be observed in the other environment, which is the record of what a conformance suite can and cannot prove in a simulated DOM.
- Recurring reasons a behavior is browser-only, stated in the tests themselves: happy-dom has no layout, so document scroll offsets and geometry cannot be modeled; happy-dom stubs `scrollIntoView`; happy-dom shares one set of constructors between a frame and its parent, so cross-realm event identity is unobservable; happy-dom implements no document named getter, so a form control shadowing `document.activeElement` cannot be reproduced; a synchronously looping keydown handler would hang the happy-dom worker rather than fail; and `vitest-fail-on-console` turns React's own development warnings into failures, so some tests that deliberately trigger them live only in the browser run.
- Recurring reasons a behavior is happy-dom-only: `press.up` synthesizes a click on any focused native button regardless of where the keydown happened, so a test that depends on real browser Space-activation cancellation asserts less there; a real browser blurs an element that disables itself while happy-dom does not; and WebKit skips native buttons when tabbing under the default macOS keyboard settings, so tests that need Tab to reach a button script the focus move instead.
- Assertion style: the simulated tests use `expect.poll(query.lazy(...))` for anything that settles asynchronously, and the `.lazy` query variant exists precisely so a query can be re-run inside a polling matcher. The browser tests use Playwright's own retrying `expect`. Several tests carry comments noting that a negative assertion has no positive state to wait for, and therefore cross a checkpoint (`flushFrames`, `sleep`, or a fixed `waitForTimeout`) before asserting that something did not happen.

### Headless UI

- Both packages run on Jest 26 with `@swc/jest` as the only transform for `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js` and `.jsx`, driven by `scripts/test.sh` which wraps `npx jest` and adds `--maxWorkers=4 --ci` when `CI` is set. (headlessui: scripts/test.sh, jest/create-jest-config.cjs)
- Neither package sets `testEnvironment`, so both run in jsdom, which is Jest 26's default; there is no vitest and no real-browser runner anywhere in the repo. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/jest.config.cjs, packages/@headlessui-vue/jest.config.cjs)
- The root `jest.config.cjs` is a projects config pointing at `packages/*/jest.config.cjs`, and both package configs are produced by the shared `jest/create-jest-config.cjs` factory, so React and Vue cannot drift on transform, globals, or setup files. (headlessui: jest.config.cjs, jest/create-jest-config.cjs)
- The shared factory injects the same two setup files into both packages, `jest/custom-matchers.ts` and `jest/polyfills.ts`, and sets the `__DEV__` global to true; React adds one extra setup file and Vue adds none. (headlessui: jest/create-jest-config.cjs)
- The React project sets `displayName: 'React'` and the Vue project `displayName: ' Vue '` with padding spaces so the two labels line up in the reporter output. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/jest.config.cjs, packages/@headlessui-vue/jest.config.cjs)
- React's extra setup file only sets `globalThis.IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT = true`, which is what makes the `act` wrappers inside its `interactions.ts` effective. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/jest.setup.js)
- `jest/custom-matchers.ts` loads `@testing-library/jest-dom/extend-expect` for both packages and adds one matcher, `toBeWithinRenderFrame`, which passes when the actual value is within two 60fps frames (about 33ms) of the expected value. (headlessui: jest/custom-matchers.ts)
- `jest/polyfills.ts` mocks the Web Animations API and `ResizeObserver` through `jsdom-testing-mocks`, defines `innerText` on `HTMLElement.prototype` as an alias for `textContent`, and installs a `PointerEvent` class that carries `button` and `pointerType` with `pointerType` defaulting to `'mouse'`; every one of these is a jsdom gap the transition and pointer tests depend on. (headlessui: jest/polyfills.ts)
- React and Vue are kept in parity mainly by duplication rather than sharing: `fake-pointer.ts` and `report-dom-node-changes.ts` are byte-identical across the two packages, and `interactions.ts`, `execute-timeline.ts`, `suppress-console-logs.ts` and `accessibility-assertions.ts` are line-for-line copies apart from the framework-specific differences listed above. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/)
- The two `interactions.test` files are the same 22-case table with the same `it.each` name, differing only in the expected focus event names and in how the fixture is built, so the keyboard event model is pinned identically in both frameworks. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.test.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.test.ts)
- Vue keeps parity with React's testing-library surface by reimplementing it: `vue-testing-library.ts` exposes `render`, `fireEvent` and `screen` with the same shape the React suites get from `@testing-library/react`, including an `afterEach` cleanup and an `asFragment()` for snapshot diffing. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/vue-testing-library.ts)
- The shared `scenarios.tsx` generators exist only in the React package, so the Field, Fieldset, Label and Description composition matrix is not mirrored in Vue at all. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/scenarios.tsx)
- Vue's assertion file lacks the whole Field-era block that React has: `getLabel`, `getLabels`, `getDescription`, `getDescriptions`, `getControl`, `getInput`, `getSelect`, `getTextarea`, `getCheckbox`, the `CheckboxState` enum, `assertCheckbox`, `assertLinkedWithLabel`, `assertNotLinkedWithLabel`, `assertLinkedWithDescription` and `assertDisabledish` are all React-only, which matches Vue having no `Field`, `Fieldset`, `Checkbox`, `Input`, `Select` or `Textarea` component. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- React's assertion file lacks the dialog overlay block that Vue has: `getDialogOverlay`, `getDialogBackdrop`, `getDialogOverlays` and `assertDialogOverlay` are Vue-only, because React renamed `Dialog.Overlay` to `DialogBackdrop` and asserts it inline. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- React's label getters accept the generic `headlessui-label` id prefix in addition to the component-specific one for combobox, listbox and switch, and accept a `label` element for the radio group, while Vue accepts only the component-specific prefixes; a Vue component that emitted a generic label id would not be found by its own test helper. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- The popover overlay getter targets a different id prefix in each framework, `headlessui-popover-backdrop-` in React and `headlessui-popover-overlay-` in Vue, so the same assertion name checks a differently named DOM node. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- React resolves the active element through the element's root node in `assertActiveElement` and `assertContainsActiveElement`, so React's focus assertions work inside a shadow root while Vue's, reading `document.activeElement`, do not. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- No assertion helper in either framework hard-codes a `data-headlessui-state` token list, or checks `data-open`, `data-active`, `data-focus`, `data-hover`, `data-disabled`, `data-selected`, `data-autofocus`, `data-closed`, `data-enter`, `data-leave`, `data-slot` or `data-headlessui-focus-visible`; those are all asserted by the component suites through the generic `attributes` bag or inline `toHaveAttribute` calls, and the observed token lists are space-separated sets such as `''`, `'active focus'` and `'checked active focus'`. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- The only `data-*` attributes any assertion helper requires directly are `data-checked` and `data-indeterminate` on the React checkbox, and each is checked for presence only, never for a value. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/accessibility-assertions.ts)
- Vue's `suppressConsoleLogs` defaults to silencing `console.warn` while React's defaults to `console.error`, and Vue has no `mockingConsoleLogs`, so a Vue test cannot assert on the warning text it suppresses. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/suppress-console-logs.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/suppress-console-logs.ts)
- React has `rawClick` for firing a click outside an `act` scope and Vue does not, and React's `click`, `focus`, `blur` and Tab focus moves are all wrapped in `act` while Vue's are bare. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- React's `mouseEnter` fires its three events with no pointer coordinates while Vue's randomises the fake pointer and attaches `screenX`/`screenY`, so the two frameworks do not exercise the library's pointer-position tracking equally. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- React's timeline recorder drops non-monotonic outlier frames and Vue's does not, so a flaky extra frame fails a Vue transition snapshot but is filtered out of a React one. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/execute-timeline.ts)
- Vue's SSR helper never resets the environment flag to `client` during hydration while React's does, so a Vue component that branches on the server flag behaves differently after hydration in tests than in a real app. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/ssr.tsx, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/ssr.ts)
- React's `word` helper fires the value-change event for a focused `textarea` as well as an `input`; Vue's covers only `input`. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
- React awaits three nested `setImmediate` calls after each interaction and Vue awaits two, so the React helpers give the library one extra macrotask to settle. (headlessui: packages/@headlessui-react/src/test-utils/interactions.ts, packages/@headlessui-vue/src/test-utils/interactions.ts)
